title: Phenotype, treatment, and determinants of prognosis in Erdheim-Chester disease: an international, retrospective, cohort study.
abstract: Erdheim-Chester disease is a rare histiocytosis driven by MAPK pathway gene mutations. Its clinical presentation is heterogeneous, and there is a shortage of data on natural history and prognosis. We aimed to characterise clinical presentation, associated conditions, treatments, outcomes, and determinants of prognosis in a large international Erdheim-Chester disease cohort.We conducted an international, retrospective, cohort study of patients with biopsy-proven Erdheim-Chester disease diagnosed between Jan 1, 1985, and Dec 31, 2024. Data were collected in ten countries by participating investigators from referral centre records using standardised criteria, and were collected by participating investigators from referral centre records using standardised criteria. Patients with available data on treatment and outcome, and a minimum follow-up duration of 6 months, without excluding those who died before month 6, were included. Outcomes were response to treatment and overall survival. Mortality predictors were assessed using multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression.From Jan 1 to Dec 31, 2025, we included 1174 patients (males 801 [68%], females 373 [32%]), whose median age at diagnosis was 58 (IQR 47-67) years. Multisystem disease (at least four organs) was present in 724 (62%) of 1174 patients, the most frequently affected sites being long bones (940 [80%] patients), retroperitoneum (742 [63%] patients), large vessels (540 [46%] patients), central nervous system (446 [38%] patients), and heart (412 [35%] patients). 643 (62%) of 1043 tested patients were BRAFV600E mutated, and 250 (36%) of 690 patients had clonal haematopoiesis. Overlap with other histiocytoses occurred in 161 (14%) of 1174 patients, whereas 321 (27%) patients had second cancer. First-line therapies most commonly included interferon-α (362 [34%] of 1057 patients) or targeted therapies (BRAF/MEK inhibitors 350 [33%] patients), with targeted therapies achieving the highest objective response rates (286 [74%] of 387 patients for BRAF inhibitors, and 185 [71%] of 262 patients for MEK inhibitors). After a median of 49 months (IQR 20-91), 261 (22%) patients died. Multivariable analysis identified older age (p<0·0001), neurodegeneration (HR 4·2, 95% CI 2·4-7·1; p<0·0001), high C-reactive protein (3·8, 1·6-9·1; p=0·0022), second haematological cancer (3·0, 1·5-6·0; p=0·0023), and no response to treatment (2·8, 1·6-5·1; p=0·0006) as independent predictors of mortality.In a large Erdheim-Chester disease cohort spanning multiple eras, mortality remains substantial. title: A Contemporary Analysis of Positive Surgical Margin Length and Oncologic Outcomes After Radical Prostatectomy: Results from an Institutional Registry with Long-Term Follow Up.
abstract: To evaluate the impact of positive surgical margins (PSM) after radical prostatectomy (RP) and oncologic outcomes in a large institutional registry with long-term follow up and explore various methods of margin characterization. Prior studies remain limited by heterogeneous margin characterization, small cohorts, and limited follow-up.We queried our prospectively maintained institutional registry for patients who underwent RP from 1987-2023. PSM were analyzed as binary (negative/positive) and focality (negative/unifocal/multifocal). Cox proportional hazards regression models evaluated associations with oncologic outcomes. Cutpoint analysis identified an optimal threshold that differentiated outcomes by linear PSM length.Among 24,855 patients with median follow-up of 10.9 years, 6454(26%) had PSM. On multivariable analysis, PSM were associated with increased risk of biochemical recurrence (BCR, HR 1.74 [1.57-1.93], p<.0001), but not metastasis-free (MFS), cancer-specific (CSS), or overall survival (OS). Unifocal (HR 1.66 [1.48-1.86]) and multifocal (HR 2.01 [1.7-2.37]) PSM were similarly associated with increased risk of BCR (p<.0001), but not MFS, CSS, or OS. Cutpoint analysis identified a threshold of 1mm. PSM length ≥1mm was associated with increased risk of BCR (HR 1.72[1.53-1.92, p<.0001), while <1mm was not.In this large cohort with long-term follow-up, PSMs were only associated with BCR but not with MFS, CSS, or OS. These results may inform postoperative surveillance protocols and adjuvant therapy risk stratification. title: A Predict → Confirm → Act Framework for AI-Augmented MDRO Control Across Hospitals and Long-Term Care Facilities.
abstract: Multidrug-resistant organism (MDRO) control depends on identifying colonized patients and emerging transmission events early enough to intervene, without overwhelming infection prevention and control (IPC) teams or unnecessarily isolating patients. Predictive models using electronic health records, microbiology data, patient movement, and genomic information may support this task. We propose a practical Predict → Confirm → Act framework for artificial intelligence (AI)-augmented infection control across hospitals and long-term care facilities. In this framework, AI generates risk signals; microbiology, genomic data, and epidemiological review provide confirmation; and IPC teams apply proportionate actions such as targeted screening, preemptive precautions, cohorting, environmental investigation, or de-escalation. The framework is model-agnostic and is intended to shift attention away from algorithmic performance alone toward bedside and unit-level decisions. llm_summary: Controlling multidrug-resistant organisms (MDROs) in hospitals and long-term care facilities requires early detection of colonized patients and transmission events, but current approaches risk overwhelming infection prevention teams or unnecessarily isolating patients. Researchers propose a Predict → Confirm → Act framework that uses artificial intelligence applied to electronic health records, microbiology data, patient movement patterns, and genomic information to generate risk signals for MDRO transmission. In this framework, AI-generated signals are then confirmed through microbiology testing, genomic analysis, and epidemiological review before infection prevention teams implement proportionate actions ranging from targeted screening to de-escalation of precautions. Safe implementation of this model-agnostic approach requires local calibration of alert thresholds, clear assignment of alert ownership, established microbiological confirmation pathways, de-escalation protocols, and prospective monitoring using outcomes relevant to infection control such as additional carriers detected, time to isolation, and isolation days avoided. The framework shifts focus from algorithmic performance metrics alone toward practical bedside and unit-level decision-making while requiring evaluation of unintended consequences and alert burden on clinical teams.

title: Brain-Specific Quantification of Somatostatin Receptor Expression: SUVmax and SUVRsss as Quantitative Correlates of the Krenning Score in Meningioma.
abstract: Somatostatin receptor type 2 is highly expressed in meningiomas and can be quantified using [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE PET. The Krenning score, originally developed for [111In]In-octreotide scintigraphy, remains the standard visual grading system for somatostatin receptor expression and is widely used to guide eligibility for peptide receptor radionuclide therapy. However, visual grading may not optimally translate to intracranial disease. This study evaluated the relationship between brain-specific quantitative PET parameters-SUVmax and SUV ratio normalized to the superior sagittal sinus (SUVRsss)-and the Krenning score in meningioma. Methods: This single-institution retrospective study included 44 patients (70 meningiomas) who underwent clinical vertex-to-thigh [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT. Quantitative parameters (SUVmax, SUVRsss, lesion size) were extracted from coregistered PET and MR images. Spearman rank correlation analysis was performed to assess associations between imaging variables and Krenning score. Differences in quantitative PET parameters across Krenning categories were evaluated using Kruskal-Wallis test and Holm-Bonferroni-corrected Mann-Whitney U test. Receiver-operating-characteristic curve analysis using the Youden J index identified optimal cutoffs for clinically relevant thresholds (Krenning score of <3 vs. ≥3 and 3 vs. 4). Results: SUVRsss and SUVmax were strongly correlated with the Krenning score (SUVRsss: Spearman ρ = 0.70; 95% CI, 0.55-0.82; SUVmax: Spearman ρ = 0.77; 95% CI, 0.64-0.85; P < 0.0001). PET parameters differed significantly across Krenning categories (all P < 0.001). SUVRsss optimal thresholds were 9.00 (area under the curve [AUC], 0.86; 95% CI, 0.74-0.96) for Krenning scores of 2 versus 3 and 29.84 (AUC, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.93-1.00) for Krenning scores of 3 versus 4. SUVmax optimal thresholds were 7.20 (AUC, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.84-0.99) and 30.70 (AUC, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.95-1.00), respectively. Conclusion: SUVRsss and SUVmax are complementary quantitative correlates of Krenning scores 2-4 in [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE PET-visible, MRI-measurable meningiomas. Brain-only PET evaluation may provide an alternative to liver- and spleen-based visual grading and reduce the need for whole-body imaging in selected settings. Receiver-operating-characteristic curve-derived SUV thresholds correspond to Krenning scores used for eligibility for treatment with peptide receptor radionuclide therapy, supporting further evaluation of quantitative PET parameters for theranostic decision-making for patients with meningioma.© 2026 by the Society of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging.

title: Toward a Diagnostic Template for Acquired Apraxia of Speech: Insights From an Academy of Neurologic Communication Disorders Review.
abstract: Significant variation is observed in diagnostic assessments for individuals with acquired apraxia of speech (AOS). The lack of consistency across research related to AOS impacts the comparison of intervention outcomes. This extends to diagnostic criteria, assessment, and the inclusion of patient demographics. This viewpoint examines outcomes related to the consistency in diagnostic tool use and collection of demographic information and introduces a template to support researchers and clinicians conducting diagnostic evaluations. Materials include guidelines for a thorough case history, current diagnostic characteristics, and diagnostic assessment tools available for describing AOS. The template illustrates how such materials can be structured and applied in research and clinical practice.The recommendations provided in this viewpoint are part of a recent systematic review about AOS treatment outcomes. Trained raters extracted data from a comprehensive literature search from 1951 to April 2024 using a consensus protocol.Of the 92 studies included in data extraction, demographic information such as age, gender, etiology, and months post-onset was commonly reported, and information about race and ethnicity (described in 15% of studies), socioeconomic status (0%), current/previous occupation (8%), language history (10%), and education (59%) was described less frequently. Reported diagnostic characteristics varied across studies, reflecting differences in using discriminatory versus nondiscriminatory features. Concomitant diagnoses, such as aphasia severity (37%) and presence of dysarthria (32%), were not consistently reported or described.A template with specific criteria and assessments can support research replication, raise awareness of diagnostic strategies, and offer a structured framework for investigators and clinicians.https://doi.org/10.23641/asha.32012346.

llm_summary: Researchers examined inconsistencies in how acquired apraxia of speech (AOS), a neurological disorder affecting speech production, is diagnosed across clinical and research settings, which complicates the ability to compare treatment outcomes between studies. The team conducted a systematic review of 92 studies published between 1951 and April 2024, extracting data on demographic information collected and diagnostic characteristics reported using a consensus protocol. Common demographic variables like age and gender were described in most studies, but important information such as race and ethnicity (15% of studies), socioeconomic status (0%), and language history (10%) were rarely reported, and concomitant conditions like aphasia severity (37%) and dysarthria (32%) were inconsistently documented. The authors developed a diagnostic template that specifies criteria, assessment tools, and demographic data collection to standardize how AOS is evaluated in both research and clinical practice. Implementing this structured template could improve research replication, enhance clinician awareness of diagnostic strategies, and provide a consistent framework for evaluating individuals with AOS.

title: Midlife and Late-Life Alzheimer Disease Blood Biomarkers and 11-Year Cognitive Decline.
abstract: Plasma biomarkers of Alzheimer disease (AD) neuropathology (amyloid-β42 to amyloid β40 [Aβ42/40] ratio, phosphorylated tau at threonine [p-tau181]), neurodegeneration (neurofilament light [NfL]), and neuroinflammation (glial fibrillary acidic protein [GFAP]) in late-life are associated with cognitive decline. Whether these biomarkers in midlife are predictive of subsequent cognitive decline, and whether they are associated with different cognitive domains, is uncertain. In this study, we investigated associations of midlife and late-life plasma Aβ42/40, p-tau181, NfL, and GFAP with late-life change in domain-specific (memory, language, and executive function) and global cognitive function.We performed a prospective cohort analysis of the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Neurocognitive Study (ARIC-NCS). Outcome follow-up was from ARIC visit 5 (2011-2013) to visit 9 (2021-2022). We included all individuals from ARIC field centers (Jackson, Mississippi; Forsyth County, North Carolina; Washington County, Maryland; and Minneapolis suburbs, Minnesota) with biomarkers measured from stored specimens in midlife (visit 3, 1993-1995, mean age 59.0 years) and late-life (visit 5, 2011-2013, mean age 76.8 years). Aβ42/40, p-tau181, NfL, and GFAP were measured with the Quanterix Simoa platform and standardized to visit 3 to facilitate cross-biomarker comparisons of their rate of change from midlife to late-life. We estimated change in memory, language, executive function, and global cognition factor scores from visit 5 to visit 9 with linear mixed-effect models.In 1,515 included participants, 60.7% (n = 920) were female and 25.5% (n = 387) were Black. Each SD increase in p-tau181 in midlife was significantly associated with faster late-life memory decline (β = -0.030 [95% CI -0.059 to -0.001] SD. Midlife Aβ42/40, NfL, and GFAP were not associated with subsequent decline in any cognitive domain. In late-life, p-tau181, NfL, and GFAP were significantly associated with faster decline in different cognitive domains, with the strongest associations seen with memory (β = -0.091 [95% CI -0.123 to -0.058] SD; β = -0.064 [95% CI -0.106 to -0.023] SD; and β = -0.048 [95% CI -0.082 to -0.013] SD, respectively).Midlife p-tau181 was associated with faster 11-year memory decline beginning 20 years later in the ARIC cohort, which underscores a potentially long prodromal phase of cognitive decline that could precede dementia onset. In late-life, biomarkers for AD, neurodegeneration, and neuroinflammation were associated with faster decline across different cognitive domains, but associations remained strongest for p-tau181 and memory.

title: Sex differences and prevalence of prior deep vein thrombosis among patients with incidental iliac vein compression on computed tomography.
abstract: PurposeThe purpose of this study was to identify risk factors and evaluate clinical outcomes associated with incidental left common iliac vein compression on CT imaging.MethodsThis is a retrospective study that reviewed venous-phase abdomen and pelvis CT scans to identify patients with incidental extrinsic compression of the left common iliac vein due to an overlying right common iliac artery. A total of 726 patients were included (364 females, 362 males; mean patient age: 61.9 ± 15.9 years). Board-certified radiologists reviewed all CT scans. Significant left iliac vein compression was defined as >50% luminal narrowing.ResultsSignificant iliac vein compression was identified in 114 (15.7%) patients and was more common in females (19.5%) versus males (11.9%) (p < 0.01). Patients with iliac vein compression >50% had significantly lower BMI than those without compression (24.8 ± 6.2 vs 28.7 ± 7.2 kg/m2, p < 0.01). Patients with incidental left iliac vein compression had a higher rate of prior left lower extremity DVT (p = 0.02).ConclusionIncidental left common iliac vein compression was present in approximately 16% of patients and was more frequent among females. Compression was associated with lower BMI and more than twice the rate of ipsilateral DVT, despite no prior diagnosis of MTS. These findings suggest that incidental iliac vein compression could have more clinical significance than previously recognized.

title: Acute kidney injury in pregnancy is associated with increased risks for adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes: an integrated health system study.
abstract: Pregnancy-related acute kidney injury (PrAKI) is an uncommon but serious complication associated with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes, with limited data in high-resource settings.We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 29 586 deliveries at Mayo Clinic hospitals between 2017 and 2022. PrAKI was defined using Kidney Disease Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) creatinine criteria. Maternal characteristics, nephrotoxin exposure, clinical interventions, and neonatal outcomes were compared between patients with and without PrAKI.PrAKI occurred in 341 patients (1.15%). Compared with controls, PrAKI was associated with higher rates of chronic hypertension (28.7% vs 5.2%), cesarean delivery (68.5% vs 35.1%), intensive care unit (ICU) admission (59.1% vs 6.2%), and nephrotoxin exposure (58.7% vs 31.6%) (all P < .0001). Dialysis was required in 7.1% of patients with PrAKI, with 1.17% remaining dependent at discharge and 0.88% at 30 and 90 days; no control patients required dialysis. Neonates of mothers with PrAKI had higher rates of prematurity and neonatal ICU (NICU) admission (48.7% vs 9.8%; P < .0001). Maternal mortality was rare.PrAKI is a marker of severe maternal illness and is associated with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. Although most patients recover kidney function, a subset develop persistent dysfunction. title: Early Introduction and Prolonged Full-Dose Anakinra Reduce Recurrence Risk After Discontinuation in Recurrent Pericarditis: An International Multicenter Cohort.
abstract: Anakinra is effective in recurrent pericarditis, yet optimal treatment duration and strategies for safe drug discontinuation remain uncertain. Identifying predictors of sustained remission after discontinuation is important for clinical management.We retrospectively analyzed 185 consecutive adult patients with corticosteroid-dependent and colchicine-resistant refractory recurrent pericarditis across 16 international referral centers, who permanently discontinued therapy after clinical remission. The primary end point was pericarditis recurrence after drug discontinuation. Univariate and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression and Kaplan-Meier analyses were performed to identify demographic, clinical, and therapeutic predictors of postdiscontinuation relapse.Among 185 patients who discontinued anakinra (58.4% women, mean age 50.4±17.8 years, 77% idiopathic cause), treatment was initiated a median of 10 months (interquartile range [IQR], 4.0-19.5) after the first episode and continued at 100 mg/d for a median of 6 months (IQR, 4-12). Over a median follow-up of 7.2 months (IQR, 1.5-23.3) after discontinuation, 68 patients (36.8%) experienced recurrence, with a median time to recurrence of 2.1 months (IQR, 0.7-8.5). Initiation within 12 months from the first pericarditis episode and maintenance of full-dose therapy (100 mg/d) for ≥6 months were independently associated with lower recurrence risk (hazard ratio [HR], 0.33 [95% CI, 0.18-0.66]; P=0.001 and HR, 0.48 [95% CI, 0.23-0.86]; P=0.017; respectively).Early initiation of anakinra and maintenance of full-dose therapy for at least 6 months are associated with a significantly lower risk of relapse after discontinuation and may inform treatment duration and discontinuation strategies in recurrent pericarditis.

llm_summary: Researchers examined 185 patients with recurrent pericarditis (inflammation of the heart's outer lining) who had stopped responding to standard treatments and were treated with anakinra, an anti-inflammatory medication, to determine which factors predicted whether the condition would return after discontinuing the drug. Among patients who discontinued anakinra after achieving remission, 68 patients (36.8%) experienced recurrence over a median follow-up of 7.2 months, with recurrence occurring a median of 2.1 months after stopping treatment. Starting anakinra within 12 months of the first pericarditis episode and maintaining the full 100 mg daily dose for at least 6 months were independently associated with substantially lower recurrence risk (hazard ratios of 0.33 and 0.48, respectively, both statistically significant). These findings suggest that earlier treatment initiation and longer duration of full-dose therapy may reduce the likelihood of disease relapse after stopping anakinra. Future prospective studies would be needed to confirm whether these associations reflect causal relationships and to establish optimal treatment protocols for this condition.

title: Knotless Suture Repair For Chronic Lateral Ankle Instability: A Systematic Review and Single-Arm Meta-Analysis.
abstract: IntroductionThere is a need to assess the use of knotless sutures in cohorts with chronic ankle instability (CAI).MethodsA literature search of Embase, Ovid MEDLINE, Cochrane Library and Scopus was conducted from each database's inception to August 15, 2025. Eligible studies reported patients with CAI undergoing foot and ankle surgery with knotless suture repair. This review was registered in PROSPERO (ID: CRD420251106305).ResultsA total of 11 studies comprising 476 patients met the eligibility criteria. American Orthopaedic Foot and Ankle Society (AOFAS) scores preoperatively were 63.23 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 60.60-65.86, I2 = 91%) and at final follow-up were 90.67 (95% CI: 88.09-93.24, I2 = 96%). Karlsson-Peterson (KP) scores preoperatively were 62.75 (95% CI: 61.16-64.34, I2 = 79%) and at final follow-up were 88.03 (95% CI: 84.20-91.87, I2 = 97%). Visual analog scale (VAS) scores preoperatively were 5.80 (95% CI: 4.34-7.25, I2 = 100%) and at final follow-up were 1.23 (95% CI: 0.74-1.72, I2 = 96%). Anterior drawer preoperatively was 7.37 mm (95% CI: 5.21-9.53, I2 = 98%) and postoperatively was 3.12 mm (95% CI: 1.08-5.16, I2 = 99%). Talar tilt preoperatively was 7.000 (95% CI: 3.92-10.08, I2 = 98%) and postoperatively was 3.110 (95% CI: 2.76-3.46, I2 = 29%). The overall complication rate was 6% (95% CI: 0.03-0.09, I2 = 57%). The reoperation rate was 2% (95% CI: -0.01-0.03, I2 = 0%).ConclusionBased on low-quality evidence, knotless repair appears associated with improved functional scores and a low complication rate in this pooled analysis. Direct comparative studies against traditional Broström-Gould knotted approaches are warranted to determine the gold standard in CAI repair moving forward.

title: Endoscopic Decompression for Lateral Recess Stenosis Due to Vertebral Compression Fracture: A Case Report.
abstract: Case presentation.The interlaminar endoscopic lateral recess decompression (IE-LRD) represents a novel surgical alternative to consider in carefully selected cases, particularly when patients do not respond to conservative treatment.Lumbar spinal stenosis (LSS) constitutes one of the most prevalent spinal conditions in the elderly population around the world. A myriad of causes have been elucidated, and although infrequent, vertebral compression fractures (VCF) may also cause LSS. Conservative treatment might be the first option; however, patients often require surgery.A 76-year-old woman with a medical history of dementia consulted for radicular pain in her left leg during the past 6 months, without any favorable response to conservative treatment. Neurological examination revealed a positive straight leg raising test on the left. A spine MRI revealed a VCF in L5, linked with spondylolisthesis (grade I) at L5-S1. An IE-LRD was planned, as the patient did not consent to a classical open surgery. The incision was placed over the inferior medial edge of the left L4 lamina. Following sequential dilatators, the working channel was located on the inferomedial edge of the left L4 lamina. Lateral fluoroscopy (LF) guided the entire procedure. During the procedure, laminotomy was extended cranially and caudally to ensure sufficient vertebral decompression.After surgery, the patient was mobilized in the first 6 hours and discharged in the next 24 hours. Her lower back pain score improved significantly to 2-3, while her leg VAS pain improved to 0-1. After a follow-up for 18 months, the patient did not manifest complications or recurrences, and no additional treatment was carried out.(1) IE-LRD might be a useful and safe surgical procedure for the surgical management of LSS caused by VCF. (2) Consider this surgical alternative for elderly patients without a previous response to conservative medical treatment.Copyright © 2026 Wolters Kluwer Health, LLC. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Lumbar spinal stenosis, a common spinal condition in elderly patients, can occasionally result from vertebral compression fractures, which typically require surgical intervention when conservative treatment fails. This case report describes a 76-year-old woman with dementia who experienced six months of unrelieved left leg radicular pain caused by a vertebral compression fracture at L5 with grade I spondylolisthesis and underwent interlaminar endoscopic lateral recess decompression as an alternative to open surgery. Following the minimally invasive procedure, the patient's lower back pain score improved to 2-3 on a visual analog scale and her leg pain improved to 0-1, with mobilization occurring within six hours and discharge within 24 hours. At 18-month follow-up, the patient experienced no complications or recurrence of symptoms and required no additional treatment. The authors suggest that interlaminar endoscopic lateral recess decompression may represent a useful and safe surgical option for managing lumbar spinal stenosis caused by vertebral compression fractures in elderly patients who have not responded to conservative medical treatment.

The procedure involved sequential dilation and laminotomy guided by lateral fluoroscopy, with cranial and caudal extension to ensure adequate decompression. Following surgery, the patient demonstrated substantial pain improvement, with lower back pain visual analog scale scores decreasing to 2-3 and leg pain scores decreasing to 0-1, and was discharged within 24 hours. At 18-month follow-up, the patient experienced no complications, recurrences, or need for additional treatment. This case report suggests IE-LRD may represent a safe and useful surgical alternative for elderly patients with lumbar spinal stenosis secondary to vertebral compression fracture who have failed conservative management, though conclusions are limited by the single-case design.

title: Latent effector capacity governs reversible T cell exhaustion: A theoretical mathematical model of PD-1 blockade response.
abstract: T cell exhaustion is often viewed as a terminal state marked by irreversible loss of function during chronic infection and cancer. However, the rapid recovery of antitumor activity in clinical responders after PD-1 blockade suggests that some exhausted T cells retain hidden functional potential. To explain this paradox, we present a theoretical framework that separates latent effector capacity from active effector function. Latent effector capacity represents a history-dependent state reflecting preserved epigenetic accessibility and regulatory readiness, distinct from ongoing gene expression. In this model, PD-1 signaling acts as a reversible mask that suppresses effector function without eliminating the underlying effector capacity. The framework explains preserved chromatin accessibility, rapid reinvigoration after checkpoint blockade, and variable therapeutic responses. By incorporating nonlinear maintenance and erosion of latent effector capacity, the model predicts a bistable system with a point of no return beyond which exhaustion becomes irreversible. These principles may guide development of mechanistically informed biomarkers and artificial intelligence models predicting response to PD-1 therapy.

The model proposes that PD-1 signaling acts as a reversible suppressor that masks effector function without destroying the underlying capacity for immune response. title: GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment and cardiovascular outcomes following aortic valve replacement: a nationwide observational study.
abstract: GLP-1 receptor agonists reduce major adverse cardiovascular events among patients with diabetes, overweight, and obesity. Whether these benefits extend to patients undergoing aortic valve replacement (AVR) for severe aortic stenosis (AS) remains unknown. Thus, we investigated the association between GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment and cardiovascular outcomes after AVR.Nationwide population-based cohort study including consecutive patients with severe AS undergoing TAVI or SAVR in Western Denmark between January, 2016 and April, 2022. Patients were followed until death, emigration, crossover, or end of follow up on May 12, 2026. Propensity score-matching was performed to balance confounding. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, or aortic valve reoperation. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, aortic valve reoperation, with analyses accounting for the competing risk of death.Among 5259 eligible patients undergoing AVR, 292 propensity score-matched patients were included in the final analyses. During a mean follow up of 4.8±2.4 years, GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment was associated with a lower risk of the primary composite outcome compared with controls (HR 0.69, 95%CI 0.50-0.96, p=0.029). GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment was also associated with lower risk of all-cause mortality (HR 0.66, 95%CI 0.46-0.95, p=0.025). In competing risk analyses accounting for death, lower risks were observed for heart failure hospitalization (HR 0.67, 95%CI 0.48-0.93, p=0.018), and aortic valve reoperation (HR 0.69, 95%CI 0.49-0.98, p=0.037).Treatment with GLP-1 receptor agonists was associated with lower risk of cardiovascular outcomes including mortality following AVR among patients with severe AS.© The Author(s) 2026. title: Survival disparities in primary malignant spine tumors: a national analysis of academic and community hospital care.
abstract: Primary malignant osseous tumors of the mobile spine are rare and require complex, multidisciplinary care. Treatment outcomes may differ between academic and community hospitals due to variations in resources, expertise, and infrastructure. This study evaluates demographics, care delivery patterns, and clinical outcomes, including both short- and long-term survival, for patients treated at academic versus community cancer programs using the National Cancer Database.A retrospective analysis of a prospectively maintained database was performed. Nine hundred forty-three patients diagnosed with primary malignant osseous tumors of the mobile spine between 2004 and 2017 were identified. Patients were stratified by facility type: there were 601 patients treated at academic comprehensive cancer programs (ACADs) and 342 treated at comprehensive community cancer programs (CCCPs). Demographic, treatment, and clinical data were compared using descriptive statistics. Outcomes included inpatient length of stay, time to treatment, 30- and 90-day mortality, vital status at last contact, and overall survival. A multivariable Cox proportional hazards model assessed factors associated with overall survival.Patients at ACADs were significantly younger and more likely to have private insurance. The size and histopathological composition of the tumors did not differ significantly between facility types. ACAD patients experienced significantly longer inpatient stays and longer time to radiation initiation among patients receiving radiation with documented start dates. Time to chemotherapy did not significantly differ (p = 0.91). Thirty- and 90-day mortality were comparable between facility types among eligible surgical cases. At last follow-up, a significantly greater proportion of ACAD patients were alive (50.2% vs 38.3%, p < 0.001), and the median time from diagnosis to last contact or death was longer at ACADs (40.8 vs 33.2 months, p = 0.001). In the primary multivariable Cox model, treatment at an academic facility was associated with improved overall survival (hazard ratio [HR] 0.766, 95% CI 0.627-0.937; p = 0.009). In a sensitivity model adjusting for histopathology rather than grade, this association was attenuated and no longer statistically significant (CCCP vs ACAD, HR 1.19, p = 0.081).Patients treated at academic centers had longer inpatient stays and longer time to radiation initiation, yet academic facility treatment was associated with improved overall survival in the primary multivariable model. After accounting for histopathological subtype in sensitivity analysis, the facility-type association was attenuated, suggesting survival differences reflect both tumor biology and system-level care pathways.

title: US-based Delphi Consensus Study on Adjuvant Radiation Therapy (ART) in Node-Negative Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma (CSCC).
abstract: There is a paucity of high-level evidence for adjuvant radiation therapy (ART) in cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC) creating practice variations. This study provides expert consensus recommendations on patient and tumor selection, timing, duration, dosage, and additional considerations for ART in node-negative CSCC.The Delphi panel included 35 experts in radiation oncology (15), dermatology/Mohs micrographic surgery (9), medical oncology (7), head and neck surgery (3), and surgical oncology (1). Consensus was defined as ≥80% concordance; near-consensus 70-79% concordance.Consensus was reached to recommend ART when further surgery is not possible, but the tumor has positive gross or histologic/microscopic margins (35/35, 100%). Key consensus or near-consensus recommendations for recommending ART to the tumor bed following negative-margin surgery include: 5-year cumulative incidence of local recurrence (29/35, 83%) or nodal metastasis (27/35, 77%) ≥ 20%; gross cortical bone/marrow invasion (32/35, 91%); skull base invasion (32/35, 91%); 4 risk factors (RF) (35/35, 100%); 3 RF (30-33/35, 86-94%); PNI ≥ 0.1 mm and one other RF (30/35, 86%); and clinical nerve invasion (31/35, 89%). Immune status influenced ART decision-making (30/35, 86%) with 77% (27/35) more likely to recommend ART for immunosuppressed patients. Consensus was reached to omit ART for pathologic complete response following neoadjuvant immunotherapy (34/35, 97%). Among radiation oncologists, 100% (15/15) agreed the optimal window for ART to the tumor bed is 4-8 weeks and that hypofractionated regimens can be appropriate (12/15, 80%). Consensus was reached for prescription doses of 60-66 Gy in 2 Gy/fx (15/15, 100%) or 50-55 Gy in 2.5 Gy/fx (13/15, 87%), and that superficial radiation and brachytherapy are inappropriate ART modalities for node-negative high-stage CSCC (14/15, 93%). There was no consensus on elective nodal basin irradiation.This Delphi study provides an expert consensus-based framework to standardize ART for node-negative high-stage CSCC following surgery, informing future guidelines and utilization.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. llm_summary: Rusfertide is a hepcidin agonist being investigated as a potential treatment for polycythemia vera, a blood disorder characterized by excessive red blood cell production. The authors reviewed the mechanism of action of rusfertide and evaluated clinical trial results demonstrating its efficacy in managing this condition. Rusfertide works by activating hepcidin signaling pathways, which regulate iron metabolism and subsequently reduce abnormal red blood cell production in polycythemia vera patients. The clinical trial data presented indicate that rusfertide provides measurable therapeutic benefit in controlling disease manifestations in this patient population. This incremental benefit assessment suggests rusfertide may represent a valuable addition to the treatment options available for polycythemia vera, though further investigation and clinical experience will be needed to establish its optimal role in patient management.

title: Management Strategies and Clinical Outcomes of Methicillin Resistant Staphylococcus Aureus Native Vertebral Osteomyelitis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) is a major cause of native vertebral osteomyelitis (NVO) and is associated with persistent infection, complications, prolonged hospitalization, and increased mortality.We conducted this systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the antimicrobial and surgical approaches used for MRSA NVO and their associated clinical outcomes.Systematic review and meta-analysis.A systematic literature search of MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science was conducted on November 27, 2025. Studies were eligible if they included adults with MRSA NVO, evaluated medical or surgical treatment strategies, reported clinical outcomes, and included at least five patients. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and the Murad et al. tool. Random-effects models were used to pool proportions of treatment success, reinfection, and mortality.Thirty studies including 677 patients were included. Treatment strategies were heterogeneous and included prolonged anti-MRSA antimicrobial therapy and surgical approaches ranging from debridement and drainage to decompression and spinal stabilization or fusion. Vancomycin-based regimens were the most frequently reported antimicrobial strategy. Among studies reporting treatment duration, intravenous therapy commonly ranged from 4 to 8 weeks, with some patients receiving oral step-down or suppressive therapy. The pooled treatment success rate was 84.9% (95% CI, 76.7%-90.7%), pooled reinfection rate was 15.3% (95% CI, 9.5%-23.6%), and pooled mortality rate was 3.1% (95% CI, 0.8%-10.8%). Subgroup analyses were not feasible because treatment-specific data were limited and inconsistently reported.Management of MRSA NVO varied substantially across studies, with vancomycin-based antimicrobial therapy and diverse surgical strategies commonly reported. Pooled outcomes showed high treatment success with lower rates of reinfection and mortality. The substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity of the available evidence highlights the need for prospective studies with standardized treatment and outcome reporting.Copyright © 2026. llm_summary: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) causes serious spinal bone infections that can lead to persistent disease, complications, and prolonged hospitalization, making it important to understand which treatments work best. Researchers conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of 30 studies involving 677 patients to evaluate different antimicrobial drugs and surgical approaches used to treat MRSA native vertebral osteomyelitis, with vancomycin-based antibiotic regimens being the most commonly reported medication strategy. The pooled analysis found a treatment success rate of 84.9% (95% CI, 76.7%-90.7%), a reinfection rate of 15.3% (95% CI, 9.5%-23.6%), and a mortality rate of 3.1% (95% CI, 0.8%-10.8%), suggesting favorable overall outcomes with current approaches. These results indicate that combined antimicrobial and surgical management of MRSA spinal infections achieves high success rates, though the substantial variation in how different studies reported their treatments and outcomes limits the ability to determine which specific strategies.

title: Dose Optimization of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors: A Policy opportunity to reduce costs and improve access to immunotherapy in the United States.
abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have revolutionized cancer treatment, but are associated with high costs and limited accessibility. Optimizing dosing strategy to achieve a Pharmacokinetics/Pharmacodynamics (PK/PD) supported alternative lower dose (PPALD) that maintains clinical benefit and offers a cost-minimization strategy with substantial health system savings.We conducted a literature review of Phase 1/2 trials describing the PPALD dose of three commonly used ICIs: Pembrolizumab, Nivolumab and Atezolizumab. Alternate dosing strategies based on data for pembrolizumab (2mg/kg), nivolumab (2mg/kg) and atezolizumab (10mg/kg) were proposed. Public CMS Medicare Part B data on expenditure for these therapies was used to obtain average cost/dose, mg/dose, and number of Medicare beneficiaries between 2018-2021. Costs were calculated based on current FDA approved dosing and alternate dosing strategies.PPALD resulted in substantially lower drug costs per patient for an 80kg individual compared with fixed dosing: pembrolizumab ($7,393.60 vs $9,242.00), nivolumab ($4,153.60 vs $12,460.80), and atezolizumab ($5,744.00 vs $8,616.00). Estimated 2018-2021 Medicare savings based on beneficiaries were $382.2 million for pembrolizumab, $943.1 million for nivolumab, and $114.4 million for atezolizumab, totaling nearly $1.44 billion.Alternate immunotherapy dosing represents a high-value cost saving strategy to reduce health care costs and improve global access. Implementation requires regulatory adaptation, smaller vials, or vial-sharing to minimize waste.This policy analysis demonstrates that evidence-based alternate dosing of commonly used checkpoint inhibitors (Pembrolizumab, Nivolumab and Atezolizumab) could substantially reduce drug expenses while maintaining efficacy. Using Medicare Part B utilization data, we estimated that implementation of these alternative dosing strategies can help save over $1.44 billion between 2018-2021. These findings have important implications for health policy by improving patient access to immunotherapy and curtailing financial toxicity. This can be further facilitated by the support of policymakers, regulatory agencies supporting prospective validation studies and development of reimbursement models that encourage dose optimization.Copyright © 2026. title: Changes in Peripheral Immune Cell Subsets Following Endoscopic Sinus Surgery Differ Between CRSwNP and AERD.
abstract: Changes in peripheral eosinophils follow endoscopic sinus surgery (ESS) in chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP), with and without aspirin sensitivity. Cytometry by time-of-flight (CyTOF) identifies more immune cell subsets than conventional assays or clinical testing. We hypothesized that ESS-associated changes in peripheral immune cell subsets differ between aspirin-tolerant (AT)-CRSwNP and aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease (AERD) as measured by CyTOF.Pre- and post-ESS peripheral blood from patients with CRSwNP (n = 13) or with AERD (n = 15) was analyzed for immune cell populations using a 37-marker CyTOF panel. CITRUS analysis identified cell clusters most predictive of patient group or sample timepoint.In the combined cohort of 28 patients, circulating CD4+ naïve T cells and CD194+ neutrophils increased after ESS, while eosinophils decreased. When stratified by disease, CD4+ naïve T cells increased in both AERD and CRSwNP post-ESS; however, eosinophils decreased after ESS only in CRSwNP. Neutrophil subsets showed a mixed response in both patient groups after ESS. Dendritic cells increased in CRSwNP but not in AERD after ESS. Individual timepoint analyses showed more CD141+ monocyte-derived DCs (moDCs) in CRSwNP than in AERD pre- and post-ESS. Pre-ESS, both CD185+ and CD194+ neutrophils were higher in AERD compared to CRSwNP.CD141+ moDCs were more prevalent in CRSwNP versus AERD, both before and after ESS. Naïve CD4+ T cells increased, and neutrophil subsets changed in all groups after ESS, but eosinophils decreased only in CRSwNP. Our study points to possible systemic immune effects of ESS and candidate immune signatures in CRSwNP and AERD.© 2026 ARS‐AAOA, LLC.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether endoscopic sinus surgery (ESS) produces different changes in immune cell populations between patients with chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) and those with aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease (AERD), using advanced flow cytometry analysis of blood samples from 28 patients before and after surgery. The study found that while naive CD4+ T cells increased after ESS in both disease groups and eosinophils decreased only in CRSwNP patients, dendritic cells increased only in the CRSwNP group. Additionally, a specific type of dendritic cell called CD141+ monocyte-derived dendritic cells was more prevalent in CRSwNP compared to AERD both before and after surgery. These distinct immune responses suggest that ESS may have different systemic immunological effects depending on whether patients have aspirin sensitivity. The findings point to potential immune signatures that could distinguish between these two conditions, though further research is needed to understand the clinical significance of these changes.

title: Personalized Circulating Tumor DNA Analysis for Predicting Outcomes and Tracking Response to Radiotherapy and Pembrolizumab in Localized Sarcomas: Analysis of the SU2C-SARC032 Trial.
abstract: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) holds promise for prognostication and disease monitoring in solid tumors. However, rare and heterogenous tumors with low mutational burden like soft tissue sarcomas (STS) present a technical challenge for ctDNA analysis. We investigated the ability of personalized ctDNA analysis to predict outcomes and track response to radiotherapy and pembrolizumab in patients with localized STS.We analyzed 313 plasma samples collected pretreatment, postradiotherapy/presurgery, and postsurgery from 106 patients treated with preoperative radiotherapy with or without perioperative pembrolizumab for high-risk, localized STS in the SU2C-SARC032 phase II randomized trial. Personalized ctDNA assays were designed to track a median of 46 somatic mutations per patient. Associations between ctDNA levels and outcomes were assessed using univariable and multivariable models adjusting for clinical risk factors.Personalized ctDNA profiling detected baseline ctDNA in 85% of patients. Baseline ctDNA levels correlated with tumor size, grade 3 disease, and expression of genes related to hypoxia and the cell cycle. ctDNA levels pretreatment, after radiotherapy with or without immunotherapy but before surgery, and postsurgery were strongly associated with disease-free and overall survival on univariable and multivariable analyses. Patients treated with pembrolizumab, who had significantly better disease-free survival, had a greater decrease in their ctDNA levels after neoadjuvant therapy. Finally, personalized ctDNA analysis enabled noninvasive subclone tracking and patients with multiple tumor clones detected by ctDNA analysis after surgery had inferior outcomes.Tumor-informed, personalized profiling enables sensitive ctDNA detection and quantitative monitoring in localized STS, providing independent prognostic information across the perioperative course. These findings support prospective ctDNA-guided interventional trials in STS.

llm_summary: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), fragments of cancer DNA found in blood, could help predict outcomes and monitor treatment response in soft tissue sarcomas, a rare cancer type that has historically been difficult to track using ctDNA due to low mutation rates. Researchers analyzed blood samples from 106 patients with localized soft tissue sarcoma who received preoperative radiotherapy with or without the immunotherapy drug pembrolizumab, designing personalized ctDNA assays to track an average of 46 mutations per patient across samples collected before treatment, after radiotherapy, and after surgery. Baseline ctDNA was detected in 85% of patients and correlated with larger tumors and more aggressive disease, while ctDNA levels at all three timepoints were strongly associated with disease-free and overall survival independent of other clinical risk factors. Patients who received pembrolizumab showed greater decreases in ctDNA levels after neoadjuvant therapy and had better disease-free survival, and the presence of multiple tumor clones detected by ctDNA analysis after surgery was associated with worse outcomes. These findings suggest that personalized ctDNA profiling could provide independent prognostic information.

title: Pathologic Complete Response (pCR) Rate and Predictors of Response to Taxane, Trastuzumab, and Pertuzumab in HER2‑Positive Breast Cancer: Secondary Analyses of EA1181/CompassHER2 pCR.
abstract: EA1181 (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT04266249) is a single-arm trial evaluating neoadjuvant taxane, trastuzumab, and pertuzumab (THP) in patients with clinical stage II/IIIa human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-positive breast cancer. This report focuses on the secondary end points of pathologic complete response (pCR) rates and associated factors. The primary end point-3-year recurrence-free survival among patients achieving a pCR (ypT0/Tis, ypN0)-will be reported when data mature.Patients received four cycles of trastuzumab and pertuzumab (HP) with either once per week paclitaxel (12 weeks) or docetaxel (every 3 weeks for four cycles), followed by surgery. Clinicopathologic characteristics were assessed in all patients. The HER2DX pCR score was determined using diagnostic biopsy samples in a representative subset. Logistic regression models identified factors associated with pCR.A total of 2,175 patients were enrolled (781 HER2+/estrogen receptor‑negative [ER-]; 1,394 HER2+/ER+). Of 2,141 patients who initiated THP, the overall pCR rate was 43.8%: 63.7% in HER2+/ER- and 32.4% in HER2+/ER+ tumors. Higher pCR rates were observed in tumors that were ER-negative or low ER expressing, progesterone receptor-negative or low expressing, HER2 immunohistochemistry (IHC) 3+, and in patients treated with once per week paclitaxel. T3 disease was associated with a lower pCR rate in HER2+/ER- tumors; otherwise, tumor (T) and nodal (N) stage did not significantly affect pCR. Among 569 patients assessed for HER2DX pCR scores, a high score was independently associated with higher pCR rates, after adjustment for clinicopathologic variables.Neoadjuvant THP achieved pCR in nearly two-thirds of patients with HER2+/ER- and one third with HER2+/ER+ breast cancer. Low hormone receptor expression, HER2 IHC 3+ status, once per week paclitaxel use, and a high HER2DX pCR score were independent predictors of pCR. These findings should help optimize risk stratification and treatment personalization for patients with HER2-positive breast cancer.

title: Breast Cancer Follow-Up and Surveillance After Primary Treatment: ASCO Guideline Update.
abstract: ASCO Guidelines provide recommendations with comprehensive review and analyses of the relevant literature for each recommendation, following the guideline development process as outlined in the https://www.asco.org/practice-patients/guidelines/guideline-methodology. ASCO Guidelines follow the https://www.asco.org/about-asco/legal/conflict-interest-coi.Clinical Practice Guidelines and other guidance ("Guidance") provided by ASCO is not a comprehensive or definitive guide to treatment options. It is intended for voluntary use by clinicians and should be used in conjunction with independent professional judgment. Guidance may not be applicable to all patients, interventions, diseases or stages of diseases. Guidance is based on review and analysis of relevant literature, and is not intended as a statement of the standard of care. ASCO does not endorse third-party drugs, devices, services, or therapies and assumes no responsibility for any harm arising from or related to the use of this information. See complete disclaimer in Appendix 1 and Appendix 2 (online only) for more.To offer clinicians recommendations concerning breast cancer follow-up and surveillance after primary treatment.ASCO convened an Expert Panel to develop recommendations based on a systematic review and a formal consensus process.One randomized controlled trial (RCT) was identified and formed the evidentiary basis for the surveillance mammography guideline recommendation. No RCTs were identified that evaluated different follow-up approaches by risk of relapse in patients treated for early-stage breast cancer. Given the dearth of evidence identified in the systematic review of the literature, formal modified Delphi consensus-based recommendations were generated.The guideline offers recommendations on the role of a risk-based approach to the frequency and intensity of follow-up among patients with breast cancer in the adjuvant setting. Regular history, physical examination, and mammography are recommended for breast cancer follow-up. Either virtual or in-person visits can be offered. Certain patients at a high risk of cancer recurrence warrant closer surveillance, such as those patients with locally advanced disease or residual disease following neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Recommendations on the use of blood-based biomarkers and supplemental imaging are provided. Guideline recommendations will be updated once additional evidence-based tools become available to better individualize surveillance.Additional information is available at www.ascopubs.org/topics/asco-guidelines/breast-cancer.

llm_summary: ASCO convened an expert panel to develop evidence-based recommendations for breast cancer follow-up and surveillance after primary treatment to guide clinical practice. The panel conducted a systematic review of the literature and identified only one randomized controlled trial evaluating surveillance mammography, while no trials were found comparing different follow-up approaches based on recurrence risk in early-stage breast cancer patients. The resulting guideline recommends regular history, physical examination, and mammography as standard follow-up care, with the option of either virtual or in-person visits for patient convenience. Patients at high risk of cancer recurrence, such as those with locally advanced disease or residual disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy, warrant closer surveillance intensity and frequency tailored to their individual risk profiles. The panel provided recommendations on blood-based biomarkers and supplemental imaging while acknowledging that future guideline updates will incorporate additional evidence-based tools as they become available to better personalize surveillance strategies.
llm_summary_expert: An Expert Panel convened by ASCO developed recommendations for breast cancer follow-up and surveillance after primary treatment through systematic literature review and formal consensus methodology. The systematic review identified only one randomized controlled trial evaluating surveillance mammography and no RCTs comparing different follow-up approaches stratified by recurrence risk in early-stage breast cancer patients, necessitating modified Delphi consensus-based recommendations. The guideline recommends regular history, physical examination, and mammography for all patients, with either virtual or in-person visits offered as options. Patients with locally advanced disease or residual disease following neoadjuvant chemotherapy warrant closer surveillance intensity based on recurrence risk stratification. The recommendations on blood-based biomarkers and supplemental imaging are provisional pending availability of additional evidence-based tools to better individualize surveillance strategies.

title: Inactivation of the polycomb repressive complex 2 (PRC2) in osteoblasts increases post-natal trabecular bone mass and mechanical bone strength.
abstract: The epigenetic methyltransferases Ezh1 or Ezh2 each interact with two structural proteins (Eed and Suz12) to form Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2). Inhibition of Ezh2 stimulates osteoblast differentiation and bone formation, but Ezh2 conditional knockout (cKO) mice have variable skeletal phenotypes. Ezh1 null mice are phenotypically normal. Here, we show that combined homozygous ablation of both Ezh1 and Ezh2 alleles results in a pronounced bone phenotype, suggesting genetic redundancy between Ezh1 and Ezh2. Transient loss of Eed, Suz12 or Ezh2 by siRNA depletion or treatment with distinct PRC2 inhibitors (A395, EED226 and GSK126) enhances differentiation of MC3T3-E1 pre-osteoblasts (i.e., increased Bglap, Ibsp and mineralization). We compared Ezh2 cKO mice with Ezh1 null (KO) mice, and mice with both Ezh2 cKO and Ezh1 KO alleles (dKO mice) in the presence of the Osterix/Sp7-Cre recombination driver. During active bone development (post-natal 8 weeks), both male and female dKO mice exhibit significantly increased L5 trabecular bone mass, femoral cortical thickness and the relative midshaft bone volume (μCT), as well as bone strength (3-point bending) compared to Ezh1 KO or Ezh2 cKO mice. Suppression of Cre recombination using doxycycline (DOX) for 8 weeks prevents the dKO phenotype, but subsequent DOX removal increases trabecular bone mass in dKO mice by 14 weeks. Conditional Eed ablation (which inactivates PRC2/Ezh1 and PRC2/Ezh2) results in a similar high- bone and increased mechanical strength phenotype in male and female Eed cKO. Our findings identify PRC2 as a suppressor of post-natal bone accrual in Osx/Sp7 lineage cells, and a potential target for strategies to improve bone mass accrual.Copyright © 2026. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether inactivating the Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2), a group of proteins that silences genes through epigenetic modifications, could enhance bone formation in osteoblasts, the cells responsible for building bone. Using genetically modified mice with deletions of PRC2 components (Ezh1, Ezh2, or Eed) in bone-forming cells, they measured trabecular bone mass, cortical thickness, and mechanical strength during the post-natal bone development period. Mice lacking both Ezh1 and Ezh2 (dKO mice) and mice lacking Eed showed significantly increased trabecular bone mass, cortical thickness, and bone strength compared to mice with single component deletions. These findings suggest that PRC2 normally acts as a brake on bone formation during post-natal development, and removing this brake enhances bone accrual and mechanical properties. The results identify PRC2 as a potential therapeutic target for strategies aimed at improving bone mass, though further research would be needed to translate these findings from animal models to clinical applications.

During active bone development at 8 weeks post-natal, dKO mice exhibited significantly increased lumbar vertebra 5 trabecular bone mass, femoral cortical thickness, and relative midshaft bone volume on microcomputed tomography, along with enhanced bone strength measured by three-point bending compared to single knockout controls. title: Updated treatment targets in inflammatory bowel disease (STRIDE-III): an initiative of the International Organization for the Study of IBD.
abstract: Since Selecting Therapeutic Targets in Inflammatory Bowel Disease-II (STRIDE-II), new evidence has become available across inflammatory and patient-centred outcomes. We aimed to update the STRIDE recommendations for Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis. We searched MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL for studies published after the STRIDE-II search period. Findings were integrated with surveys of International Organization for the Study of IBD (IOIBD) members and paediatric gastroenterologists from the Porto group of the European Society for Paediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition. Statements were subsequently voted on using a modified Delphi approach; consensus was defined as ≥75% of participants rating a statement 7-10 on a 10-point scale. Of 13 071 records identified in the systematic review, 1018 were included. Surveys were completed by 60 of 79 IOIBD gastroenterologists and 23 of 30 paediatric gastroenterologists in the Porto group. STRIDE-III defines three conceptually distinct categories of treatment targets. Actionable targets include clinical response and remission, which reflect patient priorities, and objective inflammatory targets (C-reactive protein normalisation, faecal calprotectin within target range, and endoscopic remission), supported by interventional evidence demonstrating benefits of target-guided treatment modification. Adjunctive targets (ie, urgency, histological remission in ulcerative colitis, transmural remission in Crohn's disease, and growth) are supported by studies showing association with favourable outcomes and guide treatment optimisation and tighter monitoring but do not necessarily require a change in therapeutic class. Patient-centred targets (ie, disability, fatigue, and quality of life) directly reflect patients' well-being and are impaired in a substantial proportion of patients with inflammatory bowel disease; impairment should prompt assessment of inflammation and alternative causes and management through shared decision-making. Targets are further classified as immediate, short-term, intermediate, and long-term. STRIDE-III also defines treatment-specific times to target achievement, new faecal calprotectin thresholds, and adaptations for resource-limited settings. STRIDE-III distinguishes targets that should prompt treatment change from those that primarily guide optimisation and monitoring, while establishing a separate patient-centred pathway based on shared decision-making. STRIDE-III establishes three categories of treatment targets: actionable targets (clinical response, remission, and objective inflammatory markers like C-reactive protein and fecal calprotectin) that should prompt treatment changes when not achieved; adjunctive targets (such as histological remission and growth) that guide optimization and monitoring without necessarily requiring new medications; and patient-centered targets (disability, fatigue, quality of life) that reflect well-being and warrant investigation of underlying causes through shared decision-making. The framework classifies targets by timing of achievement (immediate, short-term, intermediate, and long-term) and defines specific fecal calprotectin thresholds and adaptations for resource-limited settings. This updated guidance distinguishes between targets requiring therapeutic escalation and those primarily guiding treatment refinement, providing a structured, evidence-based approach to individualized care in inflammatory bowel disease.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether incident cerebral microhemorrhages (CMHs)—small brain bleeds detected on MRI—contribute to early cognitive decline in cognitively unimpaired individuals with elevated amyloid, a protein associated with Alzheimer's disease risk. In this post hoc analysis of the A4 study, participants underwent serial MRI scans and cognitive assessments while researchers tracked longitudinal changes in multiple measures including the Clinical Dementia Rating-Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) and Cognitive Function Index (CFI), adjusting for baseline amyloid burden and demographic factors. Participants who developed two or more incident CMHs showed greater worsening on the CDR-SB (estimate = 0.44; 95% CI, 0.09–0.80; P = . 009) and CFI (estimate = 1.37; 95% CI, 0.11–2.60; P = . 03), but not on objective cognitive testing or activities of daily living measures.

title: Medicare and Medicaid Professional Fee Reimbursement for Spinal Cord Stimulation: An Analysis of National and State-level Trends.
abstract: Spinal cord stimulation (SCS) is an important modality for treating chronic pain in patients who have failed conservative therapy and a substantial portion of the population rely on fee-for-service Medicare or Medicaid for coverage. We aimed to determine physician professional fee reimbursement rates and the ratio of Medicaid to Medicare professional fee reimbursement (MMI) for three common Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) codes related to SCS therapy (63650, 63685, and 63655) across states. Secondarily, we explored trends in utilization and reimbursement of these procedures by Medicare at the national level between 2013 and 2023.Medicaid professional fee reimbursement data were extracted from publicly available fee schedules where available for individual states, while Medicare reimbursement data were extracted from the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) Physician Fee Schedule. Baseline and wage-adjusted MMI values were calculated for each state.Medicaid reimbursed 11.5-21.0% less than Medicare across the evaluated CPT codes after wage adjustment, with differences of 11.8% for CPT 63650 (facility), 18.0% for CPT 63650 (non-facility), 11.5% for CPT 63685 (facility), and 21.0% for CPT 63655 (facility). Medicaid MMI values ranged from 0.397-1.87 across codes and settings. State-level Medicaid professional fee reimbursement varied substantially, ranging from $194.52-$639.38 for CPT 63650 (facility), $978.72-$2,781.65 for CPT 63650 (non-facility), $160.82-$558.00 for CPT 63685 (facility), and $375.97-$1,045.15 for CPT 63655 (facility); Medicare reimbursement was substantially less variable. From 2013-2023, Medicare utilization, rendering providers, beneficiaries, and standardized payments generally increased, although trends varied by CPT code and site of service.Medicare physician professional fee reimbursement largely exceeds Medicaid physician professional fee reimbursement for three of the most common SCS procedural codes, suggesting potential access barriers to chronic pain procedures. title: Life-Course Blood Pressure Trajectories and Focal Myocardial Fibrosis in Older Age in MyoFit46.
abstract: The impact of life-course blood pressure (BP) trajectories on later-life focal left ventricular (LV) fibrosis by late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) remains elusive.MyoFit46 prospectively recruited ≈500 participants from a 1946 birth cohort for a cardiovascular magnetic resonance scan at 77 years, assessing LV LGE calculated using the 3-SD method or 5-SD method. Systolic BP (SBP) and diastolic BP were recorded at 36, 43, 53, 63, 69, and 77 years. For each participant, annual rates of BP change (steepness) and area under the BP trajectory (cumulative burden) for each age interval were calculated using mixed-effects models. Associations between life-course BPs and LGE were tested using generalized linear models, adjusted for antihypertensives, demographics, lifestyle, and comorbidities. Time-to-event associations between LGE and incident major adverse cardiovascular event (hospitalizations for coronary artery disease, stroke, heart failure, and atrial/ventricular arrhythmias; n=29) were also evaluated.Among 472 participants (54% male), each 10 mm Hg greater individual SBPs at 36 to 69 years were associated with 6% to 11% greater LV LGE calculated using the 3-SD method (all P≤0.033), whereas each 10 mm Hg sustained greater SBPs on any age interval from 36 to 69 associated with 16% to 24% greater LGE calculated using the 3-SD method at 77(all P≤0.005), independent of SBP at 77 years. Each 1 mm Hg/y steeper SBP rise during age intervals 36 to 43, 43 to 53, and 53 to 63 was associated with 6% to 12% greater LGE calculated using the 3-SD method at 77 years. LGE presence was associated with greater major adverse cardiovascular event rates (hazard ratio, 2.5 [95% CI, 1.2-5.2]).Higher life-course BPs, cumulative burden, and steeper increases were associated with greater older-age LV LGE, which was linked to incident major adverse cardiovascular events. BP trajectories, beyond single-point BP measurements, warrant further investigation as tools to guide BP management strategies.

llm_summary: The MyoFit46 study examined whether blood pressure patterns across a person's lifetime predict heart muscle scarring (focal fibrosis) detected by cardiac imaging in older age, since the long-term effects of blood pressure trajectories on heart structure remain unclear. Researchers followed approximately 472 participants from a 1946 birth cohort, measuring their systolic and diastolic blood pressure at ages 36, 43, 53, 63, 69, and 77 years, then performed cardiac magnetic resonance scans at age 77 to assess left ventricular scarring using late gadolinium enhancement imaging. Each 10 mm Hg higher systolic blood pressure at ages 36 to 69 years was associated with 6% to 11% greater scarring at age 77, and sustained higher systolic blood pressure across any age interval showed even stronger associations with 16% to 24% greater scarring, independent of blood pressure at age 77 itself. title: ICare-FASTER (Improving Care by Faster Risk Stratification Through Use of High-Sensitivity Point-of-Care Troponin in Patients Presenting With Possible Acute Coronary Syndrome in the Emergency Department): A Stepped-Wedge Cluster-Randomized Trial.
abstract: Point-of-care high-sensitivity cTn (cardiac troponin; hs-cTn) testing has the potential to expedite decision-making and reduce emergency department (ED) length of stay for patients presenting with possible myocardial infarction by ensuring that results are consistently available when sought by clinicians. We assessed the real-life effectiveness and safety of implementing point-of-care hs-cTn testing in the ED.We conducted a pragmatic, stepped-wedge cluster-randomized trial. The control arm was usual care with an accelerated diagnostic pathway using a single-sample rule-out step with a central laboratory hs-cTn assay. The intervention arm used the same pathway with a point-of-care hs-cTnI assay. The primary effectiveness outcome was ED length of stay assessed using a generalized linear mixed model. The safety outcome was myocardial infarction or cardiac death within 30 days.Six sites participated, with 59 980 ED presentations (44 747 individuals; mean 61±19 years of age; 49.5% female) from February 2023 through January 2025; 31 392 presentations were during the intervention arm. After adjustment for covariates associated with length of stay, the intervention reduced length of stay by 13% (95% CI, 9%-16%; P<0.001), corresponding to a reduction of 47 minutes (95% CI, 33-61 minutes) from a mean length of stay in the control arm of 376 minutes. The 30-day myocardial infarction or cardiac death rate was similar in the control and intervention arms (0.39% and 0.39%, respectively; P=0.54).Implementation of whole-blood hs-cTnI testing at the point of care into an accelerated diagnostic pathway was safe and reduced length of stay in the ED compared with laboratory testing.URL: https://www.anzctr.org.au; Unique identifier: ACTRN12619001189112.

llm_summary: The ICare-FASTER trial evaluated whether point-of-care high-sensitivity cardiac troponin testing could improve emergency department efficiency for patients with suspected heart attacks compared to traditional central laboratory testing. Researchers conducted a stepped-wedge cluster-randomized trial across six sites involving 59,980 emergency department presentations (44,747 individuals) from February 2023 through January 2025, comparing usual care with laboratory testing to the same diagnostic pathway using a bedside troponin assay. The intervention reduced emergency department length of stay by 13% (95% CI, 9%-16%; P<0.001), equivalent to 47 minutes shorter stays from a baseline of 376 minutes, with no difference in safety outcomes as the 30-day rates of myocardial infarction or cardiac death were 0.39% in both groups (P=0.54). These results suggest that implementing point-of-care high-sensitivity troponin testing into accelerated diagnostic pathways can safely expedite patient care in emergency departments. The pragmatic design reflects real-world implementation, though the findings are specific to the participating sites and the particular troponin assay.
llm_summary_expert: The ICare-FASTER trial was a pragmatic, stepped-wedge cluster-randomized trial comparing point-of-care high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) testing versus central laboratory hs-cTn testing within an accelerated diagnostic pathway for 59,980 emergency department presentations (44,747 individuals; mean age 61±19 years; 49.5% female) across six sites from February 2023 through January 2025. The primary effectiveness outcome was emergency department length of stay, analyzed using a generalized linear mixed model with adjustment for covariates, while the safety outcome was myocardial infarction or cardiac death within 30 days. Point-of-care hs-cTnI testing reduced length of stay by 13% (95% CI, 9%-16%; P<0.001), corresponding to a 47-minute reduction (95% CI, 33-61 minutes) from a control mean of 376 minutes. The 30-day myocardial infarction or cardiac death rate was 0.39% in both intervention and control arms.

title: ASFNR Clinical State of Practice Statement on Imaging of Chronic Subdural Hematoma.
abstract: The efficacy of middle meningeal artery embolization (MMAE) for chronic subdural hematoma (cSDH) has heightened interest in imaging biomarkers that may reflect neomembrane activity, predict recurrence, and identify patients most likely to benefit from treatment. Characterization of hematoma internal architecture, referred to as the imaging phenotype, may provide indirect information regarding the biological activity and maturation of the neomembrane. However, imaging phenotype has not been incorporated into randomized trials or validated treatment-selection algorithms, and standardized definitions and reporting remain lacking.The American Society of Functional Neuroradiology Clinical Practice Committee developed this State of Practice statement through expert consensus and review of the available literature.Noncontrast CT (NCCT) remains the primary imaging modality for cSDH assessment. Hematoma burden should be characterized by maximum thickness measured perpendicular to the inner table, midline shift, and, when appropriate, volume. Volume may be estimated using the ABC/2 formula, whereas segmentation is more accurate for irregular, crescentic, or multiloculated collections when available. Internal architecture should be described using the Nakaguchi framework of homogeneous, laminar, separated, and trabecular phenotypes, with mixed or transitional features explicitly reported. Advanced techniques, including dual-energy CT, photon-counting CT, MRI, and arterial spin labeling, may provide information regarding membrane activity but are supported by limited, largely single-center evidence and currently have a problem-solving rather than routine role. Standardized reporting and prospective validation are needed before imaging phenotype or advanced-imaging biomarkers can guide treatment selection.© 2026 by American Journal of Neuroradiology.
