llm_summary: The American Society of Functional Neuroradiology Clinical Practice Committee developed a consensus statement to standardize imaging assessment of chronic subdural hematoma, a condition where blood collects between the brain and its outer membrane, because improved imaging methods may help predict which patients will benefit from middle meningeal artery embolization, a minimally invasive treatment. The statement recommends that noncontrast CT remain the primary imaging tool and that hematoma size be measured by maximum thickness, midline shift, and volume when appropriate, with volume estimated using the ABC/2 formula or segmentation for irregular collections. The internal structure of the hematoma should be described using the Nakaguchi framework, which categorizes appearance as homogeneous, laminar, separated, or trabecular, with mixed features explicitly noted. Advanced imaging techniques such as dual-energy CT, MRI, and arterial spin labeling may provide information about membrane activity and biological maturation, but currently lack sufficient validation and remain limited to problem-solving rather than routine clinical use. Standardized reporting and prospective validation studies are needed before imaging characteristics can reliably guide treatment decisions for individual patients.
llm_summary_expert: The American Society of Functional Neuroradiology Clinical Practice Committee developed a state of practice statement through expert consensus and literature review to establish standardized imaging approaches for chronic subdural hematoma assessment. Noncontrast CT remains the primary imaging modality, with hematoma burden characterized by maximum thickness perpendicular to the inner table, midline shift, and volume estimation using the ABC/2 formula or segmentation for irregular collections. Internal architecture should be described using the Nakaguchi framework, which categorizes phenotypes as homogeneous, laminar, separated, and trabecular, with mixed or transitional features explicitly reported. Advanced imaging techniques including dual-energy CT, photon-counting CT, MRI, and arterial spin labeling may provide information regarding neomembrane activity but currently lack sufficient validation and have only a problem-solving rather than routine role. Standardized reporting and prospective validation are needed before imaging phenotype or advanced biomarkers can reliably guide treatment selection in chronic subdural hematoma management.

title: Clinicopathologic and Outcome Characteristics of Glomerulopathy With Striated Deposits: A Case Series.
abstract: Glomerulopathy with striated deposits (GSD) is a rare entity defined by ultrastructural deposits with striated substructure. Prior data were limited to case reports. This case series characterizes GSD's clinicopathologic spectrum and prognosis.Case series.Eighteen GSD cases identified from the nephropathology archives of Mayo Clinic and Columbia University, 2011-2025.Fifty percent of the patients were male, 78% were Caucasian, and their median age was 73 years. Most patients presented with CKD (median creatinine, 2.6 mg/dl), proteinuria (median, 3.8 g/day), and hematuria (80%), a minority (29%) with hypocomplementemia, and none with extrarenal manifestations. Fifteen (88%) patients had hematologic conditions, primarily (56%) monoclonal gammopathy of renal significance (MGRS). Histologically, most cases (67%) had a membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis pattern on biopsy. All exhibited striated ultrastructural deposits of regularly stacked straight electron-dense bands (13 nm in mean diameter) with distinctive periodicity (mean 20 nm), which were present mostly in subendothelial and mesangial regions. Ten (56%) cases exhibited monotypic Ig glomerular deposits (IgGκ in 7) on immunofluorescence (IF), which were masked in 6 (60%), requiring IF evaluation using pronase-digested paraffin tissue for unmasking. Six of these 10 patients (60%) had a circulating MIg whose isotype matched the deposited Igs. The remaining cases exhibited polytypic Ig glomerular deposits (4 cases) or had no detectable Ig (4 cases) identified histologically. After follow-up (median 14 months) in 15 patients, 6 (40%) progressed to kidney failure within a median of 11 months, including 1 with recurrence in a kidney allograft. Kidney response to clone-directed therapy was observed in all 4 evaluable patients.Retrospective design, small sample size.GSD is a rare heterogeneous glomerulopathy presenting in older patients with CKD and proteinuria, and frequently associated with hematologic conditions, particularly MGRS. We propose adding GSD with monotypic Ig deposits to the spectrum of MGRS lesions. Further studies are needed to elucidate precise deposit composition(s) and effective therapeutic approaches.Copyright © 2026 National Kidney Foundation, Inc. Published by Elsevier Inc. llm_summary: Glomerulopathy with striated deposits (GSD) is a rare kidney disease characterized by distinctive ultrastructural deposits that had previously been documented only through individual case reports, prompting researchers to systematically characterize its clinical features and outcomes. In this case series, researchers identified 18 GSD patients from nephropathology archives at Mayo Clinic and Columbia University between 2011 and 2025, finding that most were older adults (median age 73 years) who presented with chronic kidney disease, proteinuria (median 3.8 g/day), and hematuria, with 88% having associated hematologic conditions, particularly monoclonal gammopathy of renal significance. The kidney biopsies showed characteristic regularly stacked electron-dense bands with 13 nanometer mean diameter and 20 nanometer periodicity in subendothelial and mesangial regions, with 56% of cases displaying monotypic immunoglobulin deposits that were sometimes masked and required special tissue preparation to detect. During median follow-up of 14 months, 40% of the 15 evaluable patients progressed to kidney failure within a median.

title: An improved protocol to isolate enriched immune cells from murine intestinal epithelium and lamina propria.
abstract: The intestine is home to more immune cells than any other non-lymphatic peripheral tissue, but research of these cells is stymied by the technical difficulties involved in isolating them. Here, we describe a protocol to isolate highly viable immune cells from murine intestinal epithelium and lamina propria. This protocol can be used to characterize cells by flow cytometry or single-cell transcriptomics, as in Crotts et al., or by other analysis methods.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). llm_summary: The intestine contains a higher concentration of immune cells than most other peripheral tissues, yet isolating these cells for research has presented significant technical challenges. Crotts and Shapiro developed an improved protocol to extract viable immune cells from both the intestinal epithelium and lamina propria (the tissue layer beneath the intestinal lining) in mice. The protocol enables researchers to obtain enriched populations of immune cells suitable for detailed analysis. These isolated cells can be characterized using flow cytometry, which identifies cell types by their surface markers, or single-cell transcriptomics, which measures gene expression in individual cells, as demonstrated in the authors' related work. This method provides a practical tool for studying intestinal immune cells through multiple analytical approaches.
llm_summary_expert: Crotts and Shapiro describe an improved protocol for isolating enriched immune cells from murine intestinal epithelium and lamina propria, tissues containing more immune cells than other non-lymphatic peripheral tissues. The protocol yields highly viable immune cells suitable for characterization by flow cytometry, single-cell transcriptomics, or other analysis methods. The authors developed this approach to address technical difficulties that have previously hindered research on intestinal immune populations. The protocol enables comprehensive immunological profiling of these anatomically distinct intestinal compartments. The abstract does not report specific quantitative efficacy measures or comparative data against alternative isolation methods.

title: The Job Demands-Resources model: a framework for fostering trainee engagement on the inpatient wards.
abstract: The inpatient ward is a cornerstone of medical training but is increasingly strained by high levels of trainee burnout and withering educational engagement. The Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) model offers a useful framework for understanding these challenges. The model categorizes aspects of work as either demands or resources and describes how mismatches between the two can lead to exhaustion and impaired performance, while the right balance (high demands with commensurate resources) promotes work engagement and professional growth. Although widely used in other work settings, the JD-R model has seen limited application in medical education. This perspective describes the JD-R model and illustrates how it can be applied to evaluate educational practices on the inpatient wards. These practices can function either as demands or as resources depending on how they are implemented. A day-in-the-life vignette illustrates the application of the JD-R model, highlighting opportunities for attending physicians and program leaders to shape the work environment in ways that promote demand-resource balance and foster trainee engagement and learning on the inpatient wards.© The Author(s) 2026. title: Matrix metalloproteinase-guided targeting of vesicular stomatitis virus to tumors following systemic administration.
abstract: The lack of tumor-specific targeting by oncolytic viruses (OVs) restricts their therapeutic potential. Here, we report a "cap-linker" strategy to modify the vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV) glycoprotein (G protein, VSV-GIN). The modified VSV (Pro-VSVIN) loses its ability to infect cells until present in the tumor microenvironment, where the linker is cleaved by tumor-enriched matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs). When Pro-VSVIN is armed with a single-chain IL-12 (Pro-VSVIN-IL-12) and systemically injected into MC38 tumor-bearing mice, Pro-VSVIN-IL-12 eradicates established tumors while avoiding systemic toxicity, and elicits long-term anti-tumor immune memory. Systemic administration of Pro-VSVIN-IL-12 also markedly inhibits the growth of metastatic cancers in the lung. The efficacy of Pro-VSVIN-IL-12 was further improved when combined with PD-1 checkpoint blockade. title: Reverse genetics and comparative pathogenesis of Lone Star virus.
abstract: Lone Star virus (LSV) is a bandavirus first isolated from Amblyomma americanum ticks in the United States and is phylogenetically related to severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV), Heartland virus (HRTV), and Bhanja virus, each of which has been associated with severe human disease. In contrast to these better-characterized bandaviruses, LSV remains poorly studied, and its pathogenic potential is not well defined. The recent detection of LSV RNA in the cerebrospinal fluid of an immunocompromised patient in Idaho, U.S., with fatal meningoencephalitis further highlights the need for experimental systems to investigate LSV biology. Here, we rescued recombinant LSV (rLSV) from cloned complementary DNA (cDNA) plasmids and characterized the virus. rLSV replicated similarly to the parental LSV isolate in mammalian cells and caused rapid, systemic, and lethal disease in IFNAR-/- mice, with widespread detection of viral RNA (vRNA) across multiple tissues, hepatic and splenic pathology, and induction of inflammatory cytokines. In contrast, C57BL/6J mice controlled infection and exhibited no clinical disease. To place LSV within a broader comparative framework, we generated rSFTSV from cloned cDNA and compared rLSV, rSFTSV, and HRTV in cell culture and IFNAR-/- mice. Our studies revealed distinct disease kinetics among these related tick-borne bandaviruses and showed that HRTV-induced immunity protected against homologous HRTV rechallenge and heterologous rSFTSV challenge, but not rLSV challenge. Together, these findings establish reverse-genetics platforms and small-animal models for comparative bandavirus studies, define key features of LSV pathogenesis, and place this neglected virus within a framework of related bandaviruses that differ in virulence and immunological overlap.IMPORTANCETick-borne bandaviruses include several viruses associated with severe human disease, yet many related viruses remain poorly characterized. Lone Star virus (LSV) was first isolated from Amblyomma americanum ticks decades ago, but experimental tools and animal models to study LSV infection have been lacking. Here, we generated a recombinant LSV and used it to define the outcome of infection in immunocompromised and immunocompetent mice. We show that LSV can cause rapid, systemic, and lethal disease when type I interferon signaling is absent, whereas immunocompetent mice restrict infection and remain clinically normal. By comparing LSV with Heartland virus and severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus, we also show that related tick-borne bandaviruses differ in disease kinetics and immune protection. These findings provide foundational tools for studying LSV and highlight the importance of experimentally characterizing neglected tick-borne viruses before their pathogenic potential is fully understood.

title: Mapping human genetic associations to drug targets in valvular heart disease: an integrative evidence synthesis.
abstract: Valvular heart disease (VHD) lacks disease-modifying pharmacological therapies. Drug repurposing guided by human genetics may help identify therapeutic opportunities. We aimed to integrate human genetic associations, drug-target information, and clinical evidence to identify repurposing opportunities and prioritise potentially druggable targets across the VHD spectrum.We retrieved VHD-associated genetic variants from the NHGRI-EBI Genome-Wide Association Studies Catalogue and Ensembl, interrogated annotated genes in the Open Targets Platform, and evaluated linked drugs through structured searches of MEDLINE and ClinicalTrials.gov. The study protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251071741).We identified 1464 genetic associations corresponding to 844 unique variants and 582 candidate genes. Of these genes, 431 had tractability information and 51 had linked compounds, comprising 388 distinct pharmacological agents, 273 in phase 3 or 4 of clinical development. Drug-linked targets were concentrated in aortic stenosis. Clinical evidence supported therapeutic potential for 14 drugs, with preclinical or mechanistic cardiovascular support for eight additional drugs and adverse cardiovascular signals for four. An exploratory evidence-weighted framework prioritised targets according to genetic-functional evidence, tissue and mechanistic context, and translational tractability.This genetics-informed evidence synthesis identifies drug-repurposing opportunities and a substantial gap between genetically supported targets and available therapies. title: Analyzing the Economic and Logistical Impact of Lung Procurement on Transplant Centers in the Era of Continuous Distribution.
abstract: The recent transition to the Composite Allocation Score (CAS) has increased travel distances for lung transplants, but an associated cost analysis has not been performed. We assessed travel costs and short-term outcomes of lung transplantation before and after transitioning to CAS.The United Network for Organ Sharing database was queried for all lung transplants from 1/2020 to 12/2024. Redo and pediatric lung and multiorgan transplants were excluded. Patients were stratified between pre- and post-CAS, which began on 3/9/2023. Outcomes were distance of donor-to-recipient in nautical miles (nm), inflation-adjusted travel costs, and perioperative outcomes.A total of 7,835 (58.6%) pre-CAS and 5,538 (41.4%) post-CAS patients were included. Post-CAS patients were more likely female (41.7% vs. 38.5%, p<0.001), less likely White race (69.1% vs. 72.7%, p<0.001), and had shorter waitlist durations (28 vs. 33 days, p<0.001) compared to pre-CAS patients. Donor lungs were procured from greater distances in the CAS era (411 vs. 185 nm, p<0.001). Post-CAS, more procurements required flights (80.8% vs. 68.6%, p<0.001), and very long-distance procurements (>1000 nm) increased (10.7% vs. 2.0%, p<0.001). Travel costs increased, with median inflation-adjusted costs rising from $13,967 to $16,818; p<0.001. Ischemic times were longer post-CAS (7.1 vs. 5.7 hours, p<0.001). Importantly, one-year survival was similar pre- and post-CAS (88.9% vs. 90.1%, p=0.069).CAS has reduced waitlist duration with preserved one-year survival for lung transplant patients, but introduces greater logistical complexity and cost, which requires continued reevaluation to ensure economic viability and long-term sustainability of transplant programs.Copyright © 2026 The American Association for Thoracic Surgery. title: Radiation Protection Modernization in the United States: Stakeholder Perspectives on the US NRC's Proposed Rulemaking.
abstract: On 15 July 2026, the Health Physics Society (HPS), National Council on Radiation Protection and Measurements (NCRP), American Academy of Health Physics (AAHP), American Association of Physicists in Medicine (AAPM), and Conference of Radiation Control Program Directors (CRCPD) convened an open-forum webinar concerning the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission (US NRC) proposed rule, "Reforming and Modernizing the NRC's Radiation Protection Framework" (RIN 3150-AL47). More than 800 individuals attended. Moderators summarized the proposed rule, facilitated open discussion, and administered live polling; participation in single-response poll questions ranged from 213 to 404 respondents. Poll respondents expressed qualified support for modernization in principle, and forum participants raised substantial concerns about the absence of cross-agency and international harmonization, burdens placed on Agreement States, the lack of infrastructure for tracking occupational dose across licensees, potential effects on medical and x-ray practice, and reliance on implementing guidance that had not been released. In polling, 60% (153/253) of respondents strongly supported or supported the graded approach in concept. Eighty-eight percent (202/229) considered consistency between the US NRC and Agreement State regulations very or extremely important. Seventy-six percent (184/241) indicated that the proposed rule provided only partial or insufficient information for determining required program changes. Open-ended responses most often called for additional low-dose research, clearer implementing guidance, regulatory harmonization, and resolution of specific technical and operational questions. These findings describe the perspectives of a self-selected forum audience and should not be interpreted as representative of the entire radiation protection community. Overall, the forum reflected qualified support for modernization, coupled with an emphasis that its practical effect will depend on guidance, transition planning, harmonization, and dose-tracking infrastructure.Copyright © 2026 Health Physics Society.

title: Tau A152T risk variant drives distinct cell type transcriptional signatures in AD and PSP.
abstract: The A152T point mutation is a rare genetic variant in the tau gene (MAPT) that is linked to risk of Alzheimer's disease (AD) and frontotemporal dementia spectrum disorders, including progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) and corticobasal degeneration (CBD). To uncover mechanisms through which the A152T variant contributes to risk of tauopathy, we performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) on postmortem brain tissue collected from A152T carriers and pathology-matched non-carriers with either AD or PSP, along with age-matched controls. These efforts revealed that despite similar cell type composition across groups, A152T carriers exhibited distinct cell type-specific transcriptional changes in both AD and PSP. Differential expression analysis identified excitatory neurons, oligodendrocytes, and astrocytes as the most affected cell populations in AD and PSP, and these same cell types showed the strongest A152T-specific changes. These findings identify transcriptional alterations that differentiate sporadic AD and sporadic PSP from AD-A152T and PSP-A152T, as well as shared molecular signatures unique to A152T carriers in both PSP and AD. Donor-level pseudo-bulk analyses showed broad directional support with the single-nucleus findings although the proportion of donor-supported genes varied across cell type and comparison. Importantly, merging sporadic and A152T cases into a single disease group was found to mask transcriptional differences in several cell types in both AD and PSP, indicating divergence in transcriptional signature and highlighting the importance of screening for genetic risk variants like A152T in snRNA-seq data from human cohorts.© 2026. title: Chemokine receptor CXCR2 and plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 expression in colorectal adenocarcinoma are associated with prognostic features.
abstract: Chemokine receptor CXCR2 and plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (PAI-1) are incipient biomarkers across various cancers. title: Functional stratification of YWHAZ variants explains distinct neurodevelopmental disorders.
abstract: The application of clinical genomics in personalized medical practice increasingly reveals that variants from single loci can lead to phenotypic heterogeneity. This necessitates functional characterization and classification of serial variants to correlate their associated clinical features and molecular properties. Recently, a few putative pathogenic variants in YWHAZ, encoding the 14-3-3ζ protein, have been implicated in clinically variable isolated and syndromic neurodevelopmental phenotypes, based on a few reported affected individuals, but the molecular basis of this heterogeneity has remained unclear. Here, we assembled a large cohort of individuals harboring de novo YWHAZ variants and categorized their clinical stratification into distinct neurodevelopmental conditions, including a typical presentation of cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome and a developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with sleep disorders. By integrating structural analyses, molecular dynamics simulations, in vitro biochemical and cell-based signaling studies, unbiased proteomics analysis, and in vivo phenotypic assays, we define distinct functional classes of pathogenic YWHAZ variants and establish robust genotype-phenotype correlations. We show that disease-associated YWHAZ variants differentially perturb 14-3-3ζ function by variably affecting protein abundance and binding to interacting partners, including the BRAF and RAF1 kinases. Notably, the recurrent p.Ser230Trp (c.689C>G) variant uniquely underlying cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome specifically enhances MAPK signaling, whereas other variants do not significantly impact signal flow through the cascade under the used experimental conditions. title: Intraocular Pressure Following Phacoemulsification with Anterior Vitrectomy in the IRIS® Registry (Intelligent Research in Sight).
abstract: To evaluate intraocular pressure (IOP) changes following phacoemulsification with concurrent anterior vitrectomy (AV) using the IRIS® Registry (Intelligent Research in Sight).Retrospective clinical cohort study SUBJECTS: Eyes in the IRIS Registry that underwent stand-alone phacoemulsification with concurrent AV from 1/1/2013-9/30/2019.Daily mean IOP was compared to baseline IOP through postoperative day 90. An IOP spike was defined as IOP >30 mm Hg and an increase of >10 mm Hg from baseline IOP within the first postoperative week. A linear mixed-effects model was used to determine when the postoperative daily mean IOP stabilized; the final mean IOP was the average of all daily mean IOPs from that timepoint onward. A multivariable logistic regression analysis was used to identify independent risk factors and odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals for an IOP spike.Postoperative daily mean IOP; incidence and OR of IOP spike RESULTS: Phacoemulsification with AV occurred in 1,811 eyes with a baseline median (interquartile range) IOP of 16.0 (14.0,18.0) mmHg. An IOP spike was observed in 164 (9.1%) eyes. After surgery, daily median IOP for all eyes was elevated to 18.0 (14.0, 23.0) mmHg and generally remained significantly elevated above baseline through postoperative week two. Risk factors for all eyes to have an IOP spike were glaucoma diagnosis (OR 1.71 (1.17-2.5), P=0.005), male sex (OR 1.64 (1.15-2.37), P=0.007), and baseline logMAR visual acuity (OR=1.07 (1.01-1.13) per 0.2 logMAR unit increase, P=0.02). In eyes with glaucoma, risk factors for IOP spike included male sex (OR 2.36 (1.32-4.32), P=0.004), increased age (OR 1.45 (1.08-1.97) per ten years, P=0.02), and Hispanic ethnicity compared to non-Hispanic White patients (OR 2.30 (1.07-4.80), P=0.03). In eyes without glaucoma, only baseline visual acuity was a risk factor (OR 1.09 (1.00-1.18) per 0.2 logMAR unit increase, P=0.04).Ophthalmologists can anticipate a postoperative IOP elevation with resolution to baseline IOP by postoperative week two, but IOP is unlikely to decline below baseline, when AV is required during phacoemulsification. title: Characterization of IgA, IgA immune complexes and complement depositions in IgA nephropathy using laser microdissection and mass spectrometry.
abstract: IgA nephropathy is characterized by accumulation of mesangial IgA immune complexes. These IgA immune complexes result in glomerular inflammation and subsequent sclerosis. Glomerular inflammation is mediated in part by activation of the complement pathway by these immune complexes.In this study of 22 cases of IgA nephropathy, using laser microdissection and mass spectrometry (LMD/MS), we characterized both IgA and complement deposits.LMD/MS detected abundant IgA1 but also IgA2; detected in 100% and 82% of cases, respectively. Furthermore, J chains, that link IgA monomers to form dimeric IgA on mucosal surfaces, was detected in 91% of cases, while the polymeric Ig receptor found in secretory IgA was found in only 9% of the cases. IgG1 was the dominant IgG subclass and was detected in 100% of cases. IgG subclass staining and confocal immunofluorescence microscopy confirmed the IgG1 subclass and colocalization of IgG1 with IgA1 and IgA2.Evaluation of the complement pathways revealed abundant C3, C9, C5, C6, C7 and C8 with lesser amounts of C4 indicating activation of predominantly the alternative and terminal pathways of complement. LMD/MS also detected abundant complement regulating proteins including CFH, CFHR1, CFHR2 and CFHR5, CD59, and smaller amounts of CFB, indicating active regulation of the complement pathways. Although it did not reach statistical significance, high counts of C3, C5 and C9 were present in lesions with endocapillary hypercellularity/crescentic lesions. High counts of complement regulating proteins, particularly CFHR5, were also present in active lesions. C3 sequence coverage data showed the majority of amino acids detected belong to C3dg along with smaller amounts of C3c.Our data shows that the IgA immune complexes are composed of mucosal-derived dimeric IgA1/IgA2 and IgG1. title: F-Wave-Induced Repetitive Discharges: Expanding the Spectrum of Stimulus-Induced Repetitive Discharges.
abstract: The clinical significance of stereotyped post-F-wave discharges remains uncertain. We aimed to characterize F-wave-induced repetitive discharges (FIRDs) and their associated clinical and electrodiagnostic findings.We searched the Mayo Clinic electrodiagnostic database (January 1997-December 2025) using "F-wave" and "repetitive discharges" and reviewed retrieved waveforms. FIRDs were defined by repetitive discharges following F-wave activation, reproducible morphology within a train, and regular or semiregular firing.The study included 20 patients with FIRDs (median age 61 years, range 21-83 years; 10 male). Routine motor conduction attributes were normal in 90% of patients and F-wave latencies were normal in all. FIRDs consisted of brief, reproducible discharges with a regular or semi-regular firing pattern, individual durations of 2-10 ms, firing frequencies of 100-500 Hz, and amplitudes of 120-1000 μV. Neurogenic abnormalities on needle electromyography were seen in the distribution of the FIRD nerve in 65%. FIRDs were transient in a subset of patients who had repeat studies (5/5). Clinical and electrophysiological diagnoses included peripheral neuropathy (30%), radiculopathy (25%), polio (5%), brachial plexopathy (5%), and chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy (5%). Six patients (30%) had no clinical or electrophysiological evidence of a neuromuscular disorder.FIRDs represent an uncommon electrophysiological phenomenon seen in both chronic neurogenic disorders and patients without neurologic disease. Recognition may aid waveform interpretation, but their presence alone does not establish a specific neuromuscular diagnosis.© 2026 Wiley Periodicals LLC.

abstract: Evaluate the relationship between metabolic syndrome (MetS) and clinical outcomes in individuals with necrotizing pancreatitis (NP) and infected pancreatic necrosis (IPN).MetS affects a significant proportion of the global population and is associated with low-grade systemic inflammation and immune dysregulation. This has implications for several disease processes, but the impact of MetS on patients with NP is not well characterized.A retrospective cohort study of patients admitted with NP at a single tertiary center was performed. MetS was defined as meeting any 3 of the following criteria: BMI ≥30 kg/m2, triglycerides ≥150 mg/dL, fasting glucose ≥110 mg/dL, blood pressure ≥130/85 mm Hg, and low HDL (<40 mg/dL men, <50 mg/dL women). The need for intensive care, hospital length of stay, development of organ failure, and mortality were compared in patients with NP with or without MetS. title: Contemporary Survey of the Impact of Perioperative Catastrophes on Anesthesiologists.
abstract: Perioperative catastrophes are sentinel events in anesthesiology with well-described emotional and professional consequences. A landmark national survey published in 2012 demonstrated substantial and prolonged distress among anesthesiologists after such events. Since 2012, anesthesiology practice has evolved within a healthcare environment characterized by persistent workforce strain, heightened attention to clinician well-being, and expansion of peer support programs. A contemporary reassessment is warranted.A voluntary, anonymous electronic survey was distributed in 2025 to U.S.-based members of the American Society of Anesthesiologists (Schaumburg, Illinois) who had opted to receive research surveys. The 44-item instrument was adapted from the 2012 questionnaire to preserve longitudinal comparability while incorporating contemporary support modalities. Domains included experience with perioperative catastrophes, characteristics of a memorable event, emotional and physical sequelae, impact on clinical performance, recovery trajectories, and perceptions of institutional support. Descriptive analyses were performed.Of 1,725 respondents included in analysis (response rate, 7.1%), 94.2% reported involvement in at least one perioperative catastrophe during their careers. After a memorable event, 72.5% reported physical symptoms, and 91.6% reported psychosocial symptoms. Most respondents perceived impairment in ability to provide anesthesia care in the first 4 h (69.0%) and 24 h (61.5%) after the event. Nearly one fifth (19.7%) reported never fully recovering emotionally, closely mirroring rates reported in 2012. Although informal peer support was common, formal debriefing and institutionally supported time off were infrequently provided. Nearly one quarter of respondents reported considering leaving anesthesiology as a result of a perioperative catastrophe.Perioperative catastrophes remain a common experience in anesthesiology and continue to carry substantial and enduring consequences. Despite increased cultural awareness, there remains a gap between recognition of their impact and clinicians' reported recovery experiences. Routine integration of peer support, nonpunitive debriefing, and flexible duty relief may represent critical opportunities to improve clinician well-being, patient safety, and workforce sustainability.Copyright © 2026 American Society of Anesthesiologists. title: Infarcted Tenosynovial Giant Cell Tumors: Multi-Institutional Analysis of 80 Cases Highlighting Consultation Patterns and Diagnostic Challenges.
abstract: Tenosynovial giant cell tumor (TGCT) is a benign neoplasm of synoviocytic differentiation composed of variable proportions of neoplastic mononuclear cells (synoviocytes) and non-neoplastic multinucleated giant cells, foamy macrophages, siderophages, lymphocytes, plasma cells, and hemosiderin deposits. Although TGCT is usually readily diagnosed histologically, it may exhibit limited or extensive infarct-type necrosis that obscures diagnostic features and raises concern for malignancy. To better characterize this phenomenon, we analyzed TGCTs with infarct-type necrosis in a multi-institutional cohort. The authors' institutional and consultation archives were searched for TGCT with infarct-type necrosis. All available slides were re-reviewed, and clinicoradiologic data, including contributor-provided suggested diagnoses, were recorded. Eighty cases were identified (42 females, 38 males) with a mean age of 36 years (range: 8 - 81). Tumor sites included knee (55; 69%), hands/feet (15; 19%), hip (9; 11%), and infratemporal region (1; 1%). Mean tumor size was 2.9 cm (range: 0.7- 8.3 cm). Preoperative clinical or radiologic impressions were available in 64 cases (80%): TGCT was suspected in 41 (64%), a non-neoplastic process in 16 (25%), and 7 were non-specific masses (11%). More than half of the cases (53%) were pathologist-driven consultations, and contributor-suggested diagnoses were provided in 29 instances; nearly all (26/29; 90%) reflected uncertainty related to the presence of necrosis, including at least 4 cases in which malignant TGCT was considered. Most tumors (65; 81%) showed >50% necrosis, and 30 cases (38%) demonstrated complete or near-complete necrosis (>95%). Ancillary studies were performed in 14 cases (18%). Neoplastic synoviocytes expressed CSF1 mRNA and clusterin, rarely were desmin-positive, and demonstrated a characteristic peripheral rim of hemosiderin with histochemical iron stains. CD68 and CD163 immunostains identified background histiocytes. Follow-up data was available for 32 patients (40%; mean: 48 months; range: 4-185 months); all were without evidence of disease following surgical excision. We conclude that TGCT may exhibit extensive infarct-type necrosis and thereby mimic a non-neoplastic process or sarcoma; awareness of this phenomenon, along with clinical and radiologic correlation, should facilitate accurate diagnosis.Copyright © 2026. title: The Association of Social Drivers of Health and Neonatal Intensive Care Unit Discharge Delays in Children with Tracheostomy in a Single Center in Rural Minnesota.
abstract: Introduction:As neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) survival improves, the number of children with tracheostomy, along with those who require home care nursing (HCN), is rising. Discharge delays (DD) are an issue, with an emotional or financial toll on children, families, and the health care system. We aimed to investigate whether social drivers of health like socioeconomic status (SES), race, sex, and medical factors such as gestational age influenced DD for children with tracheostomy.Materials and Methods:We conducted a retrospective chart review of children who underwent tracheostomy in the NICU during a 5-year period. Four authors reviewed electronic medical records for demographics, clinical information, and DD. SES was determined based on the HOUsing-based SocioEconomic Status (HOUSES) index. The Kruskal-Wallis test and Spearman's correlation were used to assess the association between DD in days and independent variables. In addition, the cohort was divided into 2 groups based on DD ≥30 days to explore factors associated with it descriptively.Results:Sixteen children were included in the study (10 female, 6 male). Ten children were identified as White, and 3 as Black. Three children were not White or Black. Only one child did not experience DD. Median DD was 15 days (interquartile range [IQR]: 13-24; range 0-49). Three children had clinically significant DD (>30 days). The most common cause of DD was waiting for HCN (10/16, 63%, P = 0.065). Race (White versus Black versus other) was associated with DD (P = 0.045). Female sex (P = 0.039) was associated with significant DD, while birthweight (P = 0.19) and HOUSES index (P = 0.49) were not.Conclusion:DD is a common phenomenon in children with tracheostomy in the NICU, and lack of HCN is the major factor. Race and sex may play a role in DD. HCN shortages and other causes of DD should be further studied and addressed.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether social and medical factors influenced discharge delays for children with tracheostomies in a neonatal intensive care unit, as delays can burden families and the healthcare system. In a retrospective review of 16 children over five years, they analyzed demographics, clinical information, and days until discharge, using statistical tests to assess associations with factors including race, sex, socioeconomic status, and gestational age. The median discharge delay was 15 days, with 15 of 16 children experiencing some delay, and the most common reason was waiting for home care nursing (10 of 16 cases). Race was statistically associated with discharge delays (P = 0.045), and female sex was associated with clinically significant delays greater than 30 days (P = 0.039), while socioeconomic status and birthweight showed no significant association. The findings suggest that home care nursing shortages and potential disparities related to race and sex warrant further investigation to reduce discharge delays for this vulnerable population.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers conducted a retrospective chart review of 16 children (10 female, 6 male) who underwent tracheostomy in the neonatal intensive care unit over a 5-year period at a single rural Minnesota center to investigate whether social drivers of health and medical factors were associated with discharge delays. The median discharge delay was 15 days (interquartile range 13–24 days; range 0–49 days), with waiting for home care nursing accounting for the most common cause in 10 of 16 children (63%, P = 0.065). Race was associated with discharge delay (P = 0.045), and female sex was associated with significant discharge delay greater than 30 days (P = 0.039), while birthweight (P = 0.19) and socioeconomic status measured by the HOUSES index (P = 0.49) were not. Discharge delays were nearly universal in this cohort, with only one child experiencing no delay.

title: EGFRvIII overexpression and loss of mouse-specific CDKN2A in glial cells leads to spontaneous gliomagenesis in a novel mouse model.
abstract: Glioblastoma is the most common primary brain cancer in adults, with a poor prognosis and median survival of 15 months after treatment. Few in vivo transgenic models exist for testing new therapeutics.A novel mouse model for the classical subtype of human glioblastoma (GBM) has been bred using Cre-mediated EGFRvIII overexpression and homozygous p19-ARF deletion, the mouse homolog of human p14ARF/CDKN2A, in GFAP-expressing cells.Transgenic mice developed intraparenchymal and/or leptomeningeal brain lesions as early as 1 month old and 95% of mice succumb to endpoint symptoms of hydrocephalus and/or paralysis by 6 months. Immunohistochemical analysis confirms EGFRvIII overexpression and p19-ARF loss in Cre-expressing cells, along with patchy positive GFAP and high proliferation by Ki67 as well as loss of H3K27me3. Bulk and single cell RNA sequencing revealed tumors cluster closely with classical GBM and have significant upregulation of downstream markers in the JAK/STAT and P13K/AKT pathways as well as intratumoral heterogeneity. Dissociated tumors generated xenograft tumors by 3 weeks post intracranial injections into NOD-SCID mice and were characteristic of the primary lesion.We developed a spontaneous, immune-competent murine glioma model that enables characterization of tumor development within an intact immune microenvironment and provides a resource for future mechanistic studies.© The Author(s) 2026. llm_summary: Researchers developed a novel transgenic mouse model to study glioblastoma, the most common primary brain cancer in adults, by engineering glial cells to overexpress EGFRvIII and lose p19-ARF (the mouse equivalent of the human CDKN2A tumor suppressor). Transgenic mice spontaneously developed brain tumors as early as one month of age, with 95% of mice reaching endpoint symptoms of hydrocephalus or paralysis by six months. Molecular analysis confirmed that tumors displayed classical glioblastoma characteristics, including EGFRvIII overexpression, activation of JAK/STAT and PI3K/AKT signaling pathways, and genetic features consistent with human glioblastoma subtypes. Tumor cells dissociated from primary lesions successfully generated xenograft tumors in immunocompromised mice within three weeks, demonstrating the tumors' ability to propagate in vivo. This spontaneous, immune-competent model enables researchers to study glioblastoma development within an intact immune microenvironment and provides a resource for testing new therapeutic approaches.

This immune-competent model enables characterization of tumor development within an intact immune microenvironment for mechanistic studies.

title: Etiology-specific spectrum of epilepsy syndromes (ESSES): Widening the concept of etiology-specific epilepsies-Report from the ILAE 2021-2025 Terminology Commission.
abstract: A new type of epilepsy syndrome, an etiology-specific epilepsy syndrome, was defined in 2022 in recognition of major advances in identifying the many genetic and acquired etiologies underlying the epilepsies. An etiology-specific epilepsy syndrome refers to where a known etiology is associated with a distinctive epilepsy presentation, including age at seizure onset, seizure types, and other morbidities, such as learning difficulties or intellectual disability, psychiatric features, gut and musculoskeletal problems. However, as we understand more about a specific etiology, such as a gene, it is clear that many etiologies are associated not just with one epilepsy syndrome, but with a range of epilepsy syndromes. Different epilepsy syndromes due to an abnormality in the same gene may reflect different types of dysfunction caused by the specific pathogenic genetic variant. Here, we expand the concept because-knowing the genetic etiology is not enough to ensure optimal clinical care-it requires a more nuanced approach to ensure the patient is managed appropriately. We define the concept of an etiology-specific spectrum of epilepsy syndromes (ESSES), which incorporates understanding the range of epilepsy syndromes that may be associated with a specific etiology. In some cases, a genetic etiology may be associated with a functional spectrum, such as pathogenic variants in an ion channel subunit that cause loss-of-function, gain-of-function, or mixed functional effects, each associated with specific epilepsy syndromes that may require different treatment approaches. With other genes, the functional effect may not yet be known, but their spectrum of epilepsy syndromes may be well established through genotype-phenotype studies. The concept of ESSES has the flexibility to grow in its scope with new insights gained from understanding the breadth of epilepsy syndromes associated with a specific etiology and the associated functional impact.© 2026 The Author(s). llm_summary: The International League Against Epilepsy Terminology Commission expanded the classification of epilepsy syndromes to better reflect advances in understanding genetic and acquired causes of epilepsy. The researchers introduced the concept of etiology-specific spectrum of epilepsy syndromes (ESSES), which recognizes that a single genetic cause can produce multiple different epilepsy syndromes rather than just one, depending on the specific type of genetic variant and its functional effects. This framework acknowledges that different pathogenic variants in the same gene may cause loss-of-function, gain-of-function, or mixed effects, each associated with distinct epilepsy presentations that may require different treatment approaches. Understanding this spectrum is clinically important because knowing only the genetic etiology is insufficient for optimal patient management without also considering which specific epilepsy syndrome is present. The ESSES concept is designed to evolve as new genotype-phenotype studies provide deeper insights into the range of epilepsy syndromes associated with specific etiologies and their underlying functional mechanisms.

The ESSES concept provides flexibility to accommodate expanding knowledge of genotype-phenotype relationships and functional mechanisms underlying epilepsy syndromes.

title: Transradial Intracranial Aneurysm Embolization Using a 7F Sheath-Compatible 0.087-Inch Guide Catheter: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
abstract: Transradial intracranial aneurysm embolization is well established, but experience with large-bore 7F sheath-based guide platforms remains comparatively limited. We evaluated the technical feasibility and periprocedural outcomes of a 7F sheath-compatible 0.087inch guide catheter for transradial intracranial aneurysm embolization.In this single-arm, noncomparative retrospective study, we reviewed consecutive patients who underwent attempted transradial intracranial aneurysm embolization using the NeuGlide as the primary guide catheter at a single center between January 2025 and May 2026. Preaccess radial ultrasonography was performed in all patients, and radial diameter ≥1.7 mm was required for 7F access. The primary outcome was completion of the intended treatment through radial access without femoral conversion.Target-vessel catheterization was achieved in 71/74 procedures (95.9%), and radial procedural completion in 69/74 (93.2%; 95% confidence interval, 85.1-97.1%). Three procedures required femoral conversion, and 2 were terminated without aneurysm treatment; overall treatment completion was 72/74 (97.3%). Guide instability occurred in 2 procedures: 1 repositioning-only event and 1 event resulting in femoral conversion; no guide exchanges occurred. Seven patients had 9 access-site component events, all managed conservatively; all 6 hematomas were low-grade (EASY I-II). Radial artery occlusion was identified in 1/15 patients formally assessed.In this radial-first cohort, the 7F sheath-compatible 0.087-inch NeuGlide guide catheter achieved a 93.2% radial procedural completion rate across multiple intracranial aneurysm treatment strategies. These findings support the NeuGlide as a technically feasible and versatile large-bore transradial platform in appropriately selected patients.

title: Does Route of Administration Affect the Outcome of Retinal Gene Therapy Clinical Trials?
abstract: Luxturna® (voretigene neparvovec-rzyl) for RPE65-associated retinal dystrophy was the first FDA-approved in vivo gene therapy and, 9 years later, remains the only approved retinal gene therapy. A search of clinicaltrials.gov identified 80 interventional phase 1-3 U.S. studies using AAV vectors, 45 using subretinal injection (SRI), and 33 using intravitreal injection (IVT). SRI efficiently transduces photoreceptors and RPE but transduces only the detached retinal area and carries procedure-related risks. IVT provides broader exposure and avoids retinal detachment but has shown limited efficacy for retinal targets and may produce dose-dependent inflammation. Overall, 11.6% of eyes in peer-reviewed publications receiving gene therapy via SRI experienced serious adverse events (SAEs); and in some studies, 100% experienced treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs). The gap between an active clinical pipeline and regulatory success raises the question: how does route of administration interact with therapeutic biology and clinical trial design? X-linked retinitis pigmentosa (XLRP) due to RPGR variants illustrates this challenge. Nine of 10 trials treating RPGR-related XLRP used SRI, with microperimetry and low light visual acuity as efficacy endpoints; 2 completed phase 2/3 studies failed to meet their primary endpoints. The XOLARIS XLRP natural history study suggests that other measures (e.g., visual field loss, central ellipsoid zone width) may better capture progression. Thus, retinal gene therapy clinical trial design must match the route of administration to the cellular target, therapeutic mechanism, and disease distribution. Emerging vectors and delivery strategies that expand retinal coverage while reducing procedural injury are critical to improve the likelihood of successful retinal gene therapy trials.

title: State Medical Board Disciplinary Actions Related to Medical Knowledge Deficits.
abstract: The proportion of state medical board disciplinary actions taken due to medical knowledge deficits is not known. We measured the percentage of disciplinary actions with medical knowledge deficits and the association between disciplinary actions and board certification exam performance, among American Board of Internal Medicine (ABIM) physicians in California.We investigated all physicians in California with an ABIM identification number who were disciplined from January 1, 2011 to December 31, 2022. We reviewed disciplinary documentation on California's medical board website for each physician and determined through a systematic process whether actions had to do with a medical knowledge deficit. We also examined the association between these disciplinary actions and whether a physician failed on their first certification exam attempt using a chi-squared analysis.Among the 558 California disciplinary actions from 2011 to 2022, 52.3% were related to a medical knowledge deficit. In addition, 43.7% were not related to medical knowledge, and 3.9% had an 'Ambiguous' classification. Physicians who had a disciplinary action associated with a medical knowledge deficit were less likely to have passed the initial certification exam on the first attempt (chi-square=3.90, P = .048).About half of the disciplinary actions received by physicians in California with an ABIM identification number were related to medical knowledge deficits and these types of disciplinary actions were more likely among physicians who failed to pass the ABIM certification exam on the first attempt compared with those who passed. Since medical knowledge can potentially be improved, this finding allows for the possibility of a reduction in future disciplinary actions.Copyright © 2026 The Alliance for Continuing Education in the Health Professions, the Association for Hospital Medical Education, and the Society for Academic Continuing Medical Education.

title: Effect of Activin Type II Receptor Signaling in Patients With HFpEF and Pulmonary Hypertension: A Critical Analysis of Biological Mechanisms and Clinical Trials.
abstract: The totality of evidence indicates that the mechanisms underlying the increase in pulmonary vascular resistance in patients with combined postcapillary and precapillary pulmonary hypertension (CpcPH) associated with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) differ meaningfully from those responsible for the increase in pulmonary vascular resistance in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension. CpcPH-HFpEF is a complex disorder involving the pulmonary veins, left atrium, and pulmonary arterioles, but recent evidence has highlighted a potentially central role for pulmonary venous and left atrial (LA) dysfunction. Epicardial adipose tissue occupies anatomical proximity to both structures, allowing derivative secretory products to influence their structure and function. The most well-characterized proinflammatory adipokine released from an expanded epicardial fat mass is activin A, which causes fibrosis and cardiomyocyte stiffness and senescence in underlying tissues by signaling through activin type II receptor signal transduction. Such signaling regulates pulmonary venular responses to mechanical stretch, and circulating activin A is elevated in patients with HFpEF who have enlarged LA chambers, pulmonary venous hypertension and increased pulmonary vascular resistance. The adipokine hypothesis of HFpEF identified activin A and activin type II receptor signaling as key adipokine mediators in the pathogenesis of HFpEF. Experimentally, activin A signaling promotes the development of both atrial myopathy and HFpEF, and activin type II receptor ligand traps alleviate HFpEF and ameliorate both the pulmonary vascular and left heart abnormalities in experimental models in which CpcPH-HFpEF is induced by obesity. These collective observations led to the prospective hypothesis that adipokine modulation by sotatercept would mediate benefits on the left heart in patients with CpcPH-HFpEF. These expectations were validated when the CADENCE trial showed that sotatercept decreased both pulmonary artery wedge pressures and left atrial volume index in patients with CpcPH-HFpEF, which are effects that could not explained by a decrease in pulmonary vascular resistance. Activin A released from an expanded epicardial adipose tissue promotes both pulmonary venous and left atrial remodeling and fibrosis in vivo, which (in turn) are effects that can be attenuated by an activin A decoy. The efficacy of sotatercept to slow the progression of CpcPH-HFpEF is now being tested in a phase III outcomes trial.

title: Self-reported geriatric impairments and treatment toxicity in older patients with multiple myeloma.
abstract: Frailty influences treatment outcomes in older patients with multiple myeloma (MM), yet existing frailty tools capture limited geriatric domains and are incompletely studied in the context of contemporary therapies. We prospectively evaluated patient-reported comprehensive geriatric assessment (CGA) domains and their associations with treatment toxicity and patient-reported outcomes (PRO) in older adults with MM. Patients aged ≥60 years with newly diagnosed or relapsed/refractory MM initiating a new therapy completed electronic CGA and PRO questionnaires at baseline and 4 months. Outcomes included clinician- and patient-reported treatment toxicity, treatment adaptations, health care use, and health-related quality of life (HRQOL). A cumulative deficit frailty index (FI) was derived from CGA and HRQOL domains. Among 90 patients (mean age, 72 years), geriatric impairments were common, particularly physical function domains. High-grade nonhematologic toxicities were significantly associated with older age, comorbidities, patient-reported functional limitations, and anxiety. Toxicity rates on the PRO version of the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) were higher than on CTCAE, highlighting a discordance between physician- and patient-reported treatment toxicity. Frailty was present in 22% and associated with worse baseline HRQOL and increased high-grade nonhematologic toxicity but not treatment adaptations or health care use. Average CGA and HRQOL scores remained stable over 4 months, although individual trajectories varied. Patient-reported geriatric impairments are prevalent in older adults with MM and strongly associated with nonhematologic toxicities even in the contemporary treatment era. Physician-reported CTCAE may not fully reflect patients' symptom burden. Heterogeneity in individual geriatric trajectories during treatment emphasize the need for longitudinal assessment. title: Optimizing cefiderocol use in clinical practice.
abstract: Cefiderocol is the first clinically available antibiotic to exploit bacterial iron transport systems to enter gram-negative pathogens. As its availability expands, questions remain regarding: its role relative to other agents for infections caused by NDM-producing Enterobacterales, difficult-to-treat resistant (DTR) Pseudomonas aeruginosa , carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii complex (CRAB), Stenotrophomonas maltophilia , and rarer nonfermenters; performance and interpretation of antimicrobial susceptibility testing; dosing in special populations; and emergence of resistance. This review addresses these uncertainties, emphasizing practical guidance for clinicians.Emerging preclinical and clinical data have better defined cefiderocol's role in antimicrobial resistant (AMR) infections, supporting its preferential use for NDM-producing Enterobacterales and S. maltophilia , while reserving it for DTR P. aeruginosa and CRAB when preferred alternatives are unavailable or unsuitable. Susceptibility testing remains complex: breakpoints differ across standards organizations, broth microdilution requires specialized iron-depleted media, and disk diffusion is practical but may overcall resistance. Cefiderocol resistance is typically driven by a convergence of mechanisms, including impaired siderophore uptake, increased β-lactamase production or modification, reduced permeability, or PBP3 alterations.With its unique structure and broad activity against resistant gram-negative pathogens, cefiderocol represents an important and evolving addition to the AMR therapeutic landscape.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). title: Identification and characterization of a novel distinct Pineal Neoplasm with Neuroendocrine and Epithelial Differentiation (PINNED).
abstract: Pineal region tumors are rare neoplasms that occur in all ages and account for less than 1% of all central nervous system (CNS) tumors in adults but are more frequent in children. Here, we describe a previously unrecognized tumor type of pineal origin characterized by a unique and consistent DNA methylation profile that does not match any known CNS tumor class and is distinct from all currently recognized pineal tumor entities. The presented cohort (n = 27) displayed a balanced sex distribution with a mean patient age of 35 years (range 7-75 years). The histopathological analyses demonstrated a highly cellular tumor showing various degrees of necrosis, mitotic activity, papillary structures, rosettes, epithelioid cytology, or signet-ring cells. The tumors consistently expressed cytokeratin 18, synaptophysin, chromogranin A, and OTX2, whereas CRX expression was absent. Four out of 16 tumors (25%) showed ATRX mutations and/or loss of protein expression as revealed by immunohistochemistry. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing confirmed molecular distinctiveness from other pineal neoplasms but revealed the closest similarities to papillary tumors of the pineal region (PTPR). Projection of the transcriptome data onto the cellular trajectory of the developing murine pineal gland suggests that pinealocyte progenitors are the cellular origins. Taken together, our findings define a novel type of pineal region tumor that we provisionally named 'Pineal Neoplasm with Neuroendocrine and Epithelial Differentiation' (PINNED). Recognition of this tumor type appears to be important for the accurate diagnosis of pineal region tumors and may have implications for future tumor classification and treatment strategies.© 2026. title: The Surgical Anatomy of the Lymphatic System of the Stomach.
abstract: The gastric lymphatic system is essential for immune function and the metastasis of gastric cancer. However, variations in lymphatic anatomy, drainage patterns, and staging frameworks complicate surgical planning and oncologic decision-making. This study aims to review the anatomy of the gastric lymphatic system, the history and variation of JCGC and UICC/AJCC TNM gastric lymphatic staging classifications, while also exploring the differences between lymphadenectomy strategies. A PRISMA-guided search across PubMed, PMC, ScienceDirect, Elsevier Science, Wiley, and SpringerLink retrieved eligible studies meeting pre-determined inclusion criteria. Of the 79 entries returned, 40 eligible studies were identified after application of our inclusion and exclusion criteria. The JCGC and UICC/AJCC TNM systems differ in their staging methods. While the JCGC categorizes lymph nodes by their location relative to the tumor, the UICC/AJCC categorizes the N stage by the number of positive lymph nodes detected. Though the UICC/AJCC staging system is dominant in multiple countries, efforts have been made in recent years to align the protocols in both staging systems. As a result, D2 lymphadenectomy is widely practiced in JCGC adhering countries, whereas UICC/AJCC protocols favor selective dissection combined with neoadjuvant chemotherapy. The complexity of gastric lymphatic anatomy and the absence of a globally standardized staging classification can lead to heterogeneous lymphadenectomy strategies and inconsistent oncologic outcomes. This review emphasizes the need for a unified classification system that incorporates anatomical, oncologic, and imaging perspectives to improve staging and optimize surgical decision-making.© 2026 American Association of Clinical Anatomists and British Association of Clinical Anatomists.

title: Microsporidiosis After Solid Organ Transplantation: A Multi-Species Case Series.
abstract: Microsporidiosis is an uncommon opportunistic infection in solid organ transplant (SOT) recipients. Case-level data on multi-species disease and management remain limited.We retrospectively reviewed SOT recipients with microsporidiosis at Mayo Clinic from January 2000 through February 2026. Cases were identified by text search and institutional polymerase chain reaction (PCR) records. Clinical, microbiologic, treatment, immunosuppression, and outcome data were abstracted.Ten recipients were identified: six kidney, two kidney-pancreas, and two heart recipients. Eight had enteritis and two had disseminated disease. Enterocytozoon bieneusi caused seven infections; the remaining cases were Encephalitozoon sp. enteritis, disseminated E. cuniculi, and disseminated Anncaliia algerae. All enteritis cases experienced diarrhea; seven experienced weight loss, five developed acute kidney injury, and five required hospitalization. The most common treatment administered was nitazoxanide (n = 6). Among these three achieved clinical remission, one improved without documented remission, and two had transient or partial improvement followed by recurrent diarrhea. Among four patients whose antimetabolite was held, reduced, or replaced at or before treatment, all improved clinically. In the two initially treated without antimetabolite modification, responses were transient or incomplete. Both Encephalitozoon infections achieved clinical remission with albendazole. Disseminated A. algerae was fatal.Microsporidiosis after SOT demonstrated a species-associated clinical spectrum: E. bieneusi was confined to enteritis, whereas non-E. bieneusi species caused both enteric and disseminated disease. In E. bieneusi enteritis, nitazoxanide improved symptoms, but responses were incomplete when antimetabolite therapy was continued. Encephalitozoon infections responded to albendazole, whereas disseminated A. algerae was refractory and fatal.© 2026 Wiley Periodicals LLC.

title: Is There a Cervical Alignment Threshold Warranting Cervical Inclusion in the Construct?
abstract: Postoperative thoracolumbar (TL) realignment in patients with adult spinal deformity (ASD) may induce cervical spine (CS) decompensation. This study identifies predictors of CS decompensation after TL surgery and defines a baseline CS-alignment threshold based on C2-pelvic angle (C2-PA) for CS inclusion in the TL construct.Patients with ASD undergoing TL fusion to the sacrum with an upper instrumented vertebrae at T2 or below and available baseline radiographs and patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) were included. CS decompensation was defined as CS surgery or >2 SD above the mean in C2-PA, cervical sagittal vertical axis (cSVA), or T1-slope cervical lordosis (TS-CL) at the studied postoperative time point.One thousand one hundred ninety patients were included; 166 (13.9%) had CS decompensation after TL surgery, including 24 (2.0%) requiring CS extension. CS decompensation was identified in 81 patients (6.8%) at 6 weeks (4 (0.3%) extensions), 13 (1.2%) at 6 months (2 (0.2%)), 43 (3.9%) at 1 year (7 (0.6%)), and 29 (2.8%) at 2 years (11 (0.9%)). Patients with CS decompensation at 6 months showed worse global and CS alignment at 6 weeks (lumbar lordosis: 53.6 vs 46.3; cSVA: 30.5 vs 38.5; P < .05). CS decompensation at 1 year was associated with worse PROMs (physical component score: 39.0 vs 35.4; Scoliosis research society score: 3.6 vs 3.3; P < .05). CS decompensation at 2 years was associated with worse CS alignment at 1 year (TS-CL: 20.8 vs 28.6; cSVA: 31.1 vs 37.8) and worse PROMs at 2 years. Higher baseline C2-PA was associated with shorter time to CS decompensation. Cox modeling identified baseline C2-PA (hazard ratio [HR] 1.05, 95% CI, 1.03-1.06), TS-CL (HR 1.05, 95% CI, 1.03-1.06), surgical invasiveness (HR 0.99, 95% CI, 0.98-0.99), and upper thoracic instrumentation (HR 2.9, 95% CI, 1.8-4.7) as predictors of CS decompensation, with a C2-PA threshold of 26.2°.Two years after TL ASD surgery, 13.9% had CS decompensation, with 14% requiring CS extension. Baseline CS alignment independently predicted CS decompensation. Patients with preoperative C2-PA >26.2° may benefit from CS inclusion in the TL construct after external validation of this threshold by future research.Copyright © Congress of Neurological Surgeons 2026. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether patients undergoing lower spine surgery for deformity develop problems in their upper neck spine, and identified warning signs that might indicate when to include the neck in the surgical repair. About 14% of patients showed upper neck spine problems within two years after lower spine surgery, and those with a specific baseline measurement above 26.2 degrees appeared at higher risk. Cervical decompensation occurred in 166 patients (13.9%), with 24 (2.0%) requiring cervical extension surgery, and was associated with worse patient-reported outcomes at 1 and 2 years. Cox regression identified baseline C2-pelvic angle, T1-slope cervical lordosis, surgical invasiveness, and upper thoracic instrumentation as independent predictors, establishing a C2-pelvic angle threshold of 26.2° for considering cervical inclusion.

title: Diastolic Function From Artificial Intelligence-Derived Electrocardiography in Mitral Annulus Calcification.
abstract: To evaluate whether a validated artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) model for left ventricular diastolic function (LVDF) can provide prognostic risk stratification in patients with significant mitral annulus calcification (MAC).We included patients who underwent transthoracic echocardiography and electrocardiography within 1 week between September 1, 2001, and April 30, 2023, and were not included in the AI-ECG LVDF training data set. Significant MAC was defined by consensus echocardiography criteria. Patients were assigned to 3 myocardial disease (MD) categories by the AI-ECG LVDF algorithm grading: normal/grade 1 LVDF (MD-1), grade 2 LVDF (MD-2), and grade 3 LVDF (MD-3). The analysis focused on prognostic stratification in this clinically distinct population. The primary end point was all-cause mortality.Of 2506 patients with significant MAC (mean age, 77 years; 64.1% female), 709 (28.3%) were classified as MD-1, 1510 (60.3%) as MD-2, and 287 (11.5%) as MD-3. Advanced MD grade correlated with older age, male sex, lower left ventricular ejection fraction, higher rates of comorbidities, and worse LVDF echocardiographic parameters. During a median follow-up of 2.8 years, 1059 (42.3%) patients died. Multivariable survival analysis found MD-2 (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.40; 95% CI, 1.19 to 1.64) and MD-3 (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.52; 95% CI, 1.21 to 1.92) to be independently associated with higher mortality risk, also after adjustment for mitral inflow diastolic pressure gradients.Myocardial disease grading derived from AI-ECG LVDF is independently associated with increased mortality risk in patients with significant MAC, underscoring its potential value in identifying high-risk patients in this challenging clinical population.Copyright © 2026 Mayo Foundation for Medical Education and Research. title: HER2 protein expression patterns in gallbladder adenocarcinoma and extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
abstract: Gallbladder adenocarcinoma (GBCa) and extrahepatic bile duct cholangiocarcinoma (ECCa) are aggressive malignancies. For unresectable, locally advanced, or metastatic disease, systemic therapy is the only treatment option. Survival rates remain dismal, thus a better understanding of their molecular biology and study of potential targeted therapies are important unmet needs. The tissue agnostic approval of HER2-targeted therapy for medications such as trastuzumab-deruxtecan (T-DXd) for tumors with strong (3+) HER2 expression by immunohistochemistry has motivated interest in HER2 expression among these tumor types. We sought to study the frequency and clinicopathologic features of HER2 expression in GBCa and ECCa. A 14-year retrospective analysis was performed on GBCa and ECCa, including metastatic cases. HER2 immunohistochemistry (Ventana, clone 4B5) was performed on eligible cases and interpreted using the CAP/ASCO gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma scoring guidelines. Clinicopathologic features were assessed with respect to HER2 immunoreactivity, and HER2 scoring agreement was calculated using weighted kappa statistics. There were 59 total cases (GBCa n = 43, ECCa n = 16), with five cases demonstrating strong (3+) HER2 reactivity (8.5%), 22 cases showing 1 + or 2 + immunoreactivity (37.3%), and 32 with a score of 0 (54.2%). HER2 score was higher in metastases compared to corresponding primaries in 7/18 events (38.9%). Among factors considered, histologic grade differed most significantly by HER2 score, with negative cases more likely to be poorly differentiated (p = 0.006). HER2 status was not significantly associated with clinical outcomes (3-year PFS, all-cause mortality). The study describes the frequency and clinicopathologic correlates of HER2 expression in gallbladder adenocarcinoma and extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.© 2026. title: Efzofitimod versus placebo in patients with pulmonary sarcoidosis (EFZO-FIT): a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.
abstract: Oral corticosteroids are currently standard-of-care therapy for pulmonary sarcoidosis, but they are associated with substantial toxicity and reduced health-related quality of life (HRQoL). The EFZO-FIT trial aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of efzofitimod, a novel immunomodulatory fusion protein targeting the neuropilin 2 receptor, as a steroid-sparing agent in pulmonary sarcoidosis.In this multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial, adults aged 18-75 years with pulmonary sarcoidosis requiring treatment were enrolled at 85 study centres across nine countries (Brazil, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Netherlands, Spain, UK, and USA). Participants were randomly assigned 1:1:1 using stratified block randomisation to receive monthly intravenous infusions of efzofitimod 3 mg/kg, efzofitimod 5 mg/kg, or placebo over a 48-week treatment period, including a 12-week oral corticosteroid taper targeting 0 mg per day (starting on day 15). Oral corticosteroid dose could be adjusted upwards in the event of worsening sarcoidosis. The primary endpoint was change from baseline in mean daily oral corticosteroid dose at week 48. Outcome and safety analyses were done in participants who received at least one dose of the study drug and had at least one post-baseline efficacy assessment. This study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05415137) and is complete.Between Sept 22, 2022, and Aug 14, 2025, 331 patients were screened for inclusion. 63 were excluded and 268 participants were randomly assigned to receive placebo (n=91), efzofitimod 3 mg/kg (n=89), or efzofitimod 5 mg/kg (n=88). Four patients were excluded after random assignment (one in the placebo group and three in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group). 264 patients who received at least one dose of study treatment and had at least one post-baseline assessment were included in the outcome analysis and safety population (90 in the placebo group, 86 in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group, and 88 in the efzofitimod 5 mg/kg group). Among the 264 participants, the mean age was 53·8 years (SD 10·6); 114 (43%) of 264 patients were female and 150 (57%) were male. 168 (64%) identified as White. Mean steroid dose was 10·7 mg per day (SD 4·4) at baseline and 2·9 mg per day (4·5) at week 48. No difference was seen in the magnitude of oral corticosteroid taper between the active and placebo dose groups; the placebo-adjusted change from baseline was 0·02 mg per day in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group (95% CI -1·49 to 1·52, p=0·98) and -0·73 mg per day in the efzofitimod 5 mg/kg group (-2·21 to 0·75, p=0·33). The percentage of participants with serious treatment-emergent adverse events was similar between groups. Malaise was more common in the placebo group (five [6%] of 90 patients vs zero in both efzofitimod groups). TEAEs that were more common in the efzofitimod groups included headache (17 [19%] of 88 patients in the efzofitimod 5 mg/kg group, 11 [13%] of 86 patients in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group, and four [4%] of 90 patients in the placebo group), sinusitis (nine [10%], six [7%], and two [2%] patients, respectively), wheezing (seven [8%], two [2%], and zero patients, respectively), and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) increased (five [6%], one [1%], and zero patients, respectively). Most adverse events were grade 1 or 2. Two participants died, both in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group (one respiratory failure and one incarceration of a pre-existing inguinal hernia). Neither event was considered to be causally related to the treatment.Efzofitimod was well tolerated but did not result in lower steroid doses at week 48 compared with placebo. The results from steroid tapering indicate that oral corticosteroid doses can be more aggressively reduced in many patients with pulmonary sarcoidosis.aTyr and Kyorin.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Strategies for Managing Obesity and Cardiometabolic Risk in Young Children: Current Evidence and Future Directions.
abstract: Early-onset obesity is associated with adverse cardiometabolic risk factors and early vascular changes linked to atherosclerosis, yet evidence-based treatment options for young children remain limited. The purpose of the review is to examine current evidence for lifestyle, pharmacologic, and surgical interventions for obesity management in preadolescent children, with emphasis on cardiometabolic and atherosclerotic risk.Lifestyle and familybased behavioral interventions remain first line therapy but often produce modest and variable weight reduction. Pharmacologic options for children younger than 12 years are limited, emerging data suggest selected agents, including topiramate, lisdexamfetamine, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and metformin can improve weight status and cardiometabolic risk factors in carefully selected patients. Bariatric surgery provides durable weight loss and cardiometabolic benefit and adolescents with severe obesity, though data and younger children are sparse. Available interventions may improve cardiometabolic risk profiles when appropriately applied early in life, but high-quality long-term data and preadolescent children are needed.© 2026. title: Impactful Research in Microtia and Auricular Reconstruction: A Bibliometric Analysis.
abstract: Microtia is a complex congenital auricular deformity, with research spanning operative technique, epidemiology/genetics, biomaterials, and complications. Despite this breadth, there is limited work characterizing which studies have been most influential in shaping the field. This study aimed to identify and analyze the top 100 most-cited articles on microtia using a bibliometric approach.A comprehensive search using the Web of Science (WoS) was conducted to identify studies on microtia, and the top 100 articles were selected by citation count. Bibliometric data, study type (clinical, review, and basic science), clinical focus category, materials discussed, and sample sizes for clinical studies were extracted. Spearman correlation tests and Kruskal-Wallis tests were used to analyze citation patterns.The top 100 microtia studies, published between 1957 and 2022, accumulated 12,692 total citations, with a mean of 127±84 citations per article, and were published across 49 journals. Clinical studies predominated (n=58), followed by reviews (n=28) and basic science studies (n=14). Publication year significantly differed by article type (P=0.02), with basic science studies tending to be more recent. Newer publication year was associated with higher citations per year (P<0.001) but fewer total citations overall (P=0.002). Among clinical studies, technique-focused papers were most common (n=27) and were largely centered on autologous costal cartilage reconstruction (n=25). Clinical studies examining alternative materials were less represented but tended to be more recent publications.These findings suggest that the most-cited microtia literature has primarily included landmark clinical technique papers, but newer, rapidly cited work increasingly reflects emerging biomaterials and tissue engineering.Copyright © 2026 Wolters Kluwer Health, LLC.
