title: Bone Marrow Cell Depletion in Myelofibrosis Is Associated With High-Risk Features and Shortened Survival: A Bone Marrow Pathology Group Study.
abstract: Fibrosis is a key histologic finding in the bone marrow (BM) of patients with advanced BCR::ABL1-negative myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPN). Fibrotic MPN can be associated with variable BM cellularity ranging from hypercellular to severe cell depletion. The significance of BM cellularity in the assessment of patients with advanced stage myelofibrosis (MF) is largely unknown. The current study compares cell-depleted MF patients with cellular MF controls in terms of morphologic, genetic, laboratory, and clinical features, including patient outcome. BMs that fulfilled the diagnostic criteria for advanced fibrotic phase MF (with MF-3 or osteosclerosis) including cases of primary myelofibrosis, post-polycythemia myelofibrosis and post-essential thrombocythemia myelofibrosis were collected from eleven participating institutions. BM hematopoietic cellularity was defined as depleted if cellularity was <30% in patients <70 and <20% for those >70 years old, and cellular if normocellular or hypercellular for age. Only cases with an adequate BM core biopsy and available clinical information including long-term follow-up were included. Data from 141 patients with cell-depleted MF and 100 patients with cellular MF were available. Thirty-three (26%) patients had depleted MF at diagnosis. Cell-depleted MF group had significantly lower hemoglobin and platelet counts, and higher peripheral blasts and basophils compared to cellular MF, although it was not independently prognostic. Patients had an increased prevalence of osteosclerosis (p<0.001). Depleted MF cases were enriched in ASXL1 (p=0.007), U2AF1 (p=0.01), EZH2 (p=0.026) and MPL (p=0.029) mutations. Finally, patients with depleted MF had significantly shorter overall survival (p=0.001). Cell-depletion in MF-3 patients is strongly associated with high-risk hematological and molecular features. These patients exhibit a distinct molecular signature compared to the cellular MF group, suggesting both underlying biological differences and features of more advanced disease. Thus, morphologic evaluation of bone marrow cellularity, fibrosis and osteosclerosis in MF patients may lead to a more accurate assessment of the disease status and guide clinical management.Copyright © 2026. Evaluating bone marrow cellularity alongside fibrosis may help doctors better assess disease severity and guide treatment decisions.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers examined bone marrow cellularity in 241 patients with advanced myelofibrosis (141 cell-depleted, 100 cellular) to assess associations with clinical and molecular features. Cell-depleted patients demonstrated lower hemoglobin and platelet counts, higher peripheral blasts, increased osteosclerosis prevalence, and enrichment in ASXL1, U2AF1, EZH2, and MPL mutations compared to cellular controls. Cell-depleted myelofibrosis was associated with significantly shortened overall survival (p=0.001), though cellularity alone was not independently prognostic.

title: Advances in the management of renal cell carcinoma.
abstract: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is the most common form of kidney cancer, with 435 000 patients newly diagnosed worldwide each year. In addition to morphology and histology, molecular subtyping has advanced the diagnostic classification of RCC. Contemporary diagnosis relies on cross sectional imaging in the form of computed tomography or magnetic resonance imaging and selective biopsy. For localised disease, nephrectomy remains the standard of care, with partial nephrectomy being an option for smaller tumours. Ablation or stereotactic radiation is appropriate for selected patients. Adjuvant pembrolizumab provides improved disease-free and overall survival in high risk clear cell RCC. In metastatic disease, the introduction of immune checkpoint inhibitor based combinations has extended overall survival, providing a durable response in some patients. Despite these advances, primary and secondary resistance, along with the lack of predictive and prognostic biomarkers, remain a challenge.Published by the BMJ Publishing Group Limited. title: Management of Patients with High-risk Localised, Locally Advanced, and Biochemically Recurrent Prostate Cancer: Report from the 2026 Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference.
abstract: Innovations have improved outcomes in high-risk localised, locally advanced, and biochemically recurrent prostate cancer (PC), yet high-level evidence remains limited for many management decisions. The 2026 Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference (APCCC) surveyed an international panel on key clinical questions to complement evidence-based guidelines.Here we present the voting results for the questions on high-risk localised, locally advanced, and biochemically recurrent PC from APCCC 2026.Before the conference, a multidisciplinary panel of 144 international PC experts used a modified Delphi process to develop 313 multiple-choice consensus questions, of which 134 covered high-risk localised and locally advanced PC, including prostate-specific antigen (PSA) persistence and PSA recurrence, and side effects of treatment. These questions were administered to the 133 voting panel members "panellists" via a web-based survey prior to the conference.Consensus was defined a priori as ≥75% agreement, with strong consensus defined as ≥90% agreement. Overall, consensus was reached for 44 of the 134 questions (32.8%), with seven questions reaching a strong consensus. Results and limitations The voting results show varying degrees of consensus, as discussed in this article and as detailed in the Supplementary Material. An interactive heat map for the questions can be found at https://apccc.org/APCCC2026-votings-localised-and-locally-advanced-prostate-cancer/. These findings do not include a formal literature review or meta-analysis.The voting results can help physicians and patients navigate controversial areas of clinical management for which evidence is scant or conflicting. The findings can also help funders and policymakers in prioritising areas for future research. Importantly, APCCC 2026 once again identified important gaps (areas of no consensus) that merit evaluation in specifically designed trials.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). Published by Elsevier B.V. title: Assessing Resident Perceptions and Needs: Global Orthopaedic Opportunities in North American Residency Programs.
abstract: Global orthopaedics includes collaborative efforts to improve clinical care, education, research, and capacity across international settings, with an emphasis on equitable, bidirectional, and sustainable partnerships. Interest in global orthopaedics among North American residents continues to grow, yet structured opportunities for clinical, educational, and research engagement in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) remain limited. This study evaluated the availability of global orthopaedic opportunities within residency programs and assessed resident experiences, perceptions, and interest in expanding these initiatives.A cross-sectional survey was distributed to orthopaedic surgery residents in the United States and Canada through the Consortium of Orthopaedic Academic Traumatologists (COACT)-affiliated faculty and resident leads. Residents from postgraduate years 1 to 5 were eligible. Survey domains included prior global health experience, opportunities available at home institutions, resident satisfaction with existing resources, and interest in future global orthopaedic engagement. Descriptive statistics were performed.Thirty of 35 residency programs (85.7%) participated, with 299 of 300 residents completing the survey (99.7%). Forty-six respondents (15.4%) reported prior or current participation in global orthopaedic activities, most commonly through organized teaching or clinical experiences (50.0%), research collaborations (41.3%), and elective international clinical rotations (37.0%). Nearly one third of residents (30.1%) reported that their residency program offered no global orthopaedic opportunities. Residents expressed dissatisfaction with the availability of mentorship, elective international rotations, and global outreach opportunities at their home institutions. Despite limited access, interest in expanding opportunities in LMICs was notable, particularly for mentorship and guidance (73.2%), elective international rotations (72.9%), and collaborative research (54.8%).North American orthopaedic residents demonstrate substantial interest in global orthopaedic engagement that exceeds the opportunities currently available. These findings support expanding structured mentorship, international partnerships, and centralized networks such as COACT to facilitate sustainable global clinical, educational, and research opportunities during residency.Copyright © 2026 The Authors. title: Reassessing alcohol consumption and cardiovascular disease by addressing bias in observational data: results from the multi-ethnic study of atherosclerosis.
abstract: Alcohol and its relationship with cardiovascular disease (CVD) remain contentious. Several observational studies have found cardioprotective associations, while Mendelian randomization studies have found null or harmful effects of moderate drinking. Biases, including abstainer misclassification and sick-quitter effects, may obscure true associations. It is widely understood that former drinkers are often sick quitters. However, removal of former drinkers from analyses addresses bias in the abstainer group but fails to account for induced survivorship among current drinkers. This study sought to determine whether adjusting for biases altered the association between alcohol and CVD by comparing conventional models with those using (i) occasional drinkers as the reference group instead of lifetime abstainers and (ii) 'intention-to-treat' reallocation of former drinkers based on past drinking patterns.The Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis is a prospective cohort study of 6814 participants aged 45-84 years between 2000 and 2002 without baseline CVD. A total of 6755 participants were included after excluding those with missing data. Alcohol consumption was self-reported and classified as lifetime abstainer, former, or current drinker [occasional (≤1 drink/week), light (2-7 drinks/week), moderate (8-14 drinks/week), heavy (>14 drinks/week)]. Outcomes included coronary artery calcium (CAC; 0, 1-100, 101-300, and >300) and clinical events [myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, cardiovascular mortality, composite major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs), and heart failure]. Of 6755 participants, 20.6% were lifetime abstainers, 24.1% former drinkers, and 55.3% current drinkers. Adjusting for biases altered the observed relationship between alcohol and CVD, showing increased harm with light drinking, decreased protection with moderate drinking, and a dose-response relationship between alcohol and CAC, particularly CAC >300 in adjusted models. Protective associations between moderate drinking and MI [hazard ratio (HR): 0.64, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.38-1.06] and cardiovascular mortality (HR: 0.81, 95% CI: 0.53-1.25) were attenuated and became non-significant. Light drinking shifted from null to increased risk for MI (HR: 1.46, 95% CI: 1.11-1.92), stroke (HR: 1.54, 95% CI: 1.17-2.03), MACE (HR: 1.33, 95% CI: 1.12-1.57), and heart failure (HR: 1.42, 95% CI: 1.10-1.84).Associations between alcohol and CVD in observational studies are sensitive to methodologic variation. title: Revascularization in Asymptomatic Carotid Artery Stenosis With Hemodynamic Impairment and Cognitive Outcomes: The CREST-H Substudy of the CREST-2 Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract: Cerebral hemodynamic impairment in patients with asymptomatic internal carotid artery (ICA) stenosis is associated with reduced cognition. It is uncertain whether revascularization might be an effective treatment for cognitive impairment in these patients.To test whether any cognitive benefit from revascularization of high-grade, asymptomatic ICA stenosis varies based on the degree of baseline cerebral hemodynamic impairment.This substudy was conducted within a multicenter phase 3 randomized clinical trial. Adults (aged 35-86 years) without dementia with eighth-grade education or higher and unilateral asymptomatic ICA stenosis greater than or equal to 70% were enrolled from January 2018 to July 2024 at 61 sites in North America (last follow-up in July 2025). Of 607 participants screened from 2485 in CREST-2, 392 were enrolled. Magnetic resonance or computed tomographic perfusion imaging tested for baseline hemodynamic impairment defined by delayed time-to-peak (TTP) arrival of intravenous contrast in the hemisphere ipsilateral minus contralateral to the stenotic artery.Carotid revascularization (endarterectomy or stenting) plus intensive medical management (IMM) vs IMM alone.The primary outcome was the difference in composite cognitive z score over 1 year based on 5 cognitive tests. The primary analysis tested for an interaction between treatment group (revascularization vs IMM alone) and degree of baseline hemodynamic impairment among those with reduced baseline cognition (cognitive z score ≤-1.0 SD).Of 392 participants enrolled (mean age, 71 years; 125 [32%] females), 61 were excluded for missing baseline imaging and 40 for missing cognitive examinations or other covariates, leaving 291 with complete data. Fifty-one had reduced cognition at baseline (25 in the revascularization group and 26 in the IMM alone group). TTP ranged from no interhemispheric TTP delay to a more-than-2-second delay. Mean (SD) cognitive z scores were -1.36 (0.51) at baseline and -1.17 (0.47) at 1 year in the revascularization group and -1.34 (0.83) at baseline and -1.01 (0.97) at 1 year in the IMM alone group. The primary analysis showed no difference in cognition by treatment group over 1 year, adjusting for treatment group × hemodynamic status interaction and other covariates (adjusted difference in cognitive z score, -0.15 SD [95% CI, -0.54 to 0.24]). The interaction was not significant (β estimate = 0.018 [95% CI, -0.025 to 0.061]; P = .40).In this substudy of a randomized clinical trial, there was no differential effect of revascularization vs IMM alone on cognition over 1 year by cerebral hemodynamic status among those with baseline reduced cognition, suggesting that revascularization does not improve cognitive dysfunction by restoring flow to the brain in chronic asymptomatic carotid stenosis.ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03121209.

title: Investigational drug services operations: Defining core and supplemental workload metrics.
abstract: Investigational drug services (IDS) support highly complex and regulated aspects of clinical research, yet the absence of defined workload metrics limits clear and consistent understanding of IDS workload across pharmacy, research, and executive leadership. Staffing and resource requests, as well as being responsible for acceptance of new studies, require defensible, numerical workload data to secure leadership approval for additional resources. We developed a structured approach to IDS workload measurement that includes broadly applicable core metrics and site-specific supplemental metrics to support staffing justification, resource allocation, and operational planning.A modified Delphi process informed by literature-identified metrics was used to achieve expert consensus on IDS workload definitions and metrics. Subject matter experts in IDS pharmacy practice and clinical research operations participated in iterative rounds of review. Metrics were categorized into core workload elements and supplemental metrics. Core metrics broadly describe site characteristics and day-to-day operations. Supplemental metrics capture study-specific, expanded services or site-derived time-based measures.Organizing IDS workload into core and supplemental components provides a structured method to account for both routine operations and expanded study- or site- driven demands using consistent and meaningful terminology, creating a foundation for capturing and describing IDS workload data.© The Author(s) 2026. title: Uveal melanoma: innovations in therapy, prognosis, and imaging.
abstract: Uveal melanoma (UM) is the most common adult primary intraocular malignancy with local tumor control exceeding 95%, while ~50% of patients still develop metastasis. Advances in diagnostic tools, therapeutics, and prognostication guide individualized care and support a shift toward precision medicine.This narrative review covers advances in imaging, therapy, and prognosis. Literature was identified through searches of PubMed, Embase, Google Scholar, and ClinicalTrials.gov through August 2026, supplemented by reference lists and clinical practice guidelines. Topics include imaging advances in optical coherence tomography (OCT), ultrasonography, and lesion classification using artificial intelligence (AI); globe-preserving local therapies, systemic T-cell-based therapies, targeted therapies, checkpoint inhibitors, and liver-directed approaches; and prognostic tools based on gene expression profiling, preferentially expressed antigen in melanoma (PRAME), cytogenetics, and circulating tumor DNA.The clinical approach to UM is evolving rapidly, with more clinical trials than ever. Advances aim to improve early detection and preserve vision while controlling the primary tumor, and the first US Food and Drug Administration-approved therapies offer incremental improvements in survival for patients with metastatic disease. Imaging-based AI may support earlier detection, while collaboration between clinicians and laboratory scientists remains essential to improving survival.

title: Multicenter evaluation of the multiplex polymerase chain reaction QIAstat-Dx Meningitis/Encephalitis Panel for the detection of central nervous system pathogens directly in the cerebrospinal fluid.
abstract: Rapid and accurate detection of pathogens causing meningitis/encephalitis (MEN/EN) is critical to improving clinical outcomes. Multiplex polymerase chain reaction (PCR) enables simultaneous detection of multiple pathogens from the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), offering advantages over traditional methods. This multicenter study evaluated the performance of the QIAstat-Dx Meningitis/Encephalitis (ME) Panel versus conventional methods, including the BioFire FilmArray ME (BFME) Panel. The CSF samples from patients with suspected MEN/EN along with contrived samples were tested across 13 sites in Europe/USA. Positive percent agreement (PPA) and negative percent agreement (NPA) between the QIAstat-Dx ME Panel and comparator methods were determined. A total of 1,667 clinical samples (1,527 prospective, 140 archived) were tested. Pathogens were detected by the QIAstat-Dx ME Panel in 115 (7.5%) prospective samples, including Streptococcus pneumoniae (1.1%), Haemophilus influenzae (0.5%), Listeria monocytogenes (0.3%), S. agalactiae (0.2%), Escherichia coli K1 (0.1%), Neisseria meningitidis (0.1%), S. pyogenes (0.1%), enterovirus (1.5%), human herpesvirus-6 (1.0%), herpes simplex virus-2 (0.9%) and -1 (0.3%), varicella zoster virus (0.7%), cytomegalovirus (0.3%), human parechovirus (0.3%), and Cryptococcus gattii/neoformans (0.4%). Overall PPA versus BFME (n = 1,664) was 85.4%, increasing to 95.3% after discordance resolution. PPA was 100% for N. meningitidis, S. pneumoniae, and S. agalactiae. Overall NPA was 99.9%. Among 1,154 contrived positive samples, only 27 (2.3%) incorrect results were observed. The QIAstat-Dx ME Panel demonstrated high concordance with BFME, supporting its use as a reliable, fully automated multiplex PCR platform for rapid diagnosis of community-acquired MEN/EN.IMPORTANCEThis multicenter study demonstrated that the QIAstat-Dx ME Panel delivers clinical performance comparable to that of the BioFire FilmArray ME (BFME) Panel, supporting its validity as a reliable syndromic molecular diagnostic tool for MEN/EN. With its broad pathogen coverage, rapid turnaround time (TAT), and the ability to provide amplification curves and Ct values, the QIAstat-Dx ME Panel offers a valuable option for broad and timely detection of bacterial, viral, and fungal CNS pathogens. When used alongside the SoC diagnostic methods, this panel has the potential to improve early diagnosis, guide targeted therapy, and support effective clinical management of patients with suspected MEN/EN.

title: Sex-Based Outcomes After Carotid Artery Revascularization in Symptomatic Patients: A Multi-Center Cohort Study.
abstract: Sex-based differences in outcomes after carotid revascularization remain poorly defined in symptomatic patients. We aimed to compare short and long-term outcomes between men and women with symptomatic carotid artery disease who underwent carotid revascularization across a ten-year period in three stroke centers.A retrospective study was conducted on a consecutive series of cases between 2016 and 2026. Cases included patients presenting with stroke, transient ischemic attack (TIA), or amaurosis fugax attributable to ipsilateral carotid artery stenosis within six months prior carotid endarterectomy (CEA), transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR), or transfemoral carotid artery stenting (TFCAS). Patients with prior neck radiation were excluded. Primary outcomes were stroke, TIA, myocardial infarction (MI), and death within 30 days. Secondary outcomes included long-term stroke, TIA, MI, death, restenosis, and reintervention. Both primary and secondary outcomes were analyzed individually and as a composite endpoint. To account for sex-based differences and vulnerable plaque feature burden, a 1:1 propensity score-matched (PSM) analysis was performed among patients with available magnetic resonance angiography with vessel wall imaging (MRA-VWI).A total of 822 procedures were performed (men: 571, 69.5%; women: 251, 30.5%) with a mean age of 73.2 ± 9.2 years. Procedure distribution was similar between groups (CEA: 69.4% vs 70.9%; TCAR: 6.1% vs 5.6%; TFCAS: 24.5% vs 23.5%, p=0.89). Demographics and comorbidities were otherwise comparable between groups. Women had higher total cholesterol (185.9 ± 50.1 vs 158.1 ± 43.4 mg/dL, p<0.01), HDL (56.8 ± 18.1 vs 45.9 ± 15.2 mg/dL, p<0.01), and LDL (101.5 ± 45.4 vs 86.3 ± 38.0 mg/dL, p<0.01); however, the LDL/HDL ratio was not significant. Medication regimens were similar between groups, except estrogen use, which was exclusive to women (4.0%, p<0.01). Symptom presentation was comparable for stroke (49.0% vs 48.6%, p=0.91), TIA (32.0% vs 33.5%, p=0.69), and amaurosis fugax (22.1% vs 20.7%, p=0.67). At 30 days, the composite of stroke, TIA, MI, and death was similar (4.2% vs 4.0%, p=0.88), with no statistically significant differences in ipsilateral stroke (2.5% vs 1.6%, p=0.61), TIA (0.7% vs 1.6%, p=0.23), MI (0.5% vs 0.0%, p=0.25), or mortality (0.5% vs 1.2%, p=0.30). On long-term follow-up at 3.3 ± 2.6 years, the composite outcomes remained comparable (24.2% vs 24.3%, p=0.97), as were ipsilateral stroke (3.7% vs 5.2%, p=0.32), TIA (5.1% vs 4.0%, p=0.50), MI (2.6% vs 3.6%, p=0.45), mortality (17.5% vs 19.1%, p=0.58), restenosis (4.9% vs 7.2%, p=0.19), and reintervention rates (2.5% vs 4.8%, p=0.08). In the PSM cohort (men: 91, women: 91, N=182), the 30-day (3.3% vs 2.2%, p=1.00) and long-term (34.1% vs 31.9%, p=0.88) composite outcome of stroke, TIA, MI and death were similar. Restenosis (4.4% vs 7.7%, p=0.54), and reintervention (1.1% vs 6.6%, p=0.12) were also not statistically significantly different between groups.No statistically significant sex-based differences were identified in 30-day or long-term outcomes after CEA, TCAR, or TFCAS across a ten-year period at three high-volume stroke centers. Furthermore, on propensity score matching of our highest risk patient population with vulnerable plaque features did not affect their short- and long-term outcomes.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: Assessing Patient Perspectives in Seeking Radical Cystectomy Care: A Qualitative Analysis.
abstract: To assess the perspectives of patients after radical cystectomy (RC) to identify potential targets for future improvement. Relatively little is known about why patients choose to receive RC in a particular setting, where they seek information regarding their care, and what information they find difficult to identify or tasks they find most burdensome in the process of seeking out RC care.Semi-structured qualitative interviews were conducted by a single investigator (APM) with adults who underwent RC at our center between March 2020 and July 2021. Interviews were conducted from December 2021 and May 2022 using a semi-structured interview guide to assess patient experience with RC as well as features associated with decision-making regarding their care. Responses were coded based on content to identify themes and subthemes.A total of 12 patients were interviewed, of whom 2 (17%) were female and 10 (83%) were Caucasian. Four major themes emerged: challenges in managing logistics of seeking a specialized major surgery, understanding of treatment options and expectations, the physical and emotional toll of diagnosis and surgery, and quality of communication with healthcare providers as a proxy for quality of care.Bladder cancer patients cited the content and quality of communication with their healthcare team and logistics of traveling to a treating center as key considerations in determining where to undergo RC. Future interventions aimed at improving access to RC should focus on decreasing communication barriers and alleviating the burden of frequent travel.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. llm_summary: Researchers interviewed 12 bladder cancer patients who had undergone radical cystectomy, a major surgical procedure to remove the bladder, to understand their experiences and decision-making process. Patients identified four main concerns: the logistical challenges of traveling for specialized surgery, understanding their treatment options, coping with the emotional and physical impact of their diagnosis and surgery, and the quality of communication with their healthcare providers. The findings suggest that improving communication and reducing travel burdens could help make this major surgery more accessible to patients.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers conducted semi-structured qualitative interviews with 12 adults who underwent radical cystectomy at their center between March 2020 and July 2021, with interviews performed from December 2021 to May 2022 using a standardized interview guide to assess patient experiences and decision-making factors. The study population consisted predominantly of male (83%) and Caucasian (83%) participants, and responses were coded to identify emergent themes related to the radical cystectomy care-seeking process. Four major themes emerged from the analysis: challenges in managing logistics of seeking specialized major surgery, understanding of treatment options and expectations, the physical and emotional toll of diagnosis and surgery, and quality of communication with healthcare providers. Patients identified communication quality with their healthcare team and the logistics of traveling to a treating center as key considerations in determining where to undergo radical cystectomy. Future interventions to improve access to radical cystectomy should prioritize decreasing communication barriers and alleviating the burden of frequent travel, though the small sample size and single-center design limit generalizability of these findings.

title: Global, regional, and national burden of unintentional poisoning, 1990-2023: results from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
abstract: Unintentional poisoning is a preventable cause of injury-related morbidity and mortality, yet global patterns, trends, and inequalities remain incompletely characterised. Within the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) framework, unintentional poisoning includes poisoning by carbon monoxide and poisoning by other means, a category largely informed by pesticide poisoning codes plus some indirect capture of other poisoning as part of the GBD re-distribution process. Poisonings by pharmaceuticals and illicit substances are not captured in the GBD definition of poisoning. We aimed to quantify this GBD-defined burden and assess regional variation, sociodemographic gradients, and case fatality between 1990 and 2023.We analysed GBD 2023 estimates for 204 countries and territories, modelling deaths, incidence, and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) using standard GBD cause-of-death and non-fatal estimation methods with 95% uncertainty intervals. We stratified results by age, sex, region, and Socio-demographic Index (SDI), and derived case fatality from modelled deaths and incidence.In 2023, unintentional poisoning from carbon monoxide and other means caused 2·54 million incident poisonings, 69 805 deaths, and 3·68 million DALYs globally, with age-standardised DALY rates declining by 47·5% since 1990. Carbon monoxide accounted for 641 932 poisonings, 30 890 deaths and 1·34 million DALYs, with the highest burdens in central and eastern Europe and central Asia. Most regions showed substantial long-term declines, and the global age-standardised DALY rate for carbon monoxide poisoning declined by 58·2% since 1990. Poisoning by other means caused 1·90 million incident cases, 38 914 deaths, and 2·34 million DALYs, with the greatest burden in sub-Saharan Africa. Most regions showed declining age-standardised DALY rates for poisoning by other means; however, there was no clear change (with the 95% uncertainty interval including zero) in the global estimate, driven by wide uncertainty intervals in several regions (including sub-Saharan Africa). Mortality and DALYs were inversely associated with SDI, and derived case fatality was highest in low-SDI regions.Global reductions in GBD-defined unintentional poisoning by carbon monoxide and other means are consistent with decades of regulatory and environmental interventions. These include bans of highly toxic pesticides, improved heating and ventilation systems, emissions controls, and adoption of carbon monoxide alarms. Stark inequalities persist in some regions and in low-SDI settings. Compared with previous GBD publications, this study provides a detailed global assessment of unintentional poisoning by carbon monoxide and other means up to 2023, integrating incidence, DALYs, and comparative case fatality across regions.Gates Foundation and the Australian National Health and Medical Research Council.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). However, significant inequalities persist, with low-income regions experiencing higher death rates from poisoning.

title: Pazopanib alternating with bevacizumab in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma naive to treatment: a multicentre, single-arm, phase 1/2 trial.
abstract: VEGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) are considered the backbone for the treatment of metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma. We hypothesise that the administration of bevacizumab during scheduled breaks in pazopanib (TKI) treatment can improve tolerability and prolong progression-free survival compared with historical controls.In this single-arm, phase 1/2 trial in five US academic cancer centres, patients (aged ≥18 years) with histologically confirmed metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 1 or less, and adequate organ functions were included. The phase 1 portion included patients with up to one previous therapy with high-dose IL-2 or an anti-PD-1 compound alone or in combination with a CTLA-4 inhibitor. The phase 2 portion enrolled only patients with treatment-naive metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma. The primary endpoint of phase 1 was to find the recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D). We tested a novel regimen using four dose levels: oral pazopanib (600 or 800 mg daily on days 1-28, followed by a 7 day break) alternating with intravenous bevacizumab (5, 7·5, or 10 mg/kg, one on day 36 and one on day 50) on a 10-week cycle in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma naive to TKI treatment. The primary endpoint of phase 2 was median progression-free survival, assessed by a masked central statistician review. Dose selection (in patients who had completed 15 weeks) and activity (in patients who had completed one full 10-week cycle of the novel regimen) were analysed in the per-protocol population. Safety analyses included all patients who received any treatment. This trial was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01684397) and is ongoing but closed to new participants.Between Nov 21, 2012, and June 11, 2018, phase 1 enrolled 25 patients, with 18 patients evaluable for dose-limiting toxicity during the extended 15-week safety assessment period. The RP2D was established as pazopanib 800 mg daily (days 1-28) and bevacizumab 10 mg/kg on days 36 and 50 of a 10-week cycle. Between Jan 23, 2019, and Oct 19, 2023, phase 2 enrolled 53 patients, of whom 51 (including six from phase 1) were evaluable for activity and 59 were evaluable for safety. 36 (71%) patients were male and 15 (29%) were female, and 48 (94%) patients were White. 33 (65%) patients in phase 2 had favourable risk per the International Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma Database Consortium categories. After a median follow-up of 63·7 months (IQR 16·2-73·5), median progression-free survival was 24·8 months (95% CI 17·2-34·3). The most common grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events were hypertension (20 [34%] of 59) and elevated aspartate aminotransferase (seven [12%]) and alanine aminotransferase (ten [17%]). Five (8%) patients discontinued the study for drug-related serious adverse events. No treatment-related deaths occurred.The phase 1 portion identified the safe RP2D. The phase 2 portion showed that this novel regimen has promising antitumour activity in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma in the predominantly favourable risk group who are naive to treatment. title: Characterising the genomic landscape of two clinical risk groups in CD30+ T-cell lymphoproliferative disorders with cutaneous involvement: a multi-institutional retrospective study.
abstract: CD30+ T cell lymphoproliferative disorders (CD30+ T LPD) with cutaneous involvement comprise a diverse group of neoplasms with variable clinical outcomes. The molecular mechanisms underlying the prognostic differences in these diseases are poorly understood.In this multi-institutional retrospective study, 79 patients with CD30+ T LPD were evaluated. DNA and RNA sequencing were performed on skin biopsy samples to characterise molecular features. Patients were assigned to low- and high-risk groups based on treatment recommendations in clinical records. Pathogenic pathways, immune microenvironments, transcriptomic profiles, driver mutations, and mutation signatures were compared between the risk groups.Across risk groups, there was high mutational recurrence in genes involved in epigenetic regulation and intracellular signalling pathways. Mutational signature analysis revealed a shared prevalence of 5-methylcytosine deamination, UV exposure, defective mismatch repair, and POLE-associated proofreading deficiency. In contrast, gene set enrichment analysis showed that the high-risk group was enriched in pathways governing cell cycle progression, DNA damage response, and immune activation compared to the low-risk group. Furthermore, immune microenvironment deconvolution showed a higher abundance of resting dendritic cells in the low-risk group. Finally, high-risk patients exhibited significant overexpression of clinically relevant proteins, highlighting potential alternative treatment approaches for this population.Mutation analyses suggest diverse pathogenesis in these diseases. The high-risk and low-risk groups diverge in gene expression profiles and immune microenvironment, suggesting that these biological differences hold prognostic significance. Molecularly informed therapeutic strategies should be investigated prospectively through clinical trials.This work was supported by developmental funds of the Duke Cancer Institute as part of the P30 Cancer Center Support Grant. title: Optimizing inferior petrosal sinus sampling: results of a multicenter study.
abstract: Inferior petrosal sinus sampling (IPSS) confirms a central source of adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) secretion in Cushing's disease (CD). We explored IPSS protocols to optimize diagnostic sensitivity and reduce laboratory testing burden. Patients from the multicenter Registry of Adenomas of the Pituitary and Related Disorders (RAPID) who underwent IPSS for management of CD, and in whom central:peripheral (C:P) ACTH levels were evaluated, were included. A total of 93 patients (mean age 44 ± 13 years, 17% male; 78% MRI-negative, 84% long-term remission) were analyzed. At baseline, 77% of patients showed a C:P ACTH ratio ≥2X, and all of these patients reached ≥3X C:P ACTH after stimulation. Among patients with a baseline ratio <2X, 57% (n = 12/21) crossed the ≥3X threshold after stimulation, prolactin normalization confirmed one additional patient, with two further patients remaining indeterminate. Stimulation produced 3.1-, 2.8-, and 1.9-fold increases in C:P ACTH at 2, 5, and 10 min post-stimulation, respectively, with the best response at 2-5 min. Cumulatively, 77%, 79%, 88%, 90%, and 91% of patients met criteria for CD by 0, 2, 5, 10, and 15 min, respectively. In this confirmed-CD cohort these proportions represent test sensitivity, rising from 77.4% (95% CI 67.6-85.4%) at baseline to 91.4% (95% CI 83.8-96.2%) by 15 min. Because all patients had surgically confirmed CD, these values reflect test sensitivity rather than overall diagnostic accuracy. Diagnostic yield plateaued by 15 min with negligible gain thereafter, and baseline together with a limited number of early post-stimulation samples captured most cases. These retrospective, hypothesis-generating findings suggest that a streamlined protocol may reduce laboratory and interpretive burden while preserving sensitivity, pending prospective validation.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a streamlined testing protocol for inferior petrosal sinus sampling—a procedure that confirms whether a pituitary tumor is causing excess hormone production in Cushing's disease—could maintain diagnostic accuracy while reducing laboratory burden. The study found that collecting blood samples at baseline and within the first 5 to 15 minutes after stimulation captured 91% of confirmed cases, suggesting that fewer samples than typically collected may be sufficient. However, these findings are based on retrospective analysis of patients already confirmed to have the disease and require prospective validation before clinical implementation.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers examined inferior petrosal sinus sampling (IPSS) protocols in 93 patients with surgically confirmed Cushing's disease from a multicenter registry to optimize diagnostic sensitivity for detecting central adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) secretion. At baseline, 77% of patients demonstrated a central:peripheral ACTH ratio ≥2X, and stimulation increased this proportion to 91% by 15 minutes post-stimulation, with the greatest fold-increase in C:P ACTH occurring at 2–5 minutes. The diagnostic yield plateaued by 15 minutes with negligible additional gain thereafter, suggesting that baseline sampling combined with limited early post-stimulation samples captured most diagnostic cases. Among patients with baseline C:P ACTH ratios <2X, 57% crossed the ≥3X threshold after stimulation, with prolactin normalization and other criteria confirming additional cases. These retrospective findings suggest that a streamlined IPSS protocol may reduce laboratory testing burden while preserving diagnostic sensitivity, pending prospective validation.

title: Domain Adaptation of a Large Language Model for Radiology Impression Generation - Multi-Reader Evaluation.
abstract: To evaluate the clinical and practical trade-offs between domain adaptation and fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs) for radiology impression generation, with outcomes assessed through blinded expert radiologist review. In this retrospective institutional review board (IRB)-approved study 3,123,836 CT and MR reports were split into domain adaptation (80%), fine-tuning (16%), validation (2%), and test (2%) sets. Five LLM models were compared to ground truth: a base Llama-3-8B model (Meta) domain-adapted with mixed general, medical, and radiology text then fine-tuned using small (n = 1,280) and large (n = 499,814) number of report-impression pairs (DA + FTs, DA + FTl), an OpenBio-8B model with identical fine-tuning (Bio + FTs, Bio + FTl) and Gemini-1.5-Flash-002 used out-of-the-box. Four radiologists independently rated generated radiology impressions for abdominal CT and MR reports using six 5-point Likert items. Automated NLP metrics were also assessed. Domain adaptation improved performance in low-data regimes (mean score of DA + FTs 24.3 ± 2.8 vs. Bio + FTs 22.8 ± 3.5, P = 0.0004), but offered diminishing returns with large-scale fine-tuning (DA + FTl 24.9 ± 4.0 vs. Bio + FTl 25.0 ± 3.8, P = 0.89). Large-scale fine-tuned open-source models surpassed the commercial model in expert-rated quality and harmful output rates. Agreement among radiologists was low (ICC 0.22-0.49). Automated metrics showed weak correlation with human evaluation (ρ < 0.32). Domain adaptation improves LLM performance when labeled clinical data are scarce, but its incremental benefit diminishes as the fine-tuning dataset grows. Standard NLP metrics poorly reflect clinical relevance, underscoring the need for expert-informed evaluation. The findings help define the data-efficiency threshold for LLMs cost-effective deployment in clinical practice.© 2026. title: A Digital Mental Health Literacy Program Reduces Adolescent Depression and Anxiety Symptoms in a District-Wide Trial.
abstract: Adolescent mental health problems have risen sharply, creating an urgent need for scalable solutions. Although several mental health literacy (MHL) programs show promise, none with broad implementation feasibility have demonstrated reductions in adolescents' anxiety or depression. This study examined the mental health outcomes of a brief, digital MHL program.We conducted a preregistered cluster-randomized trial using an intent-to-treat approach with all ninth graders in a U.S. school district (N = 1,080), comparing an 80-minute digital MHL program to a time- and format-matched active control also framed as supporting mental health. Ten weeks later, students completed self-report measures of depression, anxiety, and MHL-related knowledge, attitudes, and help-seeking motivation.Students in the MHL condition reported significantly lower depression and anxiety symptoms. Increased willingness to seek help partially mediated the effect on depressive symptoms, but not anxiety.Findings indicate that brief digital MHL instruction can improve adolescent mental health under routine school conditions, offering a practical, scalable strategy for promoting mental health in school systems.Copyright © 2026 The Society for Adolescent Health and Medicine. title: The Exposome and Its Impact on Health and Disease.
abstract: The exposome, a term introduced by Christopher Wild, refers to all environmental exposures affecting an individual from conception onward. It was later conceptually divided into 3 partially overlapping domains, according to the nature and origin of exposures. Since its initial definition, the exposome has attracted increasing scientific interest, and mounting evidence has correlated it to a wide range of diseases, establishing that disease development consists of an intricate interplay between the endogenous-genomic background and the environment. In this review, we introduce the concept as well as elements and importance of the exposome, examine the methodologic approaches that are being employed in exposomics research, discuss challenges related to its study, and report several global exposome-related initiatives and their goals. It is increasingly clear that exposures significantly influence disease, highlighting the need for exposome research to match the scope and rigor of the Human Genome Project. This approach could help us better understand how the environment affects health, fully realize the exposome's potential in medical science, and advance the development of sophisticated, personalized medicine.Copyright © 2026 Mayo Foundation for Medical Education and Research. title: A pivotal Phase 2 study of derazantinib for previously-treated, locally advanced or metastatic cholangiocarcinoma with FGFR2 aberrations: FIDES-01.
abstract: To evaluate safety and efficacy of FGFR1-3 kinase inhibitor derazantinib, in advanced intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) harboring FGFR2 fusions or rearrangements (FGFR2F), mutations (FGFR2M), or amplifications (FGFR2A), previously treated with chemotherapy.Open-label, non-controlled Phase 2 trial. Patients with advanced iCCA, ≥1 prior chemotherapy, and FGFR2F (Substudy 1) or FGFR2M/FGFRA (Substudy 2), received once-daily oral derazantinib 300 mg until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, consent withdrawal or investigator decision to stop. Efficacy was assessed by central radiology review using RECIST v1.1. Primary endpoints were objective response rate (ORR; Substudy 1) and 3-month progression-free survival (PFS3; Substudy 2). Other endpoints were PFS, ORR (Substudy 2), disease control rate (DCR), duration of response (DOR), and overall survival (OS). In Substudy 1, ORR and DCR were 22.3% (23/103 partial responses) and 75.7%, respectively; median (95% CI) PFS was 8.1 (5.5,8.3) months, DOR was 6.5 (4.6,9.2) months, and OS was 17.2 (12.5,22.4) months. In Substudy 2, PFS3 was 63% (27/43), ORR was 9.3% (3 partial, 1 complete response), DCR was 69.8%, and OS was 11.9 (8.4,15.9) months. There were no Grade 4 or 5 drug-related events. FGFR inhibitor class-specific toxicities included drug-related hyperphosphataemia (38%, Grade 3: 3%) and dry eye (36%). title: Comparative plaque- and liquid-based phage susceptibility testing of Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates in a cystic fibrosis randomized clinical trial.
abstract: The optimal phage susceptibility testing (PST) method is unclear. Here, two PST methods were compared using Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates recovered from patients with cystic fibrosis enrolled in a placebo-controlled clinical trial of a single intravenous dose of a four-phage cocktail (WRAIR-PAM-CF1). In total, 508 P. aeruginosa sputum isolates were evaluated, including isolates collected before or after phage or placebo treatment, isolates from the same trial participants over time, and isolates of different colony morphologies from the same participants at the same time point. Susceptibility to phages PaWRA01Φ11, PaWRA01Φ39, PaWRA02Φ83, and PaWRA02Φ87 and a cocktail of all four phages was assessed using a plaque assay (PA) and a Biolog Omnilog-based liquid assay (LA) with the same bacterial inoculum. A total of 170/508 isolates (33%) and 195/508 isolates (38%) were identified as susceptible to the cocktail by PA and LA, respectively. Among the susceptible isolates, 169/170 (99%; PA) and 187/195 (96%; LA) also tested susceptible to at least one of the four phages in the cocktail. Susceptible percent agreement between the PA and LA ranged from 76% to 100% and non-susceptible percent agreement ranged from 89% to 100% for all phages studied and the cocktail. Phage PaWRA02Φ83 demonstrated the greatest individual activity, with 164/508 (32%) and 188/508 (37%) isolates testing susceptible by PA and LA, respectively. The four-phage cocktail provided numerically broader coverage of P. aeruginosa (i.e., had the highest susceptibility rate) than did any single phage. There was high concordance between PST results by PA and LA.IMPORTANCEStandardization of phage susceptibility testing (PST) methods is essential to support phage therapy trials and any future clinical implementation. There are no standardized PST methods or interpretive criteria for PST. In this study, PST was performed by a plaque assay and a Biolog Omnilog-based liquid assay on Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates recovered from cystic fibrosis patients enrolled in a clinical trial. Susceptibility of 508 isolates to four phages and a cocktail of all four was evaluated. There was high concordance between susceptibility assessed by plaque and liquid assays and numerically broader coverage of P. aeruginosa by the cocktail compared to any single phage. This manuscript should be of interest to those performing PST.

title: Minimally invasive versus open liver resection for hepatocellular carcinoma in older adults: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: As the population ages, an increasing number of older adults are diagnosed with resectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Although minimally invasive liver resection (MILR) has shown perioperative advantages, its safety and efficacy in older patients are not fully established. This meta-analysis evaluated the outcomes of MILR compared to open liver resection (OLR) in older adults (≥ 65 years) with HCC.A search was conducted in Medline, Embase, CINAHL, and The Cochrane Library from their inception until November 20, 2025. The review adhered to PRISMA guidelines and was prospectively registered on PROSPERO (CRD420251239665).Fourteen retrospective studies comprising 3,092 older adults were included (1,367 MILR, 1,725 OLR). MILR was associated with lower overall (odds ratio [OR] = 0.47; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.38-0.58; I² = 0%) and major complications (OR = 0.61; 95% CI 0.45-0.83; I² = 15%). However, no statistically significant difference was detected in 90-day mortality (OR = 0.75; 95% CI 0.41-1.38; I² = 0%), disease-free survival (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.83; 95% CI 0.60-1.15; I² = 72%), or overall survival (HR = 0.80; 95% CI 0.56-1.16; I² = 80%).In selected older adults with HCC, MILR was associated with fewer perioperative complications than OLR, while no statistically significant difference was detected in 90-day mortality or long-term survival. Residual confounding, predominance of minor resections, absence of validated frailty assessment, and limited octogenarian data preclude causal inference or confirmation that the association persists with advancing age.

title: Population Genetic Screening of Hemoglobinopathy Carrier Prevalence Compared to Medical Records.
abstract: To better understand the gap between hemoglobinopathy (HBP) prevalence and that which is documented in electronic medical records (EMRs) to quantify genetic HBP carrier prevalence compared to case counts documented in the EMR.We used genetic data from the Tapestry study to quantify the prevalence of HBPs and carrier traits, targeting sickle cell disease and β-thalassemia. Genetic findings were compared with International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision (ICD-10) codes for hemoglobinopathies (D56 for β-thalassemia and D57 for SCD).A total of 50,008 participants were included in the genetic analysis. Twelve participants with diagnosis codes for α-thalassemia and sickle cell disease were previously confirmed with genetic results leaving 49,996 individuals. Of those, 116 participants' (0.23%) genetic testing demonstrated heterozygosity for sickle cell trait, and a majority self-reported Black ancestry (75%). Most (n=97 of 116) did not carry a sickle cell ICD-10 diagnosis code. There were 98 (0.20%) participant carriers for β-thalassemia with White ancestry most common (80.6%), followed by Asian ancestry (15.3%). Only 47 (48.0%) had a β-thalassemia ICD-10 diagnosis code.Our findings demonstrate that sickle cell and β-thalassemia carrier traits are prevalent at clinically significant levels and are substantially under-represented in EMRs. This gap raises important public health concerns, as under-identification may lead to missed opportunities for early diagnosis, reproductive counseling, and preventive care. These results highlight the need for enhanced public health efforts and primary care engagement to improve detection and equitable management of hemoglobinopathies.Copyright © 2026 Mayo Foundation for Medical Education and Research. title: Vaccines, Bias, and the Perils of Non-peer-reviewed Studies: Fueling Misinformation and Vaccine Hesitancy.
abstract: Unvetted scientific claims about vaccines can spread rapidly and undermine decades of progress in immunization and public trust. A recent non-peer-reviewed analysis, promoted at political hearings, in the documentary "An Inconvenient Study," and on social media, has been used to suggest that vaccinated children experience higher rates of chronic illness than unvaccinated peers. Despite standard regression models, critical flaws - uncontrolled confounding, exposure misclassification, unequal follow-up, and outcome multiplicity, invalidate causal inference. An independent group of international experts critically appraises this analysis and contrast its claims with the consistent evidence confirming vaccine safety and effectiveness. We also show how poorly designed studies can distort public discourse, amplify misinformation, and fuel vaccine hesitancy. We outline actions to strengthen research integrity, such as transparent data sharing, labeling of non-peer-reviewed content, and evidence-based communication. Safeguarding public health demands that vaccine evidence be methodologically sound, reviewed, and interpreted by qualified experts.© The Author(s) 2026. title: The fallibility of the T6 neurological level of injury for determining autonomic dysreflexia risk.
abstract: The T6 neurological level of spinal cord injury (SCI) is classically taught as differentiating who is and is not at risk for autonomic dysreflexia (AD); yet the reliability of this metric has rarely been tested.To determine how often individuals with SCI above and below the T6 neurological level of injury (NLI) experience symptomatic AD, quantify AD in the autonomic physiology laboratory, and describe underlying mechanisms that clinically manifest.Cross-sectional.Academic medical center.138 individuals with/without SCI.Not applicable.Symptoms of AD were quantified using the validated Autonomic Dysfunction Following SCI-AD survey. Deep autonomic physiology characterization was further completed (n = 34 uninjured controls, n = 28 individuals with SCI) to identify underlying AD mechanisms. Continuous blood pressure, heart rate, regional vascular resistance in the arm/leg, and pre/posttest catecholamines were recorded. Vascular responsiveness and baroreflex sensitivity were assessed with intravenous phenylephrine boluses. Foot cold pressor and bladder pressor tests served as below level mild noxious stimuli to elicit controlled AD.AD symptoms were, as expected, significantly higher after SCI compared to uninjured controls (p < .001). Symptomatic AD was identified in 77% of individuals with SCI at/above T6, compared to 38% with injuries below T6. McNemar's statistic indicated the T6 neurological level poorly differentiated who developed symptomatic AD (p = .039). During laboratory testing, 57% of those with SCI at/above T6 experienced AD, as did 57% of those with injuries below T6 (p = .33). Physiologically, AD in individuals with SCI below T6 can be due to heightened vascular responsiveness and poor baroreflex sensitivity, leading to minimal compensatory bradycardia.Symptomatic and objective AD occurs in those with SCI above and below the T6 NLI threshold. As such, targeted autonomic testing must translate to the bedside to accurately quantify AD risk. In the interim, though the T6 threshold has become cannon in many patient and resident education materials regarding AD risk, evidence suggests clinical care should avoid using this strict cutoff.© 2026 American Academy of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether the T6 spinal level—a traditional cutoff used to predict who develops autonomic dysreflexia, a dangerous sudden blood pressure spike after spinal cord injury—actually reliably identifies at-risk patients. They found that autonomic dysreflexia occurred in similar rates among people with injuries above and below T6, suggesting this threshold poorly predicts who will experience the condition. The findings indicate that doctors should use more targeted testing rather than relying on this single anatomical marker to assess individual risk.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers examined 138 individuals with and without spinal cord injury (SCI) in a cross-sectional study to evaluate whether the T6 neurological level of injury reliably predicts autonomic dysreflexia (AD) risk, using validated symptom surveys and deep autonomic physiology characterization including continuous blood pressure monitoring, vascular resistance measurement, catecholamine quantification, and controlled noxious stimuli testing. Symptomatic AD occurred in 77% of individuals with SCI at or above T6 compared to 38% below T6, yet McNemar's statistic indicated the T6 threshold poorly differentiated who developed symptomatic AD. During laboratory testing, AD was observed in 57% of those with SCI at or above T6 and 57% of those below T6, with no significant difference between groups. In individuals with SCI below T6, AD physiology was associated with heightened vascular responsiveness and impaired baroreflex sensitivity that produced minimal compensatory bradycardia. The findings indicate that symptomatic and objective AD occurs across the T6 neurological level threshold, suggesting that clinical care should.

title: Prediction of All-Cause Mortality, Cardiovascular Mortality, and Angiographic Coronary Disease From LVEF Reserve: Findings From the Multicenter REFINE PET Registry.
abstract: Left ventricular ejection fraction reserve (LVEF-R), defined as stress EF minus rest EF, is a marker for high-risk coronary artery disease in patients undergoing positron emission tomography myocardial perfusion imaging, but its prognostic and diagnostic significance in large real-world populations remains incompletely defined. We aimed to analyze the association of LVEF-R with mortality and high-risk obstructive coronary artery disease in a large multicenter cohort.We analyzed 34 976 patients from 13 sites who underwent gated rest and vasodilator stress positron emission tomography myocardial perfusion imaging from the Registry of Flow and Perfusion Imaging for Artificial Intelligence with PET. Associations between LVEF-R and all-cause mortality and cardiovascular death were assessed using multivariable Cox regression models. Over a median follow-up of 4.1 years, lower LVEF-R demonstrated a graded association with higher mortality. Compared with LVEF-R>5%, adjusted hazard ratios for all-cause mortality were 1.20 for LVEF-R 0% to 5% ([95% CI, 1.13-1.28]; P<0.001), 1.32 for -5% to 0% ([95% CI, 1.23-1.42]; P<0.001), and 1.38 for ≤-5% ([95% CI, 1.24-1.52]; P<0.001). A negative LVEF-R identifies patients with a higher likelihood of multivessel or left-main coronary artery disease, supporting its role as a clinically relevant marker of high-risk disease.

title: Surgeon Ergonomics of Lateral Lumbar Interbody Fusion Across Four Patient Positions: A Proof-of-Concept Simulation Study Using Motion Capture and Electromyography.
abstract: Study DesignProof-of-concept simulation-based biomechanical pilot study.ObjectivesTo compare surgeon posture and muscle activity across four lateral lumbar interbody fusion (LLIF) positions and rank them by overall ergonomic burden.MethodsFive right-handed spine surgeons (case volumes 15 to 500 or more) each simulated a single-level LLIF on a synthetic model in four positions, three using direct vision (lateral decubitus, prone seated, prone lateral) and one using a camera and monitor (prone camera). Whole-body motion capture and surface EMG were recorded simultaneously, analyzed by surgical phase, and summarized per surgeon.ResultsNeck-flexion intensity was greatest in lateral decubitus and lower in every prone position, with the same ranking in all five surgeons (exact Friedman p=3.0e-06, Kendall W=1.00). Arm elevation was highest in prone seated. Across four summaries of posture and muscle activity, prone camera was the most favorable position in every surgeon, while the others reordered by measure. All positions scored medium-to-high risk. No two-position comparison reached adjusted significance, as expected at this sample size.ConclusionsPatient position in LLIF does not appear to change patient outcome, but it changes what the operation costs the surgeon. Lateral decubitus loaded the neck in every surgeon regardless of case volume or preference, prone seated loaded the shoulder, and prone camera was most favorable overall. Surgeons can reduce their exposure through position and setup, and ergonomics offers an objective way to compare setups when patient outcomes cannot separate them. These are proof-of-concept findings in five surgeons and require confirmation in a larger sample.

title: Optimizing Clinical Education: A Level-of-Learner Placement Model for Academic-Practice Partnerships.
abstract: Clinical education helps prelicensure undergraduate nursing students link theory to practice, develop clinical judgment, and build professional identity. Increasing enrollment, workforce demands, and limited placement capacity require clinical education models that intentionally match learner readiness with unit readiness.Standard placement processes may fail to align learner readiness, course expectations, and unit readiness, resulting in uneven learning experiences and increased burden for faculty, clinical nurse teachers, preceptors, and unit staff.This article describes the Level of Learner Clinical Placement Model for prelicensure nursing students across early, intermediate, and advanced points in the curriculum. The model may be applied in a Dedicated Education Unit, preceptorship, hybrid, observation, and faculty-led placements; it is not limited to Dedicated Education Unit settings.The model provides the overall conceptual structure for academic-practice partners, clarifies expectations for unit staff through related tools, and supports intentional progression toward practice readiness.Copyright © 2026 Wolters Kluwer Health, LLC. llm_summary: Researchers developed a clinical placement model to better match nursing students at different stages of their education with hospital units suited to their skill level and learning needs. The Level of Learner Clinical Placement Model organizes students into early, intermediate, and advanced categories and can be used across various clinical settings to clarify expectations and support progression toward becoming a practicing nurse. This approach aims to improve learning experiences and reduce burden on faculty and hospital staff by intentionally aligning student readiness with unit capacity.
llm_summary_expert: Clinical education researchers developed the Level of Learner Clinical Placement Model to intentionally match prelicensure undergraduate nursing students' readiness with unit capacity across early, intermediate, and advanced curriculum points. The model provides a conceptual framework applicable across multiple placement types including Dedicated Education Units, preceptorships, hybrid models, observation-based, and faculty-led settings. Standard placement processes were identified as potentially misaligning learner readiness with course expectations and unit readiness, thereby creating uneven learning experiences and increased burden on faculty, clinical nurse teachers, preceptors, and unit staff. The proposed model clarifies expectations for unit staff through related tools and supports intentional progression toward practice readiness while addressing constraints from increasing enrollment, workforce demands, and limited placement capacity. The abstract does not report quantitative outcome data, comparative effectiveness results, or empirical validation of the model's impact on student learning or clinical outcomes.

title: AI-Assisted Lung Segmentation for Lung Transplant Volumetry: Effect of Radiation Dose Reduction.
abstract: Accurate lung volumetry is essential for donor-recipient size matching in lung transplantation. This study evaluated the impact of radiation dose reduction on the robustness of AI-based whole-lung segmentation, 5-lobe segmentation, and automated tissue classification.Fifty cases from the Cancer Image Archive (TCIA) Low-dose CT Image and Projection Data set were analyzed. A reduced-dose data set at 10% of the routine dose for each case was generated using validated projection-domain noise insertion. Whole-lung and 5-lobe segmentation were performed using the Lung CT Segmenter module with the lungmask deep learning model in 3D Slicer. Segmentation accuracy was quantified using the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), 95th percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95), and maximum Hausdorff distance (HDmax). Automated tissue classification and volumetry were performed using the Lung CT Analyzer module.Whole-lung segmentation demonstrated excellent consistency between full-dose and 10% dose images (mean DSC 0.997±0.002, HD95 0.73±0.26 mm). In contrast, 5-lobe segmentation showed substantially lower accuracy and greater variability, even at routine dose. Automated tissue classification revealed a mean decrease in functional (inflated) lung volume of 17.12%±5.69% in the right lung and 17.15%±5.56% in the left lung, accompanied by marked increases in emphysema, infiltrated, and collapsed volumes.AI-based whole-lung segmentation remains highly accurate at 10% of the routine dose, supporting its potential for lung transplant volumetry. However, tissue classification and 5-lobe segmentation exhibited notable degradation, highlighting limitations of existing tools at ultra-low dose levels.Copyright © 2026 Wolters Kluwer Health, LLC. title: Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion Versus Oral Anticoagulation in Atrial Fibrillation: A Comprehensive Evidence Synthesis.
abstract: Oral anticoagulation (OAC) remains the cornerstone of stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation (AF) but is limited by bleeding risk. Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) devices offer an alternative; however, recent randomized trials have reported inconsistent efficacy compared with OAC.We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing LAAO with OAC through April 1, 2026, using MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Cochrane CENTRAL. Eligible studies enrolled adults (≥18 years) with AF randomized to LAAO or OAC. Primary and secondary outcomes were pooled as risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Individual patient-level data (IPD) were reconstructed from published Kaplan-Meier curves for time-to-event sensitivity analyses.Six RCTs (n = 7,004; mean age 72 years; CHA2DS2‑VASc 3.9; HAS‑BLED 1.7; mean follow-up 38 months) were included. LAAO showed no significant difference in ischemic stroke (RR 1.20, 95% CI 0.82-1.76), major bleeding (RR 0.77, 95% CI 0.50-1.17), or all-cause mortality (RR 0.96, 95% CI 0.82-1.13) compared with OAC. Hemorrhagic stroke risk was significantly lower with LAAO (RR 0.53, 95% CI 0.30-0.93). Reconstructed IPD demonstrated similar stroke and bleeding risks (HR 1.24 and 0.84, respectively) but lower all-cause mortality with LAAO (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.52-0.95).LAAO provides comparable ischemic stroke prevention and major bleeding outcomes to OAC and reduces hemorrhagic stroke risk. Reconstructed IPD analyses suggest a possible mortality benefit that warrants further investigation. Future studies using contemporary devices and post-ablation populations are needed to refine patient selection and further characterize the comparative clinical outcomes of LAAO and OAC in AF patients.© 2026 Wiley Periodicals LLC.

title: Snare-Assisted Retrieval of a Mechanically Locked-Open TEER Device: A Novel Bailout Technique.
abstract: Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) is an established intervention for patients having severe mitral regurgitation (MR) with prohibitive surgical risk. Complications during deployment related to device malfunction are uncommon but necessitate prompt decision-making and management. A 54-year-old gentleman with dilated cardiomyopathy, severe left ventricular dysfunction, and severe MR underwent TEER using the MyClip system (Meril Life Sciences Pvt. Ltd., Vapi, Gujarat, India). Initial deployment across the A2-P2 scallops of mitral leaflets achieved partial MR reduction. Significant residual MR required a second clip for optimal leaflet coaptation. While deploying the second clip, it failed to close because of a mechanical locking failure. So, we everted the clip, pulled back to LA, and it stayed in open position and failed to close. We report a novel bailout snare technique that enabled safe retrieval without the need for a second transseptal puncture. The ability to close the clip arms prior to withdrawal minimized the risk of tearing the atrial septum and facilitated the successful completion of the TEER procedure. Another clip was deployed successfully, resulting in significant MR reduction. This case demonstrates a rare complication during deployment, a malfunction of the device, and a novel strategy for safely bailing out a challenging intra-procedural complication.© 2026 Wiley Periodicals LLC.

The medical team developed a novel rescue technique using a snare device to safely retrieve the malfunctioning clip without requiring additional punctures, allowing them to successfully place another clip and complete the procedure. This case demonstrates both a rare complication during valve repair and an effective bailout strategy for managing device malfunctions.

During deployment of a second clip intended to optimize leaflet coaptation, mechanical locking failure occurred, leaving the device locked in an open position within the left atrium. The authors developed a novel snare-assisted bailout technique that enabled safe retrieval of the malfunctioning clip without requiring a second transseptal puncture. The ability to close the clip arms prior to withdrawal using the snare minimized the risk of atrial septal tearing and allowed successful completion of the procedure with deployment of an alternative clip. This case report demonstrates a rare device malfunction complication during TEER and presents a novel retrieval strategy for managing this challenging intra-procedural scenario.

title: Global Burden of Anorexia Nervosa and Bulimia Nervosa, 1990 to 2023, With Forecasts to 2050: A Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 Analysis.
abstract: Eating disorders are a major cause of nonfatal mental health burden, yet global evidence on their long-term trends, geographic distribution, and future trajectories remains limited.To estimate the global, regional, and national prevalence and disability burden of anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa-and mortality attributable to anorexia nervosa-from 1990 to 2023, and to forecast prevalence to 2050.Using Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 methods, data were synthesized from systematic literature reviews, population surveys, and vital registration systems. Estimates were produced for 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2023, with forecasts through 2050. These data were analyzed from October 2025 to August 2026.Anorexia nervosa or bulimia nervosa diagnosis.Counts and age-standardized rates with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs) for anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa prevalence, years lived with disability (YLDs), and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs), and anorexia nervosa mortality, reported by age, sex, and location.In 2023, an estimated 18.1 million people (95% UI, 13.9-24.0) globally were living with anorexia nervosa or bulimia nervosa, of whom 12.6 million (69.4%) were female, 5.5 million were male (30.6%), and 41.2% were aged 10 to 24 years. These cases accounted for 3.83 million DALYs (95% UI, 2.23-5.69). Since 1990, the global number of prevalent cases increased by 71.0%, while age-standardized prevalence and DALY rates rose by about 21%. Females experienced substantially higher prevalence and DALY rates than males. The highest age-standardized prevalence rates were observed in high-income regions, particularly Australasia and Western Europe, whereas the largest relative increases in age-standardized prevalence occurred in East Asia, South Asia, and Southeast Asia. Forecasts indicate continued increases in prevalent cases through 2050.This GBD 2023 analysis found that anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa contribute substantially to global nonfatal health loss. These findings support the integration of eating disorders into mental health surveillance, prevention, and service planning worldwide.

llm_summary: Researchers examined global trends in anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa from 1990 to 2023, finding that approximately 18 million people worldwide were living with these eating disorders in 2023, with cases increasing by 71 percent since 1990. Women accounted for nearly 70 percent of cases, and young people aged 10 to 24 represented 41 percent of those affected, with the highest rates occurring in wealthy regions like Western Europe and Australia. The study projects that the number of people with these eating disorders will continue to rise through 2050, highlighting the need for improved mental health services and prevention efforts globally.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers used Global Burden of Disease 2023 methods to synthesize data from systematic literature reviews, population surveys, and vital registration systems across 204 countries and territories to estimate the prevalence, disability burden, and mortality of anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa from 1990 to 2023, with forecasts through 2050. In 2023, an estimated 18.1 million people globally were living with anorexia nervosa or bulimia nervosa (69.4% female), accounting for 3.83 million disability-adjusted life-years, with 41.2% of cases occurring in individuals aged 10 to 24 years. Since 1990, the global number of prevalent cases increased by 71.0%, while age-standardized prevalence and disability-adjusted life-year rates rose by approximately 21%, with substantially higher rates observed in females compared to males. The highest age-standardized prevalence rates were observed in high-income regions including Australasia and Western Europe, whereas the largest relative increases in age-standardized prevalence occurred in East Asia, South Asia, and Southeast Asia.

title: Reimagining U.S. medicine's professionalism movement: institutional professionalism and medicine's collective identity crisis.
abstract: U.S. medicine's modern-day professionalism movement is approaching its third decade. Within this movement and across a broad array of initiatives, medicine has recast issues of professionalism from a more macro-level and sociological focus on the profession to a more micro-level and individual-oriented focus on professionals. In this commentary, the authors adopt a historical lens and briefly outline the movement to date before recommending a shift from professionalism's current focus on the individual to a more macro- and institutional-level framing. In doing so, the authors seek to redirect the focus of prevailing professionalism discussions from professionals to the profession as they argue for a more sociological emphasis on the issue of medical work and its control as opposed to an emphasis on the values, motives, behaviors, and competencies of individual physicians and trainees. To better respond to contemporary professionalism challenges, the authors introduce a new concept-institutional professionalism-and identify 3 foci in arguing for placing a greater emphasis on the profession rather than the individual: (1) semantics, (2) theory (including the deployment of sociological constructs such as organizational fields and institutional logics), and (3) a more layered micro- (individual), meso- (organizational), and macro-level (institutional) understanding of medical work. The authors argue that professionalism, as the countervailing logic to those of managerialism and commercialism, will cease to functionally exist unless medicine responds in a more collective and institutional-level fashion to current encroachments on its work. A failure to do so will leave behind a conceptually isolated and hollowed-out profession that retains the language of professionalism while losing the institutional conditions needed to support it.© The Author(s) 2026. title: State-of-the-Art Review: Native Joint Septic Arthritis Epidemiology, Pathogenesis, Microbiology, Diagnosis, Management, and Outcomes.
abstract: Native joint septic arthritis (NJSA) is a time-sensitive orthopedic and infectious diseases emergency associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, and long-term functional impairment. This State-of-the-Art Review synthesizes current evidence on NJSA epidemiology with a primary focus on bacterial etiologies, risk factors, pathogenesis, microbiology, clinical presentation, and diagnostic challenges, including the absence of validated diagnostic criteria and limitations of culture-based evaluation. We summarize current diagnostic approaches with a focus on synovial fluid interpretation and the expanding role of molecular diagnostics. Management principles emphasize timely surgical source control, appropriate antimicrobial therapy, and coordinated multidisciplinary care. Outcomes are reviewed through the lens of relapse, reinfection, and functional recovery, highlighting the influence of host factors, joint involvement, and timeliness of intervention. Finally, we identify persistent gaps in evidence including optimal surgical timing, treatment duration, oral transition, clinical utility of emerging diagnostics, and outline research priorities to improve NJSA care and outcomes.© The Author(s) 2026.
