title: Diagnostic approach and management strategy for patients with exertional rhabdomyolysis - Results from an international survey of healthcare professionals.
abstract: BackgroundRhabdomyolysis is a complex and potentially life-threatening syndrome characterized by the rapid breakdown of damaged skeletal muscle. Despite its clinical significance, universally accepted diagnostic criteria and standardized management guidelines are lacking.MethodsA cross-sectional online survey about the current diagnostic approach, assessment of risk factors and severity, and management of follow-up of rhabdomyolysis was conducted among clinicians across Europe, Australia, and the USA.ResultsFifty-four respondents from 16 countries completed the survey. Results revealed considerable variability in hospital admission practices, and patient follow-up. Some agreement was found in the frequent use of genetic and neurophysiological testing in as diagnostic tools. The survey revealed no consensus on which CK-level would be considered cut-off levels for rhabdomyolysis.ConclusionsThe survey found little to no coherent approach to diagnosing, assessment of severity, nor follow-up of rhabdomyolysis among respondents who were primarily neurologists and pediatric neurologists. It highlights the need for international guidelines in the diagnostic process, treatment and follow-up of rhabdomyolysis as well as a universally agreed definition of rhabdomyolysis.

The survey found major differences in how doctors decide when to admit patients to the hospital, what blood test results they use to confirm the diagnosis, and how they follow up with patients afterward. The results suggest that doctors need to agree on common standards for diagnosing this condition and managing patient care.

title: Nationwide Trends in Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy Utilization for Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma From 2012 to 2021.
abstract: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) is increasingly recommended in recent years to treat pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PDAC), even those tumors that are upfront resectable. Utilization across different hospital systems based on patient factors, tumor location, and tumor stage is not clear. We aimed to evaluate changes in NAC use for PDAC over the past decade using a nationwide cancer database.The National Cancer Database was queried for patients with stage I-III PDAC treated with surgery between 2012 and 2021. Patients were only included if they were documented to have chemotherapy at any point before or after surgery. Multivariable logistic regression controlling for patient clinical and demographic characteristics evaluated associations with NAC use.During the study period, 28,458 patients were treated with NAC and surgery or surgery and adjuvant chemotherapy. The percentage of all patients receiving NAC significantly increased year after year from 28% in 2012 to 65% in 2021 (P < 0.001). A significant increase in NAC was seen for patients when stratified by type of surgical resection (pancreatoduodenectomy, total pancreatectomy, or distal pancreatectomy; P < 0.001, all). A significant increase in NAC for stage I and II PDAC was noted during the study period (P < 0.01) but not for stage III (P > 0.05). This increase in NAC for stage I and II PDAC patients was similarly noted when stratified by surgery type (P < 0.001, all). Patients receiving care at an academic research facility had a higher proportion of patients undergoing NAC compared to those seen at a comprehensive community facility (51% versus 37%, P < 0.001). A multivariable logistic regression model demonstrated that younger age, Charlson-Deyo Score three or higher, non-Spanish Hispanic ethnicity, receipt of care at academic research facility, patients in a rural or urban location (versus metro), positive lymph nodes, and higher tumor T stage were independent predictors of NAC use (P < 0.05, all). Patients without insurance, poor grade, and tumors in the tail of the pancreas were likewise significantly less likely to receive NAC (P < 0.05, all).NAC use has significantly increased in the past 10 y, especially for stage I and II tumors. NAC has increased for all types of pancreas resection for PDAC. Key patient, tumor, and location differences determine whether or not a patient is treated with NAC.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: The characteristics of perivascular proinflammation in 4-repeat tauopathies.
abstract: Progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) and corticobasal degeneration (CBD) are both neurodegenerative diseases characterized by aggregates composed of 4-repeat (4R) tau protein. They have distinct neuropathological features and classic clinical symptoms; however, the signs and symptoms overlap across the two syndromes. Accumulating evidence suggests that dysregulated immune response is a major contributing factor to neurodegeneration but its role in 4R-tauopathies remains undetermined. The aim is to explore the involvement of neuroinflammation from a vascular perspective in 4R-tauopathies. Autopsies from four controls, three PSP, and three CBD cases were assessed. Samples were obtained from the superior/middle frontal gyrus (S/M-FG) and basal ganglia (BG). Immunofluorescence staining included neuroinflammatory markers: glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), ionized calcium-binding adapter molecule 1 (Iba1), cluster of differentiation 68 (CD68); vascular markers: collagen type IV (ColIV), monocarboxylate transporter-1 (MCT1), and α-smooth muscle actin (αSMA). Maximally projected confocal z-stack images of vasculature were used as a mask to quantify total perivascular GFAP+/Iba1+/CD68+ labeling. GFAP immunoreactivity ratio between MCT1 and αSMA double labeled arteries and veins was quantified to further differentiate venular and arteriolar involvement into proinflammatory activation. Both PSP and CBD had widespread perivascular proinflammatory changes, although greater in CBD. The activated GFAP+ astrocytes and microglia/macrophages in CBD were distributed extensively in S/M-FG and BG, with S/M-FG WM more affected. In PSP, abundant neuroinflammation was found in BG. The involvement of vasculature type was distinct among the two 4R-tauopathies, while CBD showed comparable proinflammatory changes in arterioles and venules, PSP exhibited predominant proinflammation in venules. The regional pattern of perivascular proinflammation differed between PSP and CBD, corresponding to the characteristic affected brain regions. CBD had more severe perivascular proinflammation that involved both arterioles and venules, while venules were more affected in PSP. Perivascular proinflammation may be a critical pathophysiological process in 4R-tauopathies.© 2026 The Author(s). title: Comparing SGLT2 Inhibitors on Incident Major Adverse Kidney Events in Type 2 Diabetes: A Target Trial Emulation.
abstract: To determine whether canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, and empagliflozin differ in rates of major adverse kidney events (MAKE) in adults with T2D at moderate cardiovascular risk and without stage 3+ chronic kidney disease (CKD) at baseline.Using target trial emulation and U.S. claims data from commercial, Medicare Advantage, and traditional Medicare plans, we compared canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, and empagliflozin among adults ≥ 21years with T2D at moderate cardiovascular risk (1-5% annualized MACE or death risk), without insulin use or stage 3+ chronic kidney disease (CKD) at baseline, initiating treatment from January 1, 2014, and December 31, 2021. Propensity scores estimated via super learner ensemble were incorporated as inverse probability weights into Cox models examining major adverse kidney events (MAKE: stage 3+ CKD, kidney failure, kidney replacement therapy initiation) and all-cause death under intention-to-treat analysis through December 31, 2022.The weighted cohort included 41,248, 17,548, and 72,638 adults initiating canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, and empagliflozin, respectively. One-year post-initiation, rates of MAKE were 3.2% in the dapagliflozin and empagliflozin arms and 3.5% in the canagliflozin arm; by three years, 8.4%, 8.5%, and 9.1%. Compared to canagliflozin, MAKE risk was lower with dapagliflozin (HR 0.91; 95%CI 0.85-0.97) and empagliflozin (HR 0.93; 95%CI 0.88-0.97), with no difference between dapagliflozin and empagliflozin.Empagliflozin and dapagliflozin were associated with modestly lower adverse kidney event rates compared to canagliflozin. title: Melanoma risk in astronauts: Clinical screening, surveillance, and the microgravity paradox.
abstract: Astronauts show significantly elevated melanoma incidence and mortality relative to the general population, a finding with direct relevance to an expanding civilian spaceflight population. We conducted a systematic review to characterize this risk and translate it into practical guidance for dermatologists. Of 11 studies meeting eligibility criteria, only one was a human clinical or epidemiological study; the remainder were experimental, and consistently showed that simulated microgravity suppresses melanoma proliferation, adhesion, migration, and invasion while promoting apoptosis through collapse of FAK-RhoA-mTORC1-ERK1/2 mechanotransduction, a laboratory finding in direct tension with the clinical risk observed in astronauts. The majority of astronauts studied were career pilots, an occupational group with an independently established approximately two-fold melanoma incidence and elevated mortality specifically among pilots from cockpit UVA exposure accrued before spaceflight, which we identify as the most clinically substantial explanation for this paradox. We recommend risk-stratified pre-flight total-body skin examination with dermoscopy, deferral of dermatologic management to the ground rather than in-flight, post-flight surveillance after long-duration missions, and individualized counseling that distinguishes career astronauts from the demographically distinct civilian spaceflight population now emerging through missions such as Inspiration4 and Polaris Dawn.Copyright © 2026. title: Pilot Evaluation of Rapid 2D Brain MR Elastography in Idiopathic Normal-Pressure Hydrocephalus.
abstract: MR elastography of the brain provides quantitative biomarkers of mechanical properties of brain tissue. Prior studies have shown that an advanced 3D MRE can differentiate idiopathic normal-pressure hydrocephalus from other neurodegenerative disorders. In this pilot study, we assessed whether a simplified 2D MR elastography protocol, which is more widely available, could detect stiffness differences between patients with idiopathic normal-pressure hydrocephalus and patients with cognitive impairment due to causes other than idiopathic normal-pressure hydrocephalus, thus providing preliminary diagnostic discrimination while using a previously developed 3D MR elastography classifier as a secondary exploratory comparator.In this prospective study, 10 patients with clinically diagnosed idiopathic normal-pressure hydrocephalus and 10 patients with cognitive impairment due to non-idiopathic normal-pressure hydrocephalus causes underwent 2D brain MR elastography between September 2024 and April 2025. Median stiffness was extracted from a standardized, manually defined region of interest at the brain vertex. A previously validated 3D MR elastography pattern-analysis support vector machine classifier was applied to this prospective cohort as a secondary exploratory comparator. Group differences were assessed using Wilcoxon rank sum tests. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis as an exploratory assessment of discrimination.Median stiffness was higher in the group with idiopathic normal-pressure hydrocephalus than the group with non-idiopathic normal-pressure hydrocephalus cognitive impairment (1.62 vs 0.98 kPa; P < .001). Stiffness demonstrated excellent discriminatory ability, yielding an apparent area under the curve of 1.00 with an optimal threshold of 1.43 kPa. The 3D support vector machine decision metric also yielded an apparent area under the curve of 1.00. The pretrained support vector machine model classified 18 of 20 subjects correctly (accuracy: 90.0% [95% CI, 68.3%-98.8%]). Although promising, these performance estimates should be interpreted cautiously given the limited sample size.This study provides preliminary evidence that a 2D MR elastography protocol may help discriminate idiopathic normal-pressure hydrocephalus from other disorders causing cognitive impairment, providing a foundation for larger, multicenter validation studies for assessing reproducibility, generalizability, and potential clinical utility.© 2027 by American Journal of Neuroradiology.

title: Direct Injection of Meningeal Diverticula for Localization of CSF-Venous Fistulas: Technique and Clinical Applications.
abstract: The recognition of CSF-venous fistulas as a cause of spontaneous intracranial hypotension has increased dramatically in recent years, in large part due to the more pervasive use of lateral decubitus myelography. Lateral decubitus positioning is critical for identification of CSF-venous fistulas, because most of these fistulas arise from meningeal diverticula along the nerve root sleeves. These diverticula must be filled with dense contrast to allow for confident visualization of contrast in veins draining CSF-venous fistulas. Even with an excellent technique, decubitus CT or fluoroscopic myelography can fail to detect some CSF-venous fistulas. In this technical report, we describe the use of direct contrast injection into the meningeal diverticula for the identification or further characterization of CSF-venous fistulas. This is a potentially useful problem-solving technique that can increase diagnostic confidence for this sometimes elusive pathology. We have found it useful to both detect CSF-venous fistulas and exquisitely determine their site of origin within meningeal diverticula.© 2027 by American Journal of Neuroradiology.

title: Cardiac mechanical efficiency in patients with cardiogenic shock.
abstract: Cardiogenic shock (CS) is characterized by impaired left ventricular (LV) mechanical performance and adverse remodelling. We evaluated whether transthoracic echocardiography (TTE)-derived modified cardiac efficiency (mCE), integrating stroke work and residual LV volume, is associated with short- and long-term mortality in CS and whether its prognostic value differs by shock aetiology.In this retrospective cohort study, consecutive adults admitted with CS to the cardiac intensive care unit at Mayo Clinic (2007-2018) were included if TTE was performed within 24 h. mCE was calculated as (stroke volume × estimated LV end-systolic pressure) divided by LV end-systolic volume and categorized into quartiles. Primary outcome was in-hospital mortality; secondary outcome was 1-year mortality. Multivariable logistic and Cox models adjusted for illness severity, comorbidity burden, shock aetiology, cardiac arrest, vasoactive therapy, and mechanical circulatory support. Among 667 patients, median mCE was 48 mmHg (IQR 32-74). In-hospital mortality was 28% and increased stepwise across decreasing mCE quartiles. The lowest quartile had a 2.5-fold higher adjusted odds of in-hospital death (OR 2.53; 95%CI: 1.49-4.37; P < 0.001). One-year mortality was 41%; the lowest quartile had a two-fold higher adjusted hazard of death (HR 2.05; 95%CI: 1.45-2.89; P < 0.001). Associations were stronger in acute coronary syndrome-related CS (interaction P = 0.035 for in-hospital; P = 0.015 for 1-year). title: Inflammation in coronary syndromes in clinical practice: a clinical consensus statement of the Association for Acute Cardiovascular Care of the European Society of Cardiology, the European Society of Cardiology Working Group on Myocardial and Pericardial Diseases, the European Society of Cardiology Council on Basic Cardiovascular Science, and the European Society of Cardiology Council for Cardiology Practice.
abstract: Inflammation is a key driver of coronary syndromes across the continuum from chronic coronary syndromes to acute coronary syndromes. It contributes to atherogenesis, plaque destabilization, and ischaemic events and influences myocardial injury, repair, and remodelling. Inflammatory activity is further amplified by metabolic and autoimmune comorbidities such as diabetes, obesity, and connective tissue diseases, with obesity representing a major driver of chronic low-grade inflammation through adipose tissue dysfunction and cytokine activation, while psychosocial stress and environmental exposures including air pollution serve as additional triggers. Genetic variations, including human leucocyte antigen genotypes, modulate individual susceptibility to vascular inflammation and myocardial injury. This expert consensus from the European Society of Cardiology's Association for Acute CardioVascular Care summarizes the current understanding of inflammation across the full spectrum of coronary syndromes, including underlying mechanisms, relevant biomarkers, and imaging approaches that characterize vascular inflammation, and integrates insights from experimental and clinical studies. Importantly, this document provides explicit consensus-based guidance on when, how, and in whom inflammation should be assessed and treated in routine clinical practice. While the causal association between inflammation and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease is well established, pharmacological modification of inflammation has produced conflicting evidence. Some agents, such as low-dose colchicine, have demonstrated modest reductions in cardiovascular events, although results across trials have been inconsistent. Other anti-inflammatory therapies have not shown clinical benefit, whereas selective cytokine inhibition with canakinumab has reduced cardiovascular risk at the cost of increased infection rates. The present manuscript also focuses on the evaluation of inflammatory activity in cardiovascular patients in routine clinical practice. llm_summary: This expert consensus statement examines how inflammation drives heart disease across different stages, from chronic conditions to acute heart attacks, and reviews which treatments might help. Inflammation drives coronary pathology through atherogenesis and plaque destabilization, with amplification by metabolic comorbidities including diabetes and obesity, as well as psychosocial stress and environmental exposures such as air pollution, while genetic variations including human leucocyte antigen genotypes modulate individual susceptibility to vascular inflammation and myocardial injury. Pharmacological modification of inflammation has yielded inconsistent results, with low-dose colchicine demonstrating modest reductions in cardiovascular events across trials, selective cytokine inhibition with canakinumab reducing cardiovascular risk at the cost of increased infection rates, and other anti-inflammatory therapies showing no clinical benefit. title: Brain perivascular macrophages regulate endothelial cell function via a cMAF-dependent transcriptional program in mouse and human.
abstract: Brain perivascular macrophages maintain brain physiology, yet their transcriptional regulators and functions in health and disease remain unclear. Using single-cell multi-omics and functional experiments, we identify cellular musculoaponeurotic fibrosarcoma oncogene (cMAF) as a key transcription factor for brain perivascular macrophages, and conditional deletion of cMAF disrupts their phenotype in vivo. Functionally, cMAF drives insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF1) expression in perivascular macrophages, enabling communication with endothelial cells. Consistently, cMAF deletion in perivascular macrophages causes transcriptional alterations in cerebral arteries, affecting vascular functions. Notably, cMAF emerges as the main transcription factor for human perivascular macrophages, suggesting conservation of this transcriptional module. During Alzheimer's disease (AD), human perivascular macrophages upregulate cMAF and IGF1 to enhance communication with vascular cells, and this response is abrogated in APOE4 carriers. Lastly, we explore an uncharacterized polymorphism in cMAF, providing evidence that the cMAF program is protective against AD. llm_summary: Researchers identified a protein called cMAF that controls specialized immune cells in the brain's blood vessels, which help maintain healthy blood vessel function. When they removed cMAF from these immune cells in mice, the cells lost their normal characteristics and blood vessel function was disrupted. In humans with Alzheimer's disease, these immune cells increased cMAF production to protect blood vessels, but this protective response was weakened in people carrying a specific genetic variant called APOE4.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers used single-cell multi-omics and functional experiments to identify cMAF as a key transcription factor regulating brain perivascular macrophages and their communication with endothelial cells. Conditional deletion of cMAF in perivascular macrophages disrupted their phenotype in vivo and caused transcriptional alterations in cerebral arteries that affected vascular functions. The study found that cMAF drives IGF1 expression in perivascular macrophages, enabling communication with endothelial cells, and this transcriptional module is conserved in human perivascular macrophages. During Alzheimer's disease, human perivascular macrophages upregulate cMAF and IGF1 to enhance vascular communication, but this response is abrogated in APOE4 carriers, and evidence suggests that the cMAF program is protective against Alzheimer's disease. The findings indicate that targeting cMAF in perivascular macrophages may offer new therapeutic strategies for neurodegenerative and cerebrovascular diseases, though the clinical translation of these mechanistic observations requires further investigation.

title: Involuntary Treatment in First-Episode Psychosis and Mania: A Retrospective Population-Based Cohort Study.
abstract: The study aimed to examine how involuntary status at first presentation affects 5-year trajectories of first-episode psychosis or first-episode mania (FEP/FEM).The authors conducted a population-based cohort study on FEP/FEM. Legal status at first episode was classified as involuntary or voluntary. Participants were followed up to 5 years to examine relapse, emergency department use, vocational status, and Social and Occupational Functioning Assessment Scale (SOFAS) scores. Relapse was compared by using log-rank tests; repeated-measures outcomes used mixed-effects models that adjusted for age and sex, with linear, logistic, or negative binomial regression as appropriate.The cohort included 200 individuals (voluntary, N=139; involuntary, N=61). The involuntary group was older than the voluntary group (p<0.001) and had greater illness severity (Clinical Global Impressions-Severity mean=5.5 vs. 5.1, p=0.002) at FEP/FEM. Time to relapse did not differ, nor did emergency department visits or psychiatric hospitalizations. Functioning improved at a similar rate in both groups; however, the involuntary group remained lower in functioning (SOFAS mean difference=-5.9, p=0.007) and had higher odds of being vocationally disengaged throughout follow-up (odds ratio=3.82, p=0.009).The authors found that involuntary treatment at FEP/FEM is common and is characterized by greater baseline illness severity. Involuntary status can serve as an entry point into care without excess long-term service utilization, and both groups showed similar rates of functional improvement. Persistently lower functioning and higher odds of vocational disengagement in the involuntary group support the need for targeted vocational interventions.

title: Organ Donation-Reaching the Next Generation: To and Through High School.
abstract: Current transplant rates meet only 10% of the global demand, and the quintessential reason is the lack of donors. The same holds for blood donations, with the number of younger donors increasingly declining.This project tested the hypothesis that awareness, knowledge, and comfort levels of blood, organ, and bone marrow (BM) donation are low among high school students but can be raised through education.A pre-/post-comparative cohort study was conducted using a 59-item electronic questionnaire administered to students in grades 9, 10, and 11 in a single high school between November 2025 and January 2026 before and after a 10-minute presentation in high school classrooms.A total of 112 students participated (59% females, age 14-17). Awareness level (5-point scale from 1 (very aware) to 5 (not aware)) was moderate-high for organ and blood donation and moderate for BM (median (IQR) 2 (1-3), 2 (1-2) and 3 (2-4), respectively). Notable increases in knowledge pertained to the number of patients on the transplant list (from 55% pre to 83% post, P < .01), the number of organs that can be donated (from 14% to 22%, P < .01), and the volume of blood per blood donation (from 17% to 24%, P < .01). Comfort level (from 1 (very) to 5 (not at all)) was higher for deceased organ donation than for living organ donation and blood donation (median (IQR) 2 (1-3) vs. 3 (2-4) and 3 (3-4), P < .05) and increased for deceased organ and blood donation after the presentation (median (IQR) 1 (1-3) and 2 (1-3), respectively, P < .001 vs. pre).Dedicated peer-to-peer initiatives can raise awareness, knowledge, and comfort levels for blood, organ, and BM donation among high schoolers.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: A Novel Arthroscopic Curette Microphone for Cartilage Defect Preparation in Joint Preservation Surgery: Proof-of-Concept and Tissue-Specific Debridement Audio Features.
abstract: ObjectiveDuring open chondral defect preparation, audible debridement sound changes mark the transition from deep cartilage to the calcified cartilage layer. We developed a novel curette microphone to characterize these audio feature differences during arthroscopic defect preparation.DesignA piezoelectric curette microphone was used to transmit and record debridement sound from 12 defect preparations (6 deep cartilage, 6 CCL) using human osteochondral allograft remnants. Live audio from the device was used to stop each debridement at the intended level, which was verified histologically. Spectrograms and power-spectral density plots were used to describe the audible transition from deep cartilage to CCL. We compared 22 audio features describing loudness, frequency, and complexity between the two tissue levels.ResultsCurette strokes against the deep cartilage were louder, higher frequency, and more acoustically complex than strokes against the CCL (p < 0.001). Cartilage debridement generated acoustically complex frequency bands above 2.5 kHz that diminished upon reaching the CCL. Debridement of the CCL produced a simpler audio profile that was predominant below 350 Hz.ConclusionThe novel curette microphone presented here transmits high-fidelity debridement audio that can be used to accurately distinguish tissue depth based on the distinct audio profiles of the deep cartilage and CCL.

title: Diagnostic challenges in light chain (AL) amyloidosis for high-risk patients.
abstract: Immunoglobulin light-chain (AL) amyloidosis is associated with high early mortality, particularly when the diagnosis occurs after advanced cardiac or multiorgan dysfunction has developed. Existing reviews have addressed diagnosis and management, but the evolving concept of high-risk disease in the modern therapeutic era has received less attention.This review explores how the definition of high-risk AL amyloidosis has evolved, with attention to organ involvement, cardiac biomarkers, clonal characteristics, tissue diagnosis, amyloid typing, multimodality imaging, artificial intelligence (AI)-supported diagnostic tools, multidimensional prognostic models, and novel B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA)-targeted immunotherapies. A focused Mayo Clinic literature search, supplemented by targeted PubMed searches by the authors, prioritized recent studies together with relevant consensus documents and landmark publications.Improving outcomes in AL amyloidosis will depend not only on the development of more potent therapies but also on the ability to deliver them before irreversible organ damage dictates the course of the illness. If advances in artificial intelligence, multimodal diagnostic tools, and highly active immunotherapies can be incorporated into everyday practice, the field may gradually move away from reacting to established high-risk disease and toward preventing patients from reaching that stage.

title: Psychometric validation of the Ru-SATED 4.0 multidimensional sleep health scale in a representative U.S. sample.
abstract: To develop and psychometrically validate a self-report questionnaire assessing multidimensional sleep health among U.S. adults using item response theory (IRT) and classic test theory analyses.The Ru-SATED 4.0 scale evaluates 6 sleep health dimensions (Regularity, Satisfaction, Alertness, Timing, Efficiency, Duration). We assessed the scale's comprehensibility with cognitive interviews (n=23) and Lexile analysis. We administered Ru-SATED and other self-reported measures to an adult sample (N=2,000; 18-89y) from the YouGov.com Internet panel, representative of the U.S. population in terms of age, sex, race/ethnicity, and education. We used factor analysis to identify the best combination of 6 items (1 per dimension); calibrated these using IRT Graded Response Models; and examined associations with validated measures to establish construct validity.Cognitive interviews confirmed comprehensibility of the items and response options. The final 6 items had excellent model fit in factor analysis (RMSEA=0.08, SRMR=0.03, CFI=0.97, TLI=0.95). IRT calibration showed individual items varied in their degree of severity assessed (location parameters) and amount of information contributed (discrimination parameters) to overall test scores (θ values). S. sample of 2,000 adults aged 18-89 years using item response theory and classical test theory analyses. title: Global, Regional, and National Burden of Bone Cancers, 1990 to 2023, With Forecasts to 2050: A Systematic Analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
abstract: Primary bone cancers include multiple histologic types, with survival differing by age and location. Results from the Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study (GBD) 2023 were analyzed to support policies and initiatives worldwide.To estimate the global burden of bone cancer from 1990 to 2023 and forecast future trends to 2050.This systematic analysis estimated bone cancer incidence, mortality, and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) in 204 countries and territories grouped by GBD super-regions and World Bank income groups from 1990 to 2023, with forecasts through 2050. Individuals of all ages with bone cancers included in the GBD 2023 study were included in analyses. Data were analyzed from June 2023 to July 2025.The GBD 2023 study used standardized estimation methods to describe bone cancer incidence, mortality, and DALYs in 2023, as well as trends over the past 3 decades and forecasts through 2050. All estimates are presented with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs), and age-standardized rates (ASRs) were calculated using GBD-specific age weights.In 2023, there were 111 000 (95% UI, 81 300-164 000) malignant bone cancer cases, 76 600 (95% UI, 60 700-96 300) deaths, and 3.02 million (95% UI, 2.29 million-3.96 million) DALYs globally. A bimodal age distribution was noted in both incidence (peaking at ages 10 to 14 years and 65 to 69 years) and mortality (peaking at ages 15 to 19 years and 65 to 69 years). The highest ASRs for incidence were in Southeast Asia, East Asia, and Oceania (1.6 per 100 000; 95% UI, 1.1-2.4), while Sub-Saharan Africa had the highest ASRs for DALYs (51.0 per 100 000; 95% UI, 27.7-79.7). By World Bank income group, upper-middle-income countries had the highest ASRs for incidence, whereas low-income countries exhibited the highest ASRs for both mortality and DALYs. Globally, incident cases, deaths, and DALYs increased from 1990 to 2023, while global mortality and DALY ASRs were relatively stable; high-income countries experienced a decline in mortality and DALY ASRs. Forecasts suggest a potential increase in global cases and deaths by 2050.In this systematic analysis, the burden of bone cancer varied by age, geography, and time, underscoring global disparities. These findings provide valuable insights to inform health system planning and resource allocation tailored to different settings.

llm_summary: Researchers analyzed global data from 1990 to 2023 to understand the burden of bone cancer worldwide, finding approximately 111,000 new cases and 76,600 deaths in 2023, with cases occurring most frequently in children and elderly people. The disease burden varied significantly by region and income level, with low-income countries experiencing the highest death rates despite having fewer total cases. Projections suggest the number of bone cancer cases and deaths may increase by 2050, highlighting the need for better health planning and resource allocation in different parts of the world.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers analyzed data from the Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study 2023 to estimate bone cancer incidence, mortality, and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) across 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2023, with forecasts through 2050. In 2023, there were approximately 111,000 malignant bone cancer cases, 76,600 deaths, and 3.02 million DALYs globally, with a bimodal age distribution peaking in adolescence and older age groups. Age-standardized incidence rates were highest in Southeast Asia, East Asia, and Oceania, while Sub-Saharan Africa had the highest age-standardized DALY rates, and low-income countries exhibited the highest mortality and DALY rates despite upper-middle-income countries having the highest incidence rates. From 1990 to 2023, absolute numbers of incident cases, deaths, and DALYs increased globally, though age-standardized mortality and DALY rates remained relatively stable, with high-income countries experiencing declines in these rates.

title: Diagnostic insights from twenty years of bilateral inferior petrosal sinus sampling for cushing disease at mayo clinic.
abstract: Bilateral inferior petrosal sinus sampling (BIPSS) is used to distinguish pituitary from ectopic sources of ACTH-dependent Cushing syndrome (CS). We reviewed two decades of BIPSS experience at a single referral center to assess diagnostic performance, safety, and patient outcomes.Retrospective cohort study of patients who underwent BIPSS between 1998 and 2018.Of 156 adults undergoing BIPSS for ACTH-dependent CS, 143 had technically successful sampling and adequate follow-up and formed the evaluable cohort. A pituitary source was identified by a baseline central-to-peripheral ACTH ratio ≥2.0 or a post-stimulation (ovine corticotropin-releasing hormone [oCRH] or desmopressin) ratio ≥3.0.Diagnostic sensitivity, specificity, and lateralization accuracy of BIPSS. A confirmed pituitary source was defined by post-operative hypocortisolism after the index transsphenoidal operation; ACTH-positive corticotroph histology was supportive.Of the 143 patients, 109 had a definitive final diagnosis and formed the basis of the diagnostic analysis. BIPSS separated pituitary from ectopic ACTH sources with a sensitivity of 98.9% (95% CI 94.3-99.8) and a specificity of 85.7% (95% CI 60.1-96.0). The inter-petrosal gradient predicted the side of the adenoma in 59% of cases at baseline and 60% after stimulation (n = 100). Technical success was achieved in 94.2% of procedures, with no recorded major morbidity. Among the 94 patients in remission, 14 (15%) recurred over a mean of 3 years.Among patients in whom a definitive diagnosis was ultimately established, BIPSS distinguished pituitary from ectopic ACTH-dependent CS with high sensitivity and more modest specificity. Its value for adenoma lateralization is limited relative to current imaging. The cohort provides an oCRH-era reference point as practice moves to desmopressin.© 2026. llm_summary: Researchers reviewed twenty years of data on a diagnostic test called bilateral inferior petrosal sinus sampling, which helps doctors determine whether abnormal cortisol levels come from a pituitary gland tumor or elsewhere in the body. The test successfully distinguished between these two sources in nearly 99 out of 100 cases, though it was less reliable at pinpointing which side of the pituitary gland the tumor was located on. The procedure was safe with a 94% technical success rate and no major complications reported.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers examined bilateral inferior petrosal sinus sampling (BIPSS) outcomes in 143 adults with technically successful procedures and adequate follow-up who underwent testing between 1998 and 2018 to distinguish pituitary from ectopic sources of ACTH-dependent Cushing syndrome. BIPSS diagnostic performance was assessed using baseline central-to-peripheral ACTH ratios ≥2.0 or post-stimulation ratios ≥3.0 (with ovine corticotropin-releasing hormone or desmopressin), with pituitary source confirmation based on post-operative hypocortisolism or ACTH-positive corticotroph histology. Among 109 patients with definitive final diagnoses, BIPSS demonstrated sensitivity of 98.9% and specificity of 85.7% for distinguishing pituitary from ectopic ACTH sources, with technical success achieved in 94.2% of procedures and no recorded major morbidity. The inter-petrosal gradient predicted adenoma lateralization in approximately 60% of cases after stimulation, and among 94 patients in remission.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Paracentral Acute Middle Maculopathy for Arteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy.
abstract: The purpose of this study was to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of paracentral acute middle maculopathy (PAMM) detected on optical coherence tomography (OCT) macula for differentiating arteritic anterior ischemic neuropathy (AAION) from nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION) in a multicenter United States cohort.Retrospective, multicenter diagnostic accuracy analysis.This study included patients diagnosed with AAION or NAION at the University of Minnesota, Mayo Clinic, and Johns Hopkins Wilmer Eye Institute between January 2020 and January 2025. Inclusion criteria consisted of patients older than 50 years who had obtained OCT macula within 14 days of symptom onset. AAION diagnoses were confirmed by temporal artery biopsy or positron emission tomography/computed tomography.Two masked fellowship-trained neuro-ophthalmologists independently evaluated OCT images for the presence of acute PAMM.Sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV) of PAMM for AAION were calculated.A total of 119 patients were included, consisting of 27 patients with AAION and 92 patients with NAION. PAMM was identified in 18.5% of patients with AAION and 5.4% of patients with NAION (p = 0.032). The sensitivity, specificity, PPV, and NPV of PAMM for AAION was 19% [95% CI: 0.08-0.37], 94.6% [95% CI: 0.88-0.98], 50% [95% CI: 0.24-0.76], and79.8% [95% CI: 0.71-0.86] respectively. Three of five NAION patients with PAMM had provoked NAION associated with severe systemic hypoperfusion.PAMM is a highly specific but insensitive OCT marker for AAION. Although its presence should increase clinical suspicion for AAION, PAMM may rarely occur in patients with NAION particularly in the setting of systemic hypoperfusion and should be interpreted within the overall clinical context.Copyright © 2026. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a specific pattern visible on eye imaging could help distinguish between two types of sudden vision loss caused by blocked blood flow to the optic nerve. They found that while this pattern was present in about one in five arteritic cases compared to one in twenty nonarteritic cases, it was not reliable enough to diagnose the condition on its own. The pattern should raise suspicion for the arteritic form but must be considered alongside other clinical information to avoid misdiagnosis.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers examined the diagnostic accuracy of paracentral acute middle maculopathy (PAMM) on optical coherence tomography for differentiating arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (AAION) from nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION) in a retrospective multicenter cohort of 119 patients older than 50 years who underwent OCT imaging within 14 days of symptom onset, with AAION diagnoses confirmed by temporal artery biopsy or positron emission tomography/computed tomography. Two masked neuro-ophthalmologists independently evaluated OCT macula images for acute PAMM, and sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value were calculated for AAION detection. PAMM was identified in 18.5% of the 27 AAION patients and 5.4% of the 92 NAION patients (p = 0.032), yielding a sensitivity of 19%, specificity of 94.6%, positive predictive value of 50%, and negative predictive value of 79.

title: Respiratory and Gastrointestinal Mycobiome Profiles Identify Distinct Patient Clusters Associated with Asthma Control.
abstract: The human microbiome contributes to asthma pathogenesis, yet most studies have focused on bacterial communities. This pilot study aimed to characterize fungal communities across multiple body sites in adults with asthma and evaluate whether integrated multisite mycobiome profiles are associated with asthma control.We enrolled 24 adults with asthma evaluated at Mayo Clinic between 2020 and 2022. Oral wash, nasal swab, sputum, and stool samples were collected, and fungal communities were characterized using ITS2 sequencing. Multisite mycobiome data were integrated using an unsupervised clustering approach , with a two-cluster solution selected for exploratory clinical comparisons. Clusters were compared with respect to fungal composition, site-specific diversity metrics, and asthma control.Two patient clusters with distinct multisite mycobiome profiles were identified. Cluster 1 demonstrated poorer asthma control, with lower Asthma Control Test scores than Cluster 2 (median [IQR], 15.0 [13.0-17.5] vs. 18.0 [17.0-19.0]; p = 0.040). Compared with Cluster 2, Cluster 1 exhibited a higher relative abundance of Cladosporium in nasal and sputum samples, and greater sputum fungal diversity (p = 0.016). In contrast, Cluster 2 exhibited a higher relative abundance of Candida in stool and sputum samples. No significant differences in fungal diversity were observed in oral, nasal, or stool samples.Integrated multisite mycobiome profiling identified distinct fungal community patterns associated with asthma control, highlighting the need for larger, longitudinal studies to define their clinical relevance.Copyright © 2026. llm_summary: Researchers examined fungal communities from multiple body sites in 24 adults with asthma to determine whether distinct fungal patterns were associated with asthma control. They identified two patient groups with different fungal profiles, with one group showing significantly worse asthma control and higher levels of a fungus called Cladosporium in nasal and lung samples. The findings suggest that fungal communities may relate to asthma control, though larger studies are needed to confirm this connection.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers examined fungal communities across respiratory and gastrointestinal sites in 24 adults with asthma using ITS2 sequencing of oral, nasal, sputum, and stool samples, followed by unsupervised clustering to identify multisite mycobiome patterns. Integrated mycobiome profiling identified two distinct patient clusters with different fungal compositions, where Cluster 1 showed higher relative abundance of Cladosporium in nasal and sputum samples and greater sputum fungal diversity compared to Cluster 2, which exhibited higher Candida abundance in stool and sputum. Cluster 1 demonstrated significantly poorer asthma control with a median Asthma Control Test score of 15.0 compared to 18.0 in Cluster 2 (p = 0.040). No significant differences in fungal diversity were observed in oral, nasal, or stool samples between clusters. The authors conclude that distinct multisite mycobiome profiles are associated with asthma control status, though larger longitudinal studies are needed to establish the clinical relevance of these fungal community patterns.

title: 52-Week Safety and Disease Control With Ruxolitinib Cream in Children Aged 2 to 11 Years With Atopic Dermatitis: Results From the Phase 3 TRuE-AD3 Study.
abstract: Ruxolitinib (selective Janus kinase [JAK]1/JAK2 inhibitor) cream demonstrated efficacy and safety vs vehicle during 8 weeks of continuous use in a phase 3 study of children with atopic dermatitis (AD).To evaluate long-term safety (LTS) and disease control with as-needed ruxolitinib cream use in children.Children aged 2-11 years with mild-to-moderate AD initially randomized to ruxolitinib cream (0.75% or 1.5%) in the 8-week study continued the same twice-daily (BID) regimen for an additional 44 weeks but only applied cream as needed BID; patients initially on vehicle were rerandomized (1:1) to apply either ruxolitinib cream strength as needed. Safety and disease control were assessed.No new safety signals emerged among children who applied ruxolitinib cream in the LTS period (N=282). Application site reactions were infrequent (1.1%), and no serious treatment-related adverse events were observed. Among patients initially randomized to ruxolitinib cream (0.75%/1.5%), disease control was maintained to Week 52 (Investigator's Global Assessment score 0/1, 79.5%/72.3%; affected body surface area, 2.0%/1.9%).No vehicle control in LTS period.Ruxolitinib cream applied as needed over 44 weeks was well tolerated and demonstrated disease control in children aged 2-11 years, consistent with findings in adolescents and adults.Copyright © 2026. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether ruxolitinib cream, a medication that reduces skin inflammation, remained safe and effective when children aged 2 to 11 years with atopic dermatitis used it as needed over 44 additional weeks. The cream was well tolerated with few side effects, and most children maintained clear or nearly clear skin through 52 weeks of treatment. However, the study lacked a comparison group during the longer follow-up period, which limits conclusions about how the cream performs compared to other treatments.

title: Sex-related differences in outcome of tricuspid valve surgery in severe isolated secondary tricuspid regurgitation.
abstract: Significant secondary tricuspid regurgitation (STR) is associated with worse morbidity and mortality. To-date, evidence on isolated tricuspid valve surgery in STR remains controversial, with uncertainty regarding management strategies. We aimed to investigate sex differences in the association of isolated tricuspid valve surgical repair/replacement (TVR) with outcomes of mortality and heart failure (HF) hospitalizations in STR.Patients with severe STR without significant aortic valve or organic mitral valve disease, congenital heart disease, pacemakers, previous valve intervention, malignancy, or end-stage kidney/liver disease were identified. Isolated TVR was studied as a time-dependent covariate in association with mortality and HF hospitalizations. Among 2857 patients (median age 76 years; 62% women), 143 underwent isolated TVR (58% repair; 42% replacement; 64% with low TRI-SCORE risk category) at a median of 56 days. Over a median of 1.6 (IQR 0.2-5.2) years, 1771 patients died and 1259 had HF hospitalization. When adjusting to age, comorbidities, left/right ventricular function, pulmonary hypertension, haemoglobin level, and dyspnoea, isolated TVR was associated with lower mortality in females (HR 0.54 95% CI 0.35-0.83) but not males (HR 1.29 95% CI 0.90-1.83), P-interaction<0.01; this remained the case when restricting to groups with normal left/right ventricular function. Isolated TVR was associated with HF hospitalization without interaction with sex (HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.46-0.998), P-interaction=0.51.Isolated TVR for STR was associated with decreased HF hospitalizations in both females and males but improved survival only in females. title: Survival Outcomes in Metastatic Colorectal Cancer Patients with BRAF Mutations Undergoing Targeted Chemotherapy: A Reconstructed Individual Patient Data Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
abstract: BRAF V600E-mutant metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) represents an aggressive molecular subtype associated with poor prognosis and limited response to conventional chemotherapy. Although multiple targeted strategies, including anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), anti-epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), and BRAF-directed therapies, are used in clinical practice, their comparative effectiveness remains uncertain. We performed a reconstructed individual patient-data (IPD) meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) to evaluate survival outcomes across targeted therapeutic classes in BRAF-mutant mCRC.A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Cochrane databases was conducted through July 2025 to identify RCTs reporting survival outcomes for BRAF-mutant mCRC. Kaplan-Meier curves were digitized and IPD reconstructed using established methods. A one-stage meta-analysis using Cox proportional hazards models was performed to estimate pooled overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS). Models were adjusted for study-level covariates and clustering, with Bonferroni correction applied for multiple comparisons.Eighteen RCTs comprising 11,931 participants were included. Pooled median OS was 22.3 months for BRAF-directed regimens, 17.1 months for VEGF-targeted therapy, and 10.1 months for EGFR-directed therapy across studies evaluating first-line therapy. Across first-line studies, BRAF inhibitor directed regimen was associated with significantly improved OS compared with EGFR inhibition (HR 0.43, 95% CI 0.31-0.60; P < 0.001) and improved PFS (HR 0.47, 95% CI 0.42-0.53; P < 0.001). VEGF inhibition also demonstrated superior OS compared with EGFR inhibition (HR 0.56, 95% CI 0.38-0.81; p < 0.001). EGFR-directed regimen consistently demonstrated the poorest survival outcomes across analyses.In this reconstructed IPD meta-analysis, BRAF-directed therapies were associated with the most favourable survival outcomes, whereas EGFR directed regimen demonstrated limited clinical benefit in BRAF-mutant mCRC. These results highlight the importance of biologically aligned pathway-targeted therapy and provide comparative evidence to inform treatment selection in this aggressive molecular subtype.© 2026. title: Vertebrobasilar Circulation Involvement in Histiocytic Neoplasms: The Coated Artery Sign.
abstract: Histiocytic neoplasms, particularly Erdheim-Chester disease (ECD), exhibit perivascular infiltration, and vertebrobasilar circulation involvement remains poorly characterized. We aimed to describe intracranial vertebrobasilar involvement.We conducted a case series nested within an observational cohort at a tertiary referral center. We identified patients from a predefined cohort of biopsy-proven histiocytic neoplasms. We included patients with ECD, Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH), or Rosai-Dorfman-Destombes disease (RDD) who demonstrated intracranial vertebrobasilar periarterial involvement, defined by MRI evidence of histiocytic infiltration encasing the vertebral and/or basilar arteries.Vertebrobasilar coated artery involvement was present in 3 patients with ECD (3/183, 1.6%), including 1 with mixed ECD-LCH, and 1 patient with RDD (1/88, 1.1%); no cases occurred in isolated LCH (0/144). Two patients with multisystemic ECD had incidental imaging findings without neurological symptoms. One patient developed a progressive brainstem syndrome due to an enlarging perivascular lesion, and 1 patient with RDD developed chronic progressive myelopathy from a cervicomedullary lesion encasing both vertebral arteries.Vertebrobasilar coated artery involvement can occur in histiocytic neoplasms, particularly ECD. Recognition of this imaging pattern may aid neurologists in diagnosis and help prevent neurological complications from compression or ischemic stroke.Copyright © 2026 Wolters Kluwer Health, LLC. title: Periodontal disease, biomarkers of ADRD risk, and cognitive functioning.
abstract: Periodontitis is a hypothesized risk factor for cognitive impairment. Many prior studies lack information on biological markers of Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (ADRD) risk or genetic risk markers. We assessed the association between periodontitis, biological markers of ADRD risk, and cognitive test performance with robust adjustment for risk factors including high risk genotypes for ADRD.We use data from the United States High School and Beyond (HS&B:80) cohort study, a nationally representative sample of ∼26,830 people enrolled during high school in 1980 through midlife in 2021. Baseline data include information about educational contexts, opportunities, and outcomes; early life circumstances; and demographic group memberships. HS&B:80 data from 2021 include indicators of periodontal disease diagnosis history, blood biomarkers of ADRD risk, and multiple measures of cognitive functioning. We calculated false discovery rates (FDR) to account for multiple comparisons.Our analyses included 13,950 HS&B:80 panelists (mean age 58 years), among whom 15.2% reported a history of periodontal disease. Periodontal disease was associated with lower general cognitive functioning and scores on some domain-specific cognitive tasks; it was also associated with increased levels of pTau-181 and C-reactive protein. We find no evidence of heterogeneity in associations by sex, race and ethnicity, or number of apolipoprotein E (APOE) ε4 alleles. Only working memory attained a FDR < 10% after multiple comparisons adjustment.In this large, diverse, population-representative, community-dwelling sample, self-reported periodontal disease was cross-sectionally associated with cognitive functioning at age ∼60 and some biomarkers of ADRD risk although most associations were not significant after multiple comparisons corrections.Poor gum health has been suggested as a possible contributor to memory and thinking problems later in life, but many studies have not been able to account for important biological and genetic risk factors linked to Alzheimer's disease and related dementias. To better understand this relationship, we analyzed data from nearly 14,000 participants in a large, nationally representative U.S. study who were approaching age 60 in 2021. About 15% reported having been diagnosed with periodontal (gum) disease. People with a history of gum disease tended to perform slightly worse on measures of overall cognitive function and some specific thinking tasks. They also had modestly higher levels of blood markers associated with inflammation and increased risk of Alzheimer's disease and related dementias. These associations were similar across men and women, racial and ethnic groups, and people with different levels of genetic risk based on apolipoprotein E (APOE) status. While this study cannot determine whether gum disease causes cognitive decline, the findings suggest that poor periodontal health may be potentially linked to both cognitive performance and biological signs associated with dementia risk in midlife, highlighting the importance of future research that can better understand if these observations are causal or coincidental.© 2026 The Author(s). title: Sudden Cardiac Death in Firefighters From the United States: A 16-Year Postmortem Analysis.
abstract: Sudden cardiac death (SCD) is the leading cause of duty-related death among firefighters. Understanding postmortem cardiovascular abnormalities associated with SCD is critical to guiding fire service cardiovascular disease screening and prevention programs.This study included US firefighters who had a duty-related death over a 16-year period (1999-2014) with available postmortem reports (autopsy/medical examiner reports). Cases were systematically reviewed to identify cases of SCD. For each SCD case, the primary etiology of SCD was adjudicated by experts in sports cardiology and cardiovascular pathology.Postmortem evaluations were available for 794 of 2100 (37.8%) on-duty firefighter deaths over the study period (average age, 44±13 years; age range, 17-82 years; 4.0% women). A total of 312 of 794 (39.3%) firefighter deaths were adjudicated as SCD. A total of 255 of 312 (81.8%) SCD events were attributable to coronary artery disease/ischemic heart disease or hypertensive heart disease, which both are associated with traditional cardiovascular risk factors. The leading etiology of SCD among young firefighters (aged <40 years) was also coronary artery disease/ischemic heart disease (24/50 [48.0%]). Of firefighters who had an exertional SCD event thought to be secondary to coronary artery disease (n=97), a total of 62 of 91 (68.1%) had severe fixed coronary stenosis, while 29 of 91 (31.9%) demonstrated acute plaque rupture/thrombosis.More than 80% of on-duty SCD events among US firefighters are due to coronary artery disease and hypertensive heart disease that may be prevented by early disease identification and risk factor modification. Future studies should assess the efficacy of more rigorous firefighter cardiovascular disease screening and management practices.

title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists in Obese Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction.
abstract: To evaluate whether GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), compared with DPP4 (dipeptidyl peptidase-4) inhibitors or sulfonylureas, are associated with reduced all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalizations in patients with obesity and type 2 diabetes, and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.PRAISE-HFpEF (Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonist in Obese Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction) was a nationwide multicenter cohort study using a new-user, active-comparator design within the national Veterans Affairs Health System (170 US hospitals). Adults with type 2 diabetes between January 1, 2000 and December 31, 2021, were identified from centralized electronic health records. Patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and a body mass index ≥30 kg/m2 were selected using a validated diagnostic algorithm. Exposure was initiation of a GLP-1RA versus DPP4 inhibitors/sulfonylurea from January 1, 2015 to December 31, 2021. The primary outcome was time to all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalization. Inverse probability of treatment weighting based on the propensity score was used to balanced baseline characteristics.Among 179 288 patients with type 2 diabetes, obesity, and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, 1024 GLP-1RA users and 796 DPP4 inhibitors/sulfonylurea users met inclusion criteria. Over a median follow-up of 1.5 years, GLP-1RA use was associated with a lower risk of the primary outcome (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.78 [95% CI, 0.64-0.95], P=0.01). title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Analog-Type Amyloidosis: A Case Report and Review of the Literature.
abstract: Amyloidosis is a heterogeneous group of diseases characterized by extracellular deposition of insoluble proteins. Glucagon-like peptide-1 analog (AGLP1)-type amyloidosis is a rare iatrogenic form of amyloidosis localized to areas of glucagon-like peptide-1 analog injections. In this study, we describe a case of AGLP1-type amyloidosis presenting as a subcutaneous mass on the abdomen of a 71-year-old woman with a history of liraglutide, semaglutide, and tirzepatide use. Biopsy, including Congo red stain, was consistent with an amyloid deposit. Amyloid protein identification by liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry showed a typical amyloid profile with low spectra for liraglutide. Immunohistochemistry, subsequently performed, showed that the amyloid deposits were positive for glucagon; there is an extensive peptide homology between liraglutide and glucagon. Only 3 cases of AGLP1-type amyloidosis have been previously reported. It is vital for clinicians and pathologists to be aware of AGLP1-type amyloidosis given the increasing worldwide use of GLP-1 agonists, as well as the potential for misdiagnosis of systemic amyloidosis, which has profound therapeutic and prognostic implications.Copyright © 2026 Wolters Kluwer Health, LLC. Testing confirmed the deposits contained amyloid protein similar to glucagon, a natural hormone that shares structural similarities with these medications. title: Systemic Hypertension and Survival in Pulmonary Hypertension.
abstract: Pulmonary hypertension (PH), a progressive and life-threatening condition with rising prevalence among older adults, frequently coexists with systemic hypertension, the prognostic impact of which is poorly understood.To evaluate the association between systemic hypertension and survival in patients with PH.This multicenter cohort study analyzed data from the Pulmonary Vascular Research Institute GoDeep meta-registry, integrating global retrospective and prospective PH cohorts (n = 3238 in Europe, n = 3014 in North America, n = 96 in Africa, n = 802 in Asia, and n = 851 in Oceania). Survival was assessed using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models and adjusted for key confounders, with sensitivity analyses to validate robustness. Independent external validation was performed in a cohort in the UK. A total of 12 771 patients with incident PH (median [IQR] age, 65 [53-73] years; 7372 [58%] female) were diagnosed via right heart catheterization and comprehensive clinical data, encompassing PH groups 1-5 and all age categories. The study spans diagnosis decades from 1980 to 2020. Data were analyzed from February 2025 until September 2026.Center-reported diagnosis of systemic hypertension, baseline systolic systemic arterial pressure (sSAP), and heart rate as well as longitudinal sSAP and heart rate trajectories.All-cause mortality, adjusted for confounding variables, including age, PH group, antihypertensive and PH-specific medications, and cardiac index.Higher baseline sSAP and preexisting systemic hypertension were independently associated with improved survival. Patients with hypertension exhibited a 26% reduced mortality hazard (hazard ratio [HR], 0.74; 95% CI, 0.68-0.79) compared to their counterparts without hypertension. Survival benefits correlated positively with increasing sSAP (80-180 mm Hg), remained consistent across PH groups and age groups, and were independent of antihypertensive and PH-specific medications. Elevated heart rate was associated with higher mortality. sSAP increments correlated with improved cardiac index and tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion. Decreased sSAP and higher heart rate during follow-up correlated with higher mortality. External validation in a separate UK cohort confirmed these findings.In this global PH cohort, higher sSAP was associated with enhanced survival, while a higher baseline heart rate and declining systemic blood pressure during follow-up were significantly associated with increased mortality risk.

title: Very short flow diverters for intracranial aneurysms: technical feasibility, angiographic outcomes, and clinical safety across diverse cerebrovascular locations.
abstract: Longer flow diverters (FDs) are often selected to facilitate deployment. Very short FDs (VSFDs; 10-12 mm) offer a targeted alternative, but technical complexity has limited their adoption, resulting in scarce clinical data.This single-center, retrospective cohort study included patients with intracranial aneurysms who underwent VSFD treatment. The primary outcome was technical success, defined as deployment of the intended VSFD across the aneurysm neck with complete neck coverage at the end of the index procedure, and analyzed per index aneurysm. Secondary outcomes included angiographic results, assessed using the O'Kelly-Marotta (OKM) grading scale, and clinical outcomes, evaluated with the modified Rankin Scale (mRS) during follow-up. Statistical analyses were performed using R software (version 4.5.2; R Foundation for Statistical Computing, Vienna, Austria).Seventy-five patients harboring 151 aneurysms were included, with 86 index aneurysms treated using 93 VSFDs. Technical success was achieved in 82 of 86 index aneurysms (95.3%); the remaining 4 aneurysms required a second device because of malposition of the first. At a mean follow-up of 15.2 ± 11.0 months, complete occlusion was achieved in 42 of 49 patients with imaging follow-up (85.7%) and adequate occlusion in 49 of 49 (100%); imaging follow-up was unavailable in 26 of 75 patients (34.7%), so these proportions apply to the imaged subgroup only. Favorable clinical outcome (mRS 0-2) was obtained in 51 of 61 patients with clinical follow-up (83.6%), and no retreatment was required during follow-up. Postprocedural permanent neurological complications occurred in 5 of 75 patients (6.7%).VSFDs were technically feasible in selected intracranial aneurysms. Whether they offer any advantage over conventional-length devices was not tested in this study and requires anatomically matched comparison. Device malposition occurred only in the middle cerebral artery territory, and in every case the device had been deployed too proximally, so deployment from distal to proximal by experienced operators is essential.© 2026. title: Facial artery morphology assessed by computed tomography angiography: a mixed-effects morphometric analysis of age, sex, and laterality.
abstract: The facial artery is the principal arterial supply to the midface and is among the most frequently encountered vascular structures during facial reconstructive, aesthetic, and minimally invasive procedures. Precise knowledge of its anatomical course and morphometric characteristics is essential to minimize vascular complications. However, previous morphometric studies have largely been descriptive and have rarely accounted for bilateral anatomical correlation or simultaneously evaluated the independent effects of age, sex, and laterality using appropriate multivariable statistical models.A retrospective cross-sectional study was performed using computed tomography angiography (CTA) examinations from 103 adults, yielding 201 evaluable facial arteries. Standardized three-dimensional morphometric measurements were obtained at the inferior border of the mandible and the lateral alar base. Linear mixed-effects models incorporating patient-specific random intercepts were used to evaluate the effects of age, sex, side, and CTA diagnostic category while accounting for within-subject correlation. Measurement reproducibility was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), Bland-Altman analysis, and Cohen's kappa.Type III, according to the Furukawa classification, was the predominant anatomical pattern (67.2%). Among 98 patients with bilateral visualization, Furukawa type showed complete right-left concordance (100%; κ = 1.00). In an additional patient-level logistic model, neither age (OR 0.992 per year; 95% CI, 0.965-1.020; P = 0.584) nor female sex (OR 1.793; 95% CI, 0.767-4.191; P = 0.178) was significantly associated with Type III versus Type II. For continuous morphometric variables, no systematic laterality effect was detected, although individual-level bilateral agreement varied across parameters. After Holm correction across morphometric outcomes, women had a smaller facial artery diameter at the inferior border of the mandible and a shorter zygomatic arch-facial artery distance than men, while increasing age was independently associated with a shorter oral commissure-facial artery distance. Quantitative morphometric measurements demonstrated good-to-excellent observer reproducibility (intraobserver ICC: 0.900-0.960; interobserver ICC: 0.760-0.860), whereas categorical assessment of facial artery position relative to the nasolabial sulcus showed perfect intraobserver (κ = 1.00) and substantial interobserver agreement (κ = 0.79).CTA provides a reproducible morphometric assessment of the facial artery. No systematic laterality effect was identified for continuous morphometric variables, although individual bilateral agreement varied by measurement, while Furukawa type showed complete bilateral concordance in patients with both arteries visualized. Age and sex were not significantly associated with Furukawa Type III versus Type II, but they influenced selected continuous morphometric parameters. These findings characterize facial artery anatomy in a Mexican clinical cohort and may inform individualized anatomical assessment and preprocedural planning; they do not establish procedural risk thresholds.© 2026. title: Control of Diaphragm Muscle in Health and Disease.
abstract: Unique to mammals, the diaphragm muscle (DIAm) is the major pump muscle for breathing. The DIAm is a skeletal muscle composed of different fiber types with different mechanical and fatigue properties. Neural control of the DIAm is mediated by recruitment of motor units (MUs), each comprising a phrenic motor neuron in the cervical spinal cord and the set of muscle fibers (of a single type) it innervates. Thus, by recruiting different MU types, a range of motor behaviors can be accomplished. To support breathing, which is a sustained behavior, fatigue-resistant slow (type I fibers) and fast (type IIa fibers) MUs are recruited. However, the DIAm also subserves short duration, higher-force airway clearance, and voiding behaviors that require recruitment of more fatigable fast (type IIx/IIb) fibers. Importantly, in disease conditions, these fatigable DIAm MUs are more vulnerable, while fatigue-resistant MUs are more resilient.

Fatigue-resistant muscle fibers support regular breathing, while more easily fatigued fibers enable powerful but brief movements. In disease, the easily fatigued fibers become more vulnerable to damage while the fatigue-resistant fibers remain more stable.
llm_summary_expert: The diaphragm is a unique mammalian skeletal muscle that serves as the primary pump for breathing and is composed of different fiber types with distinct mechanical and fatigue properties. Neural control of the diaphragm occurs through recruitment of motor units, each consisting of a phrenic motor neuron in the cervical spinal cord and the muscle fibers it innervates, allowing for varied motor behaviors depending on which motor unit types are activated. In disease conditions, the fatigable diaphragm motor units demonstrate greater vulnerability compared to fatigue-resistant motor units, which show greater resilience. The differential vulnerability of motor unit types in disease suggests that understanding diaphragm motor control mechanisms is essential for comprehending how respiratory and non-respiratory functions are compromised in pathological states.

title: Comparative survival and time toxicity outcomes of CAR-T versus bispecific antibody therapies in relapsed/refractory FL.
abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) and CD20xCD3 bispecific antibody (BsAb) therapies are both effective for relapsed/refractory (R/R) follicular lymphoma (FL), but comparative real-world survival outcomes and time toxicity have not been characterized. We performed a multicenter retrospective study of 228 patients with R/R FL treated with standard-of-care CAR-T (n = 141) or BsAb (n = 87) across 17 U.S. academic centers in the third-line or later setting. Progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were stratified by 2 or ≥3 prior lines of therapy (LOT2 or LOT3+), including propensity matching. Time toxicity was measured by physical health care contact days. Median PFS was not reached (NR) with CAR-T and 581 days with BsAb in the LOT2 cohort (p < .0001), and was NR with CAR-T and 584 days with BsAb in the LOT3+ cohort (p = .0064). CAR-T recipients were younger (p < .0001) and had better performance status (p = .007) but were more refractory to prior LOT (p = .017). PFS advantages of CAR-T were independent of these differences. OS did not differ between treatment groups. CAR-T had significantly greater time toxicity over the first year, with higher mean contact days than BsAb in both the LOT2 (58 vs 44) and LOT3+ (69 vs 49) cohorts. In this large multicenter cohort of patients with R/R FL, CAR-T was associated with superior PFS but greater time toxicity compared with BsAb therapy. title: Towards modeling the hemodynamic impact of mitral and aortic valve repair in patients with left ventricular assist devices.
abstract: Valve dysfunction is a major threat to long-term success in left ventricular assist device (LVAD) therapy, with direct implications for right heart performance. In this study, we apply a patient-specific, image-based computational modeling framework to evaluate the hemodynamic impact of simulated mitral and aortic valve repair in five LVAD-supported patients. Each patient was modeled under four conditions: (patient-specific LVAD-supported state), simulated mitral valve (MV) repair, simulated aortic valve (AV) repair, and simulated combined MV&AV repair. Because validation data for valve repair were unavailable, the simulated repair scenarios are exploratory in silico interventions based on clinically validated patient-specific models. The models integrate dynamic CT imaging, echocardiography, catheterization data, and device-specific LVAD parameters into a coupled 3D-0D simulation pipeline. Valve dynamics are governed by transvalvular pressure and flow, allowing physiological modeling of regurgitant lesions and surgical repair. The right ventricular (RV) was assessed using a combination of model-derived metrics, including right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF), pulmonary artery pulsatility index (PAPi), and RV-PA coupling. In addition, we performed blood residence time (RT) analysis to evaluate blood stasis within the left heart and aorta. The simulations suggest that valve repair improved cardiac output, reduced pulmonary congestion, and enhanced right ventricular loading conditions. Notably, mitral valve repair restored aortic valve opening during the cardiac cycle, which improved sinus washout and reduced blood residence time within the aortic root-factors associated with lower thrombotic risk. Overall, these findings suggest a potential role for valve repair in LVAD-supported hearts, though larger, validated patient cohorts are needed to confirm these results.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). title: Surveillance of C. auris and Other Potentially Pathogenic Yeast Among Anesthesia Workspace Reservoirs, Multicenter Study.
abstract: The emergence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) Candida auris has raised concern about fungal healthcare-associated infections in perioperative and critical care settings. We evaluated anesthesia workspaces to identify high-risk reservoirs and inform optimization of infection prevention practices.We conducted a prospective multicenter observational study of patients across 11 geographically dispersed U.S. hospitals from March 2023 to July 2025. A total of 6,074 reservoirs were sampled during 605 surgical cases and 273 consecutive operating room case pairs to detect C. auris and other potentially pathogenic yeast, including C. pseudohaemulonii, C. vulturna, C. diddensiae, C. metapsilosis, and Naganishia diffluens.No anesthesia workspace reservoirs tested positive for C. auris (95% CI 0%-0.61% for surgical cases and 0-1.34% for case pairs). Other potentially pathogenic yeast (24 isolates) were detected in 1.16% (7/605) of cases. Most isolates were recovered from patient skin (92%), with fewer from environmental surfaces (4%) and practitioner hands (4%). Potential transmission patterns reflected known C. auris epidemiology, including patient-to-environment and patient-to-patient spread.Outside outbreak settings, the anesthesia workspace for the studied population appears to be a low-risk reservoir for C. auris, making routine empirical environmental interventions such as high-dose ultraviolet-C irradiation difficult to justify. Surveillance for other potentially pathogenic yeast may provide a more practical approach to guide targeted infection prevention efforts.Copyright © 2026 Association for Professionals in Infection Control and Epidemiology, Inc. title: Event-to-Payment Latency in Physicians With Imaging-Related Allegations: NPDB Reports Processed 2004-2025.
abstract: To characterize event-to-payment/report-processing latency among physicians with imaging-related allegations.This retrospective cross-sectional study included National Practitioner Data Bank physician payment reports processed in 2004-2025, excluding state-fund reports. Imaging-related allegations were identified in either specific-allegation field. Latency equaled original report-processing year minus alleged-event end year, using onset year when end year was unavailable. Adjusted models included report characteristics and jurisdiction, with practitioner-clustered standard errors. Complementary analyses examined events in 2004-2010 and jurisdiction random effects.Among 199,060 eligible reports, 1,980 involved imaging-related allegations (1,852 physicians). Median latency was 4 years (IQR, 3-6); 47.0% had latency ≥5 years. The proportions were 43.7% (2004-2009), 42.9% (2010-2015), 46.1% (2016-2020), and 55.7% (2021-2025). Adjusted differences were +0.66 years for permanent injury and +0.48 for death versus nonpermanent injury; +0.38 for outpatient and +0.49 for mixed settings versus inpatient care; and +1.56 for judgment versus settlement/other. All corresponding 95% confidence intervals excluded zero. Age was associated with -0.16 years per decade-category increment. Among 562 reports for events in 2004-2010, median latency was 4 years and 44.1% had latency ≥5 years. The adjusted payment ratio per additional latency year was 1.021 (95% CI, 0.997-1.044; P=0.082).Paid reports involving physicians with imaging-related allegations frequently reflected care delivered years earlier. The payment association was small, imprecise, and not statistically significant. These selected paid-report data do not estimate litigation duration, future payment risk, or radiologist-specific performance.Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Inc.
