title: Physician Perceptions and Clinical Outcomes of a Novel Standardized Outside Hospital Admission Process.
abstract: Transfers are high-risk events, and outside hospital admissions lack standardized processes to ensure timely delivery of essential clinical information. We piloted a novel, standardized process for outside admissions to a single academic medical center's resident- and hospital medicine-attending-based medicine services. Following literature review, Epic UserWeb review, and frontline physician input, a workflow and templated electronic health record accept note were developed to centralize outside admission documentation. Completed by physicians during real-time communication with outside physicians, the template captures key clinical data and incorporates a communication checklist. Physician education was delivered electronically and in person. Subjective attending and resident perceptions were assessed via electronic prepost surveys administered 1 week before and 90 days after implementation. Secondarily, exploratory patient clinical outcomes were assessed through 90-day prepost manual retrospective chart review. Survey responses were obtained from 60/38 residents and 12/7 attendings (pre/post). Documentation sufficiency on patient arrival was directionally promising among residents (21.7% vs 39.5%, P = 0.062). Satisfaction with the admission process and perceived patient safety improved significantly among residents and attendings ( P ≤ 0.036). Most respondents rated the note as useful or very useful (84% residents; 86% attendings), and attendings reported reduced time managing outside admissions. The intervention was associated with exploratory, nonsignificant reductions in rapid response team activation, intensive care unit transfer, 30-day readmission, mortality, and length of stay compared with preintervention patients. A standardized documentation and communication process improved physician satisfaction and perceived patient safety, with promising exploratory patient outcomes. Further study is warranted to assess impact at scale.Copyright © 2026 the American College of Medical Quality.

title: Total Hip Arthroplasty in Patients With Open Triradiate Cartilage: 10-Year Follow-Up of an Expanded Cohort.
abstract: Total hip arthroplasty (THA) in patients with open triradiate cartilage remains controversial, with an open triradiate cartilage considered a challenge for acetabular component fixation. We previously reported excellent 5-year functional outcomes and implant survivorship in a series of patients undergoing THA with open triradiate cartilage. The current study expands this cohort to 10-year radiographic and functional outcomes.Our institutional Total Joint Registry was queried to identify 24 patients who underwent THA with an open triradiate cartilage between the years 2000 and 2024. Skeletal maturity was assessed utilizing the modified Oxford bone age, with only triradiate scores of 1 and 2 included. Demographic, implant, and radiographic data were collected. Functional outcomes were assessed through the Harris Hip score (HHS).The previously analyzed cohort (11 patients, 12 THAs) had a mean age of 13 years, and a mean follow-up of 10 years (range: 5 to 15). The overall expanded cohort (24 THAs) had a mean age of 14 years, with a mean follow-up of 6 years (range: 1 to 15) and a mean modified Oxford bone age was 22. The most common indications for THA were avascular necrosis ( 67%), secondary arthritis (25%), and neoplasia (8%). Preoperatively, 54% of patients utilized gait aids; at final follow-up, all patients reported independent ambulation with a mean HHS of 92. Radiographically, 92% of implants showed stable osseointegration at the latest follow-up. Two patients required acetabular component revisions for aseptic loosening, one of whom required rerevision for instability.The present study expands on the largest series in the literature of THA in patients with open triradiate cartilage. Our results demonstrate excellent functional outcomes, 92% implant survivorship, and low complication rates at long-term 10-year follow-up. These findings suggest THA is safe and durable in patients with open triradiate cartilage without the need to delay arthroplasty for closure of the triradiate cartilage.Level III.Copyright © 2026 Wolters Kluwer Health, LLC. In their study of 24 patients followed for an average of 6 to 10 years, 92% of the implants remained stable and all patients could walk independently with excellent pain relief, though two patients needed revision surgery. These results suggest that hip replacement can be performed safely in growing children without waiting for their bones to fully mature.

title: ER proteostasis failure in HYOU1 deficiency alters B cells, neutrophils, and interferon signalling.
abstract: Hypoxia upregulated 1 (HYOU1) is a stress-inducible ER chaperone. We investigated 2 unrelated patients carrying biallelic HYOU1 variants and presenting with primary immunodeficiency. Patient 1, homozygous for p.Pro444His, displayed failure to thrive, hypoglycemia, B cell lymphopenia, and neutropenia. Patient 2, compound heterozygous for p.Arg262Gln and p.Pro757_Glu758insAla, exhibited recurrent infections, enteropathy, and hypogammaglobulinemia. In Patient 1, while HYOU1 transcription was preserved, the protein was severely reduced. Tunicamycin treatment of dermal fibroblasts showed a blunted unfolded protein response and defective induction of ER stress-responsive genes. Immunophenotyping showed near-absence of circulating B cells, and single-cell RNA sequencing of bone marrow identified an arrest at the pro-B cell stage. Neutrophils displayed hypogranulation and dysregulated IFN- and apoptosis-associated transcriptional signatures, unresponsive to G-CSF. HYOU1 deficiency hence results in ER stress-induced proteostasis failure that simultaneously impairs adaptive immunity through B cell developmental arrest and innate immunity through neutrophil dysfunction and IFN pathway imbalance. This work expands the spectrum of HYOU1 deficiency and further identifies ER proteostasis as a central determinant of immune homeostasis.© 2026 Idani et al.

llm_summary: Researchers studied two patients with mutations in the HYOU1 gene, which produces a protein that helps cells manage stress in their internal structures, and found that these patients had severe immune system problems including low B cell counts and poorly functioning infection-fighting white blood cells called neutrophils. The defective HYOU1 protein prevented cells from properly responding to stress, which disrupted both the adaptive immune system that learns to fight infections and the innate immune system that provides immediate defense. These findings suggest that the protein's role in maintaining cellular health is essential for a properly functioning immune system.

title: Intracranial dural arteriovenous fistulas with perimedullary venous drainage: analysis of the multinational CONDOR registry.
abstract: Cognard type V dural arteriovenous fistulas (dAVFs), defined by spinal perimedullary venous drainage, represent a rare and aggressive neurovascular pathology. Comprehensive multicenter data remain scarce. The authors present the largest multicenter analysis to date, characterizing presentation, radiology, treatment, complications, and functional outcomes of Cognard type V dAVFs.The authors retrospectively analyzed patients with angiographically confirmed Cognard type V dAVFs from the Consortium for Dural Arteriovenous Fistula Outcomes Research (CONDOR), spanning 16 academic centers. Patient demographics, imaging features, treatment strategies, procedural complications, and modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores were recorded.Among 1077 patients with dAVFs, 37 (3%) had Cognard type V lesions. The mean patient age was 57 years, and 59.5% of patients were male. Most presented with nonhemorrhagic neurological deficits (68%), while 14% had hemorrhage. The most common location was the foramen magnum (32%). Embolization was the primary treatment in 67% of cases, complete obliteration was achieved in 71% of cases. Upfront microsurgery was performed in 22% of patients (obliteration rate 88%), and radiosurgery in 14% (success rate 40%). Salvage treatment further improved obliteration outcomes. Temporary complications occurred in 8% of patients (3/37): 2 with transient neurological deficits postembolization and 1 with transient hydrocephalus after surgery. Permanent complications were observed in 3% (1/37) due to treatment-related hemorrhage. At the last follow-up (mean 2.4 years), 69% (24/35) of patients maintained or improved to an mRS score ≤ 2. No deaths occurred. Functional improvement was seen in 29% (10/35), while mRS decline was in 40% of patients (14/35), all unrelated to the dAVF itself.Cognard type V dAVFs carry a high risk of neurological morbidity. However, favorable functional outcomes are achievable with timely, multimodal intervention. Complication rates remain low, with most being transient. These data support aggressive but tailored management to prevent permanent disability in this high-risk population.

title: Association of GLP-1 receptor agonist and SGLT2 inhibitor use with outcomes in patients with type 2 diabetes undergoing pacemaker implantation.
abstract: Heart failure (HF) remains prevalent following pacemaker implantation, with patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) representing a particularly vulnerable population. Whether use of contemporary glucose-lowering therapies is associated with subsequent clinical outcomes has not been well characterized. We investigated the associations of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor (SGLT2i) and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RA) therapy, individually and in combination, with post-implantation clinical outcomes.Electronic health records identified 3,609 patients with T2DM who underwent pacemaker implantation from 2016-2023. Based on peri-implantation medication dispensing, patients were classified as SGLT2i (n = 438), GLP-1RA (n = 193), combined therapy (n = 231), or neither (n = 2,747). Following a 90-day landmark period, three-year risks of all-cause mortality and HF hospitalization were evaluated using multinomial propensity score-based inverse probability of treatment weighting and Cox proportional hazards models.Overall, 463 patients (12.8%) died. All treatment groups showed lower all-cause mortality than controls, with the greatest reduction observed in the combination therapy group (HR 0.41; 95% CI, 0.22-0.77; P = 0.006). HF hospitalization occurred in 295 patients (8.2%), significantly reduced in combination therapy (HR 0.35; 95% CI, 0.17-0.74; P = 0.006), with trends toward benefit in monotherapy groups.Among patients with T2DM undergoing permanent pacemaker implantation, SGLT2i and GLP-1RA therapy were associated with lower all-cause mortality, while combined therapy was additionally associated with fewer HF hospitalizations. These findings support further evaluation of cardiometabolic therapies after pacemaker implantation in randomized trials.Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Inc.

Among 3,609 patients followed for three years, those taking both medications together had the lowest risk of death and heart failure hospitalization compared to those taking neither medication. title: Safety and Effectiveness of MiniMedTM 780G Advanced Hybrid Closed-Loop Use with Ultrarapid Insulin Lispro-AABC in Pediatric and Adult Type 1 Diabetes.
abstract: Given the faster onset and shorter duration of action of ultra-rapid insulin lispro-aabc (URLi, Lyumjev™ insulin), compared with insulin lispro (a rapid-acting insulin [RAI]), the present study investigated the safety and glycemic outcomes of MiniMed™ 780G advanced hybrid closed-loop (AHCL) use with URLi in youths and adults with T1D.This 19-site, single-arm, clinical trial enrolled children and adolescents (aged 7-17 years) and adults (aged 18-80 years) with T1D who underwent a run-in period (∼2 weeks) using open loop or automated basal only with an RAI (aspart or lispro), followed by a 3-month study period using URLi with AHCL (AHCL + URLi). End-of-study glycemic metrics and A1c were compared to predefined thresholds and to data from baseline/run-in. Use of recommended optimal settings (ROS, 100 mg/dL glucose target with an active insulin time [AIT] of 2 h) was also assessed.In an intention-to-treat population (N = 101 pediatric and N = 110 adult participants), percentage of time in range (%TIR) during the last ∼6 weeks of the study period was significantly greater than the predefined thresholds for both the pediatric and adult participants. A1c was unchanged in the pediatric cohort but significantly reduced in the adult cohort (from 7.4 ± 0.9% to 6.9 ± 0.6% [P < 0.001]). Compared with run-in, study period %TIR and percentage of time in tight target range (%TITR) were significantly increased (pediatric mean %TIRΔ [17.4%] and %TITRΔ [16.0%], respectively, and adult mean %TIRΔ [10.6%] and %TITRΔ [11.6%], respectively; P < 0.001 for all). Additionally, % time above range for both groups was significantly reduced. Use of ROS allowed more participants to achieve recommended glycemic targets. There were no severe hypoglycemia or diabetic ketoacidosis events. title: Cardiovascular, Renal, and Hepatic Biomarkers Outside Guideline-Recommended Thresholds: Prevalence and Determinants in Type 1 Diabetes.
abstract: The objective of the study was to evaluate the prevalence of cardiovascular, renal, and hepatic biomarkers that fall outside guideline-based thresholds in adults with type 1 diabetes (T1D), and to identify demographic and clinical factors associated with these biomarkers.This observational study linked data on 2,923 adults with T1D from the T1D Exchange Registry and NorstellaLinQ's laboratory data (2022-2023). Prevalence of biomarkers outside guideline-recommended thresholds was calculated. Generalized estimating equations (GEE) were used to model associations with age, sex, race/ethnicity, insurance, T1D duration, body mass index (BMI), and hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), while accounting for within-subject correlation due to repeated measures.Elevated low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol (≥70 mg/dL, above the recommended goal for individuals with diabetes at high risk for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease) was common (80.2%), as were overweight (33.8%) and obesity (30.3%). Additional findings included high total cholesterol (≥200 mg/dL, 22.6%), low high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol (<40 mg/dL males, <50 mg/dL females, 13.4%), elevated urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (≥30 mg/g, 13.0%), reduced estimated glomerular filtration rate (<60 mL/min/1.73 m2, 6.2%), and elevated fibrosis-4 index (FIB-4) (≥1.3, 14.4%). In adjusted GEE models, higher HbA1c was significantly associated with increased odds of abnormal cardiovascular and renal biomarkers across most measures. Male sex and BMI were linked to lower HDL cholesterol, while older age was strongly associated with elevated FIB-4.Obesity and elevated LDL cholesterol are highly prevalent in adults with T1D, indicating substantial cardiometabolic risk. The lack of outcome trials in this population underscores the need for studies to evaluate strategies to improve weight and lipid management and thereby reduce cardiovascular and renal risk in adults with T1D.

title: Routine cerebral embolic protection during TAVR: A meta-analysis and trial sequential evidence from 11,000 randomized patients.
abstract: To perform an updated meta-analysis assessing the effect of routine cerebral embolic protection (CEP) use on the incidence of stroke-disabling and non-disabling-following transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR).Electronic databases were systematically searched through August 2025 for eligible randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing CEP versus no CEP in TAVR. The primary outcomes were the incidence of overall stroke, disabling stroke, and non-disabling stroke at 2-5 days and 30 days post-procedure. Random-effects model was used to estimate risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Evaluation of the certainty of evidence was done following the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) criteria. Trial sequential analysis was performed to assess the conclusiveness and the reliability of the data.Eight RCTs, including 11,692 patients, were analyzed. No statistically significant difference was observed in overall stroke incidence between CEP and control groups at 2-5 days (RR = 0.95; 95% CI: 0.75-1.19; p = 0.64) or at 30 days (RR = 0.93; 95% CI: 0.57-1.53; p = 0.79). Disabling stroke rates were also similar at 2-5 days (RR = 0.70; 95% CI: 0.41-1.18; p = 0.18) and at 30 days (RR = 1.18; 95% CI: 0.36-3.87; p = 0.78). Non-disabling stroke showed no significant difference at either time point. Safety outcomes, including major bleeding, vascular complications, and acute kidney injury, were also not significantly different.This updated meta-analysis found that a routine CEP strategy during TAVR was not associated with a statistically significant reduction in overall, disabling, or non-disabling stroke. The neutral effect on safety endpoints suggests a limited role for routine CEP use, although smaller benefits, device-specific effects, or benefits in selected higher-risk patients cannot be excluded.Copyright © 2026 Japanese College of Cardiology. title: Neurosurgical software device safety in the US: analysis of 2017-2025 FDA Recall and Adverse Event Data.
abstract: Neurosurgeons rely on multiple software applications for surgical planning, intraoperative navigation, and neurophysiological monitoring. Combined with the proliferation of AI-based clinical adjuncts, software as a medical device (SaMD) represents an evolving frontier with profound implications for patient safety. The aim of this study was to systematically analyze all software-related neurological medical device recalls initiated in the US from 2017 to 2025 and to assess the implications of recalls and adverse events for software devices currently in use, as well as the risks posed by emerging software platforms.Recall and adverse event information related to neurological SaMDs (2017-2025) was extracted from the FDA recall, MAUDE, AccessGUDID, and openFDA databases. Product codes were identified using the FDA Product Classification database. Associated adverse event data were extracted using a custom Python script with the openFDA application programming interface.There were 20 unique software-associated neurological device recalls identified across 7 medical device companies and 4 distinct device categories, namely surgical navigation (55%), neurophysiological monitoring devices (25%), surgical planning (15%), and stereotactic devices (5%). More than half of the neurological devices that were recalled had FDA class I severity. Recalls categorized as class I displayed a significant upward trend in annual frequency from 2017 to 2024 (p = 0.027). The median recall times were shorter for class I versus class II recalls (4 vs 10 years, IQR 2-7 vs 6-11 years; Mann-Whitney U = 28, p = 0.182). There were 16,333 adverse event notifications, with 93.4% related to malfunction and 5.9% related to injury. Two surgical navigation devices alone were responsible for 88.8% of all documented adverse events. There was a significantly higher rate of severe adverse harm reported among class II than class I recalls (14.6% vs 3.6%, p < 0.001). More than 10,000 adverse events were reported after formal recall notification for two medical devices. System instability (55.0%) and software defects (43.5%) comprised 98.5% of adverse event notifications.Device recalls and adverse events associated with neurological SaMDs trended toward greater severity of harm, were concentrated in a few high-throughput platforms, and generated a significant volume of adverse events that persisted even after the recall procedure took effect. The observed discordance between recall class and reported patient harm, as well as the prevalence of runtime instability as the most common software failure mode, represent potential areas of improvement for current regulatory frameworks. Adaptation by regulatory bodies and vigilance by providers is critical, particularly for identifying SaMD-related adverse events.

title: Early-Life Polyethylene Microplastic Exposure Exacerbates ADHD-Like Behaviors in Mice via PI3K/AKT1/Nrf2 Signaling: Evidence From the Pilot Cohort and Multi-Omics Analyses.
abstract: Microplastic pollution may influence neurodevelopment, yet its relationship with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) remains unclear. We integrated a pediatric cohort, multi-omics analyses, network toxicology, and animal experiments to investigate polyethylene (PE) microplastic exposure in ADHD vulnerability. Among 90 children, PE was the predominant polymer detected in blood and was more abundant in children with ADHD. Higher PE burden was associated with greater symptom severity, increased IL-6, and reduced antioxidant capacity. Multi-omics and network analyses converged on PI3K/AKT1/Nrf2 signaling. In a perinatal nicotine mouse model, developmental PE co-exposure exacerbated ADHD-like behaviors, dopaminergic dysfunction, and oxidative injury. Melatonin partially alleviated these abnormalities by restoring PI3K/AKT1/GSK3β and Nrf2 signaling, whereas AAV-mediated PI3K knockdown weakened its protective effects. Collectively, the human findings identify circulating PE burden as an environmental correlate of ADHD-related neurodevelopmental vulnerability, while the animal experiments provide evidence that developmental PE co-exposure can aggravate ADHD-like abnormalities in a susceptible background.© 2026 The Author(s). title: What Are Recent Insights Into Pontomedullary Circuits Controlling in REM Sleep?
abstract: Recent studies have identified neurochemically defined neuronal groups in the pons and medulla that have a critical role in initiation, maintenance, and manifestations of REM sleep (REM-on neurons). The sublaterodorsal tegmental nucleus (SLD) in rodents (subcoeruleus nucleus in humans) contains a group of glutamatergic neurons that express corticotrophin-releasing hormone‑binding protein (Crhbp + neurons) that initiate REM sleep and elicit REM sleep atonia by projections to inhibitory neurons of the ventromedial medulla projecting to spinal motor neurons. A reciprocal glutamatergic excitatory loop between these SLD Crhbp + neurons and neurons in the dorsomedial medulla expressing nitric oxide synthase 1 (Nos1+ neurons) form a core circuit that initiates and maintains REM sleep. Other neurochemically defined neuronal groups in the dorsomedial medulla trigger rapid eye movements and other phasic phenomena during REM sleep. Both the ventromedial medulla and the dorsomedial medulla contain GABAergic neurons that promote REM sleep by inhibiting REM-off neurons.

llm_summary: Recent studies have identified specific nerve cell groups in the brainstem that control when REM sleep (the stage when dreams occur) starts and continues. A key circuit involves glutamate-releasing neurons in the pons that trigger REM sleep and muscle paralysis by connecting to cells in the lower brainstem, which then signal spinal neurons to prevent movement. These findings reveal how interconnected brain regions work together to produce the characteristic features of REM sleep, including eye movements and temporary muscle weakness.

title: Germline Genetic Variants and Epilepsy Surgery Response: Individual Participant Pooled Analysis of 272 Patients.
abstract: Genetic testing is increasingly used in presurgical evaluation, but the yield of resection and ablation across germline genetic epilepsies remains uncertain.We conducted a systematic review of MEDLINE (PubMed) and Scopus and added cases from 3 institutional cohorts and the Pediatric Epilepsy Research Consortium (PERC) databases, including individuals with pathogenic/likely pathogenic germline variants besides tuberous sclerosis who underwent resection or laser ablation. Etiologies were grouped into biologically informed categories (GATORopathies, vascular, overgrowth, copy number variants (CNVs), channelopathies, synaptopathies, and other). Primary outcome was seizure freedom (Engel I) at the last follow-up. Group comparisons used Fisher exact and Kruskal-Wallis tests (α = 0.05; Bonferroni when applicable). Prespecified sensitivity analyses stratified by lesional status, excluded GATORopathies, and restricted to literature-only cases.We included 224 literature cases (65 studies), 36 institutional cases, and 12 PERC cases (n = 272). The median follow-up was 24 months (interquartile range 12-48.0). Seizure freedom was achieved in vascular disorders 14/19 (73.6%), GATORopathies 79/120 (65.8%), CNVs 18/31 (58.0%), overgrowth 9/16 (56.6%), channelopathies 13/43 (30.0%), synaptopathies 4/18 (22.2%), and other 11/25 (44.0%) (overall p < 0.001). Among cases with available imaging results, 208/253 (82.2%) had epileptogenic MRI lesions, including 64% of channelopathies and 80% of the synaptopathies. In univariate contrasts (each category vs all others), odds of seizure freedom were higher for vascular disorders (2.64-fold, 95% CI 0.87-9.65) and GATORopathies (2.41-fold, 95% CI 1.44-4.09), and lower for synaptopathies (∼4.2-fold lower, OR 0.23, 95% CI 0.05-0.77) and channelopathies (∼4.5-fold lower, OR 0.22, 95% CI 0.09-0.48). Direction and magnitude were consistent across prespecified sensitivity analyses (lesional only, literature only, exclusion of GATORopathies).Resective surgeries can be effective in germline genetic epilepsies, but outcomes vary by pathway. Disorders with discrete, lesional substrates (GATORopathies, vascular) show the highest likelihood of seizure freedom, whereas channelopathies and synaptopathies, despite the presence of MRI lesions, have substantially lower yields even in lesional cases. Prospective, genotype-aware surgical registries with standardized reporting (EEG, imaging, and pathology) and time-to-event outcomes are needed to refine the selection of surgical candidates and quantify seizure and non-seizure-related outcomes.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether combining two diabetes medications—SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 receptor agonists—works better than using either drug alone for preventing heart attacks, strokes, and kidney problems in people with type 2 diabetes. The study found that using both medications together did not reduce these serious outcomes compared to using just one medication. title: Concordance Between [18F]Flortaucipir PET Visual Reads and CenTauR-Based Quantification.
abstract: Tau PET imaging with [18F]flortaucipir allows for the visualization and mapping of aggregated tau deposits, a key neuropathologic feature of Alzheimer disease (AD). A visual interpretation method for [18F]flortaucipir was approved by the Food and Drug Administration and European Medicines Agency and has been implemented for a standardized, clinically usable definition of tau PET positivity. The CenTauRz method, on the other hand, offers the possibility to harmonize the definition of tau PET positivity across different radiotracers using quantitative metrics, but its concordance with clinically relevant [18F]flortaucipir visual reads remains unclear. Methods: A convenience sample of 3991 participants, including cognitively unimpaired (CU) and cognitively impaired (CI) individuals (i.e., those with mild cognitive impairment or AD dementia), underwent [18F]flortaucipir PET imaging. Each [18F]flortaucipir scan was assessed by 3 trained readers using the approved visual interpretation method and quantified using the CenTauRz quantification pipeline in different regions of interest (ROIs). Concordance between positive visual reads and CenTauRz-defined positivity (i.e., >2 on the CenTauRz scale) was assessed using Cohen κ. Receiver-operating-characteristic (ROC) analysis evaluated the discriminative power of continuous CenTauRz values in distinguishing between negative and positive visual reads. Generalized additive models examined clinical progression on the basis of visual and CenTauRz-based assessments of tau PET positivity. Results: Concordance between visual reads and CenTauRz-based assessments of tau PET positivity was moderate, particularly in CU individuals (κ = 0.23-0.55 for CU participants, κ = 0.57-0.82 for CI participants, depending on the ROI). ROC analysis revealed that the agreement remained moderate, independent of the CenTauRz cut point used (area under the ROC curve, 0.72-0.87 vs. 0.87-0.97 for CU and CI individuals, respectively). Among discordant cases, participants with visually positive/CenTauRz-negative tau PET scans were more frequently amyloid-positive and exhibited faster clinical progression compared with visually negative/CenTauRz-positive individuals. Conclusion: Our findings highlight the relatively limited agreement between the visual assessment of [18F]flortaucipir PET images and CenTauRz-based quantification, particularly in CU individuals. Participants with visually positive/CenTauRz-negative tau PET scans showed a high frequency of amyloid positivity and faster clinical progression, suggesting that visual reads are more sensitive to heterogeneous, clinically relevant tau accumulation patterns not captured by ROI-based methods. These findings underscore the need for new quantification approaches to better capture the complex patterns of tau deposition, important for early AD detection and monitoring.© 2026 by the Society of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging.

llm_summary: Researchers compared two methods for detecting tau protein buildup in the brain using PET imaging scans from nearly 4,000 people, finding only moderate agreement between visual inspection by doctors and a computer-based quantification method called CenTauRz. Scans that appeared positive to doctors but negative to the computer method were associated with amyloid protein presence and faster cognitive decline, suggesting that visual assessment may better capture clinically meaningful patterns of tau accumulation. These results indicate that current computer-based measurement approaches may need improvement to fully capture the complex ways tau deposits in the brain.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers examined concordance between visual interpretation and quantitative CenTauRz assessment of [18F]flortaucipir PET imaging in 3,991 participants including cognitively unimpaired and cognitively impaired individuals, with visual reads performed by three trained readers and quantification conducted using the CenTauRz pipeline across multiple regions of interest. Cohen κ values indicated moderate concordance between visual positivity and CenTauRz-defined positivity (>2 on the scale), ranging from 0.23–0.55 in cognitively unimpaired participants and 0.57–0.82 in cognitively impaired participants depending on the region examined. Receiver-operating-characteristic analysis demonstrated moderate discriminative power of continuous CenTauRz values across different cut points, with areas under the curve of 0.72–0.87 for cognitively unimpaired individuals and 0.87–0.97 for cognitively impaired individuals. Among discordant cases, participants with visually positive but CenTauRz-negative tau PET scans showed higher amyloid.

title: Longitudinal Phenotyping of Circulating Tumor Cells Using a Scalable Deep Learning Framework.
abstract: Circulating tumor cells (CTC) provide a minimally invasive window into metastatic disease and treatment response, but their clinical utility has been constrained by manual, subjective, low-throughput identification in multichannel fluorescence microscopy data.To address this limitation, we developed and clinically validated the System for Enhanced Evaluation of Tumor Cells (SEE-TC), a deep learning approach for scalable, reproducible phenotyping of individual circulating cells. SEE-TC was developed and evaluated on more than 8.5 million cells from 3,386 blood samples spanning six cancer types, enabling generalization across heterogeneous imaging conditions, staining panels, and acquisition platforms.SEE-TC achieved single-cell segmentation accuracy on par with humans, learned biologically relevant latent cellular representations that correlate with established morphologic and immunofluorescent biomarkers, and reliably distinguished CTCs from background populations without reliance on arbitrary thresholds. When applied longitudinally, SEE-TC provides a quantitative, patient-level readout of CTC burden over time, which was significantly associated with worse overall survival across multiple cancer types.To our knowledge, this is the first fully automated artificial intelligence approach to single-cell segmentation and CTC phenotyping. By transforming CTC analysis from a human-dependent task into a scalable and reproducible digital assay, SEE-TC enables high-fidelity longitudinal monitoring of tumor burden and supports broader clinical deployment of CTC-based liquid biopsies in precision oncology. It is currently being deployed to identify CTCs and quantify target expression for both prognostic and predictive biomarker evaluation in multiple prospective clinical trials on a commercial platform.©2026 American Association for Cancer Research.

llm_summary: Researchers developed an artificial intelligence system called SEE-TC to automatically identify and analyze circulating tumor cells—cancer cells found in blood—from microscopy images, testing it on over 8.5 million cells from thousands of patient samples across six cancer types. The system achieved accuracy comparable to human experts and, when tracking patients over time, found that higher levels of circulating tumor cells were associated with worse survival outcomes. This automated approach could make cancer monitoring through blood tests faster and more reliable for clinical use.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers developed and clinically validated SEE-TC, a deep learning framework for automated segmentation and phenotyping of circulating tumor cells from multichannel fluorescence microscopy images, using data from 3,386 blood samples containing more than 8.5 million cells across six cancer types. The system achieved single-cell segmentation accuracy comparable to manual human analysis while learning biologically relevant latent cellular representations that correlated with established morphologic and immunofluorescent biomarkers. SEE-TC reliably distinguished circulating tumor cells from background cell populations without requiring arbitrary classification thresholds and provided quantitative, patient-level measurements of circulating tumor cell burden over time. Longitudinal circulating tumor cell burden quantified by SEE-TC was significantly associated with worse overall survival across multiple cancer types. This fully automated approach transforms circulating tumor cell analysis from a subjective, labor-intensive manual process into a scalable and reproducible digital assay now being deployed in prospective clinical trials for prognostic and predictive biomarker evaluation.

title: Nucleoporins in Cancer: Functional Roles and Therapeutic Opportunities.
abstract: The nuclear pore complex (NPC) and its building-block proteins, nucleoporins (NUP), play fundamental roles in maintaining cellular fitness by regulating nucleocytoplasmic transport, chromatin and transcriptional activity, and genome stability. These core biological processes are critical for cancer cells, and thus, tumor-driven co-option of NUP-regulated functions has emerged as an important mechanism contributing to the pathogenesis of multiple malignancies. This review discusses how NUP dysregulation mechanistically contributes to tumor initiation and progression and how these insights open opportunities for innovative anticancer therapies, including using clinical-grade molecular glues that induce selective NUP degradation and pharmacologically inhibiting NPC-regulated epigenomic/transcriptomic signaling and nucleocytoplasmic transport.Recent studies demonstrate that NUPs play fundamental roles in cancer pathogenesis by dysregulating key NPC functions and driving tumorigenesis and disease progression. NUPs and NPC-regulated mechanisms can be pharmacologically targeted, providing a strong rationale for developing much-needed innovative therapeutic strategies to combat cancer.©2026 American Association for Cancer Research.

llm_summary: Nucleoporins are proteins that control what enters and exits the cell nucleus, and researchers reviewed evidence that cancer cells abnormally use these proteins to grow and spread. The study identifies how disrupting nucleoporins contributes to tumor development and suggests that new drugs could target these proteins to stop cancer progression. These findings offer potential new treatment approaches, though the review does not present results from a single clinical trial.
llm_summary_expert: This review examines how nucleoporins (NUP) and the nuclear pore complex (NPC) contribute to cancer pathogenesis through dysregulation of nucleocytoplasmic transport, chromatin activity, transcriptional regulation, and genome stability. The authors discuss mechanistic evidence demonstrating that tumor cells co-opt NUP-regulated functions to drive tumorigenesis and disease progression across multiple malignancies. The review identifies pharmacological strategies for targeting NPC dysfunction, including clinical-grade molecular glues that selectively induce NUP degradation and inhibitors of NPC-regulated epigenomic and transcriptomic signaling. Recent studies demonstrate that NUP dysregulation represents a fundamental mechanism in cancer pathogenesis, with NPC-regulated processes serving as viable therapeutic targets. These insights provide a rationale for developing innovative anticancer therapies that exploit NUP and NPC vulnerabilities in tumor cells.

title: Clinical Outcomes after Deprescribing Thyroid Hormone Therapy: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Levothyroxine (LT4) is widely prescribed, often for subclinical hypothyroidism (SCH), despite limited evidence of clinical benefit in patients without overt hypothyroidism. This updated systematic review synthesizes current evidence on biochemical, symptom, and safety outcomes following thyroid hormone (TH) discontinuation.In this systematic review, electronic databases were searched from inception to September 25, 2026, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational studies evaluating supervised TH discontinuation. Primary outcomes included postdiscontinuation thyroid function, symptom changes, adverse events, and need for therapy reinitiation. Random-effects meta-analyses estimated pooled proportions and mean differences.Twenty-three studies met inclusion criteria (22 observational studies, 1 RCT), most evaluating LT4 monotherapy discontinuation (n = 20). Twenty-one studies including 2020 participants reported categorical TH status outcomes; 37% of participants (CI, 26%-48%; I2 = 94.5%) remained euthyroid after discontinuation. Euthyroidism was less frequent among patients with initial overt hypothyroidism (11%, CI, 2%-38%) than among those with SCH (41%, CI, 21%-65%). Eleven studies (1104 participants) reported TH reinitiation, with 60% of patients restarting therapy (CI, 39%-78%; I2 = 97.1%) in the overall population, increasing to 87% (CI, 66%-96%) among those with overt hypothyroidism. Thyroid autoantibody positivity, heterogeneous thyroid ultrasound findings, and higher baseline TSH levels were associated with therapy reinitiation. Thyroid-related symptoms after discontinuation were generally unchanged, and adverse events were uncommon.Approximately 37% of patients remained euthyroid after TH discontinuation, with higher success rates among those initially treated for SCH. These findings support consideration of deprescribing in selected patients, particularly those without clear indications for treatment initiation, using a structured approach with close biochemical monitoring and predefined criteria for therapy reinitiation.

llm_summary: Researchers reviewed studies on stopping thyroid hormone therapy, particularly in patients with mild thyroid problems, to see if they could safely discontinue treatment. About 37% of patients remained healthy after stopping the medication, with better outcomes among those who had mild rather than severe thyroid disease. The findings suggest that stopping thyroid hormone may be safe for some patients when done carefully with medical monitoring, though most patients with severe thyroid disease needed to restart treatment.
llm_summary_expert: This updated systematic review synthesized evidence from 23 studies (22 observational, 1 RCT) including 2020 participants who underwent supervised discontinuation of thyroid hormone therapy, primarily levothyroxine monotherapy. The findings support consideration of deprescribing.

title: Exercise Right Atrial Stiffness From Pressure-Volume Loops and Prognosis in Pulmonary Hypertension.
abstract: In pulmonary hypertension (PH), risk assessment focuses on right ventricular function and may overlook exercise-related right atrial (RA) functional limitation. We investigated whether RA stiffness during exercise reflects impaired right-heart filling reserve and is associated with prognosis beyond conventional measures.We prospectively enrolled 68 participants in this observational study, including 42 with precapillary PH. Participants who had PH ruled out and patients with postcapillary PH formed reference groups. Participants underwent 3-dimensional echocardiography, right heart catheterization, and invasive RA pressure-volume loop analysis at rest and during standardized semisupine exercise. RA filling stiffness was derived from the reservoir phase. Patients with precapillary PH were stratified by median exercise RA filling stiffness.At rest, high- and low-stiffness groups had comparable right ventricular function, afterload, and cardiac index, but the high-stiffness group exhibited impaired phasic RA strain and venous congestion (median [interquartile range] liver stiffness, 7.1 [6.0-8.8] versus 5.2 [4.8-5.8] kPa; P=0.021). During exercise, mean RA pressure increased similarly, but the high-stiffness group had impaired peak cardiac index (3.3±1.0 versus 4.1±0.9 L/min per m2; P=0.015) and RA strain. Unlike resting RA stiffness, high exercise RA stiffness was independently associated with mortality (adjusted hazard ratio, 4.37 [95% CI, 1.20-15.96]). A model including RA conduit strain and right ventricular functional reserve discriminated high RA stiffness (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.90).RA stiffness during exercise integrates resting congestion with limited cardiac reserve and unmasks mortality risk missed by resting metrics. RA conduit strain and right ventricular functional reserve noninvasively identify the high-stiffness subgroup.

title: Teaching Physiology Through Comparative Framing: Effects on Physiological Reasoning in Undergraduate and Graduate Exercise Physiology Students.
abstract: Background: Developing students' ability to transfer physiological principles across contexts remains challenging in physiology education. Comparative framing (CF), in which physiological principles are presented through nonhuman examples, may facilitate transfer by organizing reasoning around variation in environmental challenges and physiological function. However, whether benefits arises from CF itself or engagement with physiologically rich examples remains unclear. Methods: A between-semester controlled design was conducted across undergraduate (n = 99) and graduate (n = 43) exercise physiology courses. Semesters were randomly assigned to CF or human-centered framing (HF), with instructional content and structure held constant. Primary outcomes were parallel, non-identical transfer assessments administered before instruction, immediately afterward, and at delayed follow-up. Secondary outcomes included a content equivalence assessment, a two-tier conceptual reasoning measure, and mental effort ratings. Reflective writing was analyzed using inductive thematic analysis. Results: Both conditions demonstrated comparable content acquisition. Significant Framing x Time interactions were observed for Systems and Adaptive Integration and Translational Application, but not Mechanistic Reasoning. The benefits of CF were concentrated in reasoning tasks requiring context-dependent interpretation and integration of physiological principles and became more pronounced at delayed follow-up. Reflective writing analyses converged with the quantitative findings, with the largest thematic differences observed in adaptive versus pathological reasoning. Conclusion: CF produced more durable physiological reasoning despite comparable content learning, suggesting that its educational value extends beyond engaging students with physiologically rich examples alone. Organizing physiology around context, function, and physiological trade-offs may provide a framework for promoting transfer and context-dependent physiological reasoning.

llm_summary: Researchers tested whether teaching physiology through examples from different animal species, rather than focusing only on humans, would help undergraduate and graduate students better apply what they learned to new situations. Students taught using comparative examples showed stronger reasoning skills when solving problems that required them to interpret and adapt physiological principles to different contexts, with these benefits becoming more noticeable weeks later. The findings suggest that organizing physiology around how different organisms solve environmental challenges may help students transfer their knowledge more effectively than traditional human-centered instruction.

title: National Cross-Sectional Survey of Surgical Education Fellowships in the US.
abstract: Surgical education fellowships prepare future surgeon-educators, yet national data describing training requirements and institutional support are limited. We characterized fellowship structure, educational responsibilities, and resources to inform program development and prospective fellows.A national cross-sectional survey of accredited and non-accredited U.S. surgical education fellowships was conducted from April to December 2024. Representatives submitted collaborative program-level responses addressing structure, professional development, teaching, simulation, research infrastructure, and mentorship. Data were analyzed descriptively.Nineteen of 28 identified fellowships responded (68%), including 15 accredited and 4 non-accredited programs. Teaching was required by 16 programs (84%), simulation coordination and instruction by 17 (89%), and curriculum development by 15 (79%). However, only 10 programs (53%) reported departmental Education PhD support, and 12 (63%) provided access to statisticians at no cost. Sixteen programs (84%) offered fully funded fellowship positions. Three programs (16%) required completion of an advanced degree during the fellowship. Eight programs (42%) reserved positions for internal candidates. National conference attendance was required by 16 programs (84%). Fourteen programs (74%) had a single fellowship director; among directors with available data (n=21), median dedicated full-time equivalent was 0.2 (IQR 0,1).U.S. surgical education fellowships share substantial teaching and simulation responsibilities but differ in institutional resources, professional development opportunities, and leadership support. These national descriptive findings provide improved transparency for prospective applicants, inform future fellowship development and resource allocation, and can guide research on graduate outcomes and accreditation. Longitudinal research is needed to determine how program characteristics and accreditation relate to graduate outcomes.Copyright © 2026 by the American College of Surgeons. llm_summary: Researchers surveyed surgical education fellowship programs across the United States to understand their structure and resources available to trainees. Most programs required teaching and simulation work, but fewer than half had dedicated support for advanced degrees or statisticians, and fellowship directors typically spent only a small fraction of their time on the role. These findings reveal significant variation in how programs support future surgeon-educators and can help prospective fellows understand what to expect.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers conducted a national cross-sectional survey from April to December 2024 of accredited and non-accredited U. S. surgical education fellowships, with 19 of 28 identified programs responding (68%), to characterize fellowship structure, educational responsibilities, and institutional resources through collaborative program-level responses. title: The Contour Neurovascular System Versus Woven Endobridge for Endovascular Embolization of Cerebral Aneurysms: A Propensity Score-matched Cohort Study.
abstract: The Woven Endobridge (WEB) and the Contour Neurovascular System (Contour) are both intrasaccular devices used to treat cerebral aneurysms. We compared outcomes of these 2 devices using data from 2 large registries.Data were sourced from the WorldWideWEB Consortium, which included 1363 cases treated with WEB from 2017, and a registry of 277 Contour cases from 10 European centers starting the same year. Patient demographics, aneurysm characteristics, procedural specifics, and outcomes were analyzed. Propensity score matching was applied for comparison.Before matching, the Contour group had more men (37.9% vs 30.8%), more asymptomatic cases (83.4% vs 70.3%), and fewer acute subarachnoid hemorrhage cases (10.8% vs 26.2%). After matching, no significant differences were found in demographics or aneurysm characteristics between groups. The median age was 60 years, and median aneurysm dimensions were comparable. Logistic regression showed no significant differences between WEB and Contour in achieving complete occlusion (odds ratio [OR] = 1.01, 95% CI, 0.67-1.52, P = .971), adequate occlusion (OR = 0.85, 95% CI, 0.41-1.76, P = .665), or achieving modified Rankin Scale 0 to 2 at last follow-up (OR = 0.48, 95% CI, 0.21-1.02, P = .064). Retreatment (OR = 2.23, P = .086), thromboembolic complications (OR = 0.75, P = .452), and adjunctive treatment use (OR = 1.93, P = .141) were also similar.The WEB and Contour demonstrated comparable clinical and angiographic outcomes in this large multicenter study comprised majority small, asymptomatic cerebral aneurysms.Copyright © Congress of Neurological Surgeons 2026. llm_summary: Researchers compared two devices used to treat brain aneurysms—the Woven Endobridge and the Contour Neurovascular System—by analyzing data from over 1,600 patients across multiple centers. Both devices achieved similar rates of aneurysm closure and patient outcomes, with no significant differences in complications or the need for additional treatment. The findings suggest these two intrasaccular devices perform comparably for treating small, asymptomatic brain aneurysms.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers compared clinical and angiographic outcomes between the Woven Endobridge (WEB) and Contour Neurovascular System, two intrasaccular devices for cerebral aneurysm treatment, using data from 1363 WEB cases from the WorldWideWEB Consortium and 277 Contour cases from 10 European centers, with propensity score matching applied to balance baseline differences. After matching, the cohorts were comparable with median age 60 years and similar aneurysm dimensions, and logistic regression analysis showed no significant differences in complete occlusion (odds ratio 1.01), adequate occlusion (odds ratio 0.85), or functional outcome at last follow-up (odds ratio 0.48). Retreatment rates, thromboembolic complications, and adjunctive treatment use were also similar between the two devices. The study population consisted predominantly of small, asymptomatic cerebral aneurysms, which limits generalizability to other aneurysm presentations. Both devices demonstrated comparable safety and efficacy profiles in this large multicenter cohort.

title: Gender Diversity in Pediatric Chronic Orthostatic Intolerance: Mental Health and Quality-of-Life Outcomes.
abstract: This retrospective medical record review examined the proportion of transgender and gender-diverse (TGD) youth within a multidisciplinary pediatric autonomic dysfunction clinic specializing in chronic orthostatic intolerance, compared quality-of-life (QoL) scores between TGD and cisgender youth, and identified opportunities to improve health equity in nonpharmacological recommendations. Data on gender identity, mental health conditions, and QoL scores, were collected over 2 years. Among 145 youth, 6.9% identified as TGD, a proportion higher than population estimates. Transgender and gender-diverse youth had a significantly lower total QoL, with lower scores in social and emotional domains, and demonstrated higher rates of depression and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder; all TGD youth had an anxiety diagnosis. Overall, TGD youth demonstrated more frequent mental health concerns and greater QoL impairments than cisgender peers. Future studies are needed to determine specific mental health needs and if individualized treatment plans or adaptations to standard nonpharmacological recommendations improve outcomes in TGD youth.

Transgender and gender-diverse youth, who made up nearly 7% of the clinic population, reported significantly lower quality of life and higher rates of depression and anxiety than their cisgender counterparts. title: Feature Selection and Machine Learning Strategies to Develop a Minimal Bioassay for Cholangiocarcinoma Subtype.
abstract: To demonstrate that the combination of feature selection and machine learning methods can curate affordable, accurate RNA sequencing-based assays for cholangiocarcinoma subtype that achieve comparable results to expensive, time-intensive multiomic analysis.From 43 cholangiocarcinomas treated at Mayo Clinic in Minnesota (May 1, 1996, to July 30, 2019) and 206 treated at Fudan University in China (2009 to 2015), 35,449 RNA, protein, and phosphoprotein features were extracted. These multiomic features were used to assign patients to 3 molecular classes. Important RNA sequencing features were selected by competing feature selection methods. Machine learning classification models were tested on each feature set. Accuracy, F1 score, area under the curve, precision, and recall were validated for each feature selection and predictive model combination, bootstrapping using up-sampled, class-balanced data. A custom function of physical assay cost and classification accuracy was optimized to find the best assay. The best feature selection and model combination was tested with reserved data.A set of 20 RNA transcripts was identified as sufficient for classification with gradient boosted trees when optimizing number of features and overall accuracy simultaneously. Reserved data testing demonstrated an accuracy of 83.8% (75.1% to 92.3%); precision, 82.9% (73.3% to 92.5%); recall, 87.2% (74.8% to 99.7%); and area under the curve, 0.961 (0.925 to 0.997). Metabolic pathways were overrepresented among the features selected.Feature selection methods and predictive machine learning models work synchronously to accurately reproduce the results of a complex multiomic subtype assay based on limited RNA sequencing. This methodologic framework is a potential pathway to integrate research multiomic subtyping for molecularly complex cancers into a realistic clinical setting.Copyright © 2026 Mayo Foundation for Medical Education and Research. A simplified test based on these 20 genes correctly classified cancer subtypes about 84% of the time, matching the accuracy of the more elaborate approach. title: Efficacy and Safety of Evogliptin in Mild to Moderate Calcific Aortic Valve Stenosis: The EVOID-AS Trial Rationale and Study Design.
abstract: The only treatment of severe aortic stenosis (AS) is aortic valve replacement. No medical therapy has been proven effective for preventing or delaying AS progression despite several clinical trials. The EVOID-AS trial is designed to evaluate the efficacy of evogliptin, a dipeptidyl peptidase 4 inhibitor, at retarding the progression of aortic valve calcification and AS hemodynamic severity in patients with mild to moderate AS. In this trial, 580 patients with mild or moderate native calcific AS at 40+ clinical sites across the United States and Canada will be randomized in a 1:1 allocation to receive either evogliptin 10 mg or placebo once daily orally for 2 years. Clinical follow-up visits are scheduled at 3-month intervals; transthoracic echocardiography, aortic valve computed tomography calcium score, and laboratory testing are obtained at baseline, 1-year, and 2-year study visits. The primary end point is change in aortic valve calcification as measured by cardiac computed tomography at 2 years of therapy. Secondary end points are progression of AS hemodynamic severity by echocardiography during 2 years of therapy and time to aortic valve intervention. Secondary safety end points include incidence and severity of treatment-emergent or serious adverse events. Enrollment began in June 2022, and the study is expected to be completed in 2028. EVOID-AS is a double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized medical trial to modify the progression of calcific AS. This trial will contribute to the critical unmet clinical need of identifying an effective medical therapy to prevent or to delay the progression of AS. title: Antecedent Kidney Function and Cardiovascular Mortality in Over 300 000 Patients With Incident Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction.
abstract: Chronic kidney disease is a frequent comorbidity in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and has been proposed as a contributor to its development. However, the spectrum of antecedent kidney function before incident HFpEF and its association with subsequent cardiovascular outcomes remains unclear.We conducted a multicenter cohort study across 170 US Veterans Affairs hospitals, including patients with incident HFpEF diagnosed between January 1, 2000, and June 30, 2025. HFpEF was ascertained using natural language processing-derived left ventricular ejection fraction ≥50% closest to the incident HF date and a validated HFpEF algorithm incorporating loop diuretic use, elevated natriuretic peptide levels, and an HFpEF-age, body mass index, and atrial fibrillation score >0.5. Antecedent kidney function was classified using 2 estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) measurements obtained ≥90 days apart before incident HFpEF and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio. We characterized antecedent kidney function, including albuminuria (urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio ≥30 mg/g), and examined its associations with 5-year cardiovascular death and heart failure hospitalization. Competing-risk analysis was performed accounting for noncardiovascular death as a competing event for cardiovascular death.Of 304 712 patients meeting HFpEF ascertainment criteria, 236 910 comprised the final cohort; 51% had antecedent eGFR ≥60 mL/min per 1.73m2. Overall, 15% had an eGFR ≥90 mL/min per 1.73m2. Patients with eGFR <60 mL/min per 1.73m2 were older and had more diabetes and hypertension. 51% of the patients with eGFR <60 mL/min per 1.73m2 had body mass index <30 kg/m2, including 20% with body mass index <25 kg/m2. Progressively lower antecedent kidney function was associated with graded increases in cardiovascular death and heart failure hospitalization. title: MRI-based biomarkers for risk stratification and assessment of treatment response in Metabolic dysfunction-associated Steatotic liver disease.
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects up to 38% of the population globally. Liver biopsy, the historical reference standard, is invasive, subject to sampling error and not scalable. MRI-based biomarkers provide non-invasive, quantitative whole liver assessment. MRI proton density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF) is the most accurate noninvasive measure of steatosis (thresholds of 6.4%, 17.4% and 22.1% for grades ≥1, ≥2 and 3), and a ≥30% relative reduction is associated with histologic response. Liver stiffness by magnetic resonance elastography (MRE-LS) is the most accurate imaging biomarker for fibrosis: MRE-LS of 3.1-4.4 kPa corresponds to F2-F3 and ≥5 kPa to cirrhosis, and each 1-kPa increase is associated with a 43% higher risk of hepatic decompensation. Iron-corrected T1 is a sensitive but nonspecific marker of disease activity whose prognostic value requires further study. Composite scores, MAST, MEFIB, and MASH Resolution Index, combine imaging and blood tests for advanced fibrosis diagnosis and response assessment. MRE is cost-effective compared with vibration-controlled transient elastography for detecting advanced fibrosis. Artificial intelligence may broaden access by automating analysis and enabling PDFF from routine MRI. We review the evidence supporting these biomarkers for diagnosis, prognosis and regulatory use, and their role in clinical trials and in treatment decisions for approved MASH therapies.Copyright © 2026 American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases.

title: Delirium and Long-Term Cognitive Trajectories in Cognitively Unimpaired Adults.
abstract: Delirium is a state of acute confusion characterized by deficits in attention that occurs commonly during hospitalization and is associated with adverse outcomes; however, the association of delirium with longitudinal cognitive trajectories is not fully understood.To evaluate the association of delirium during hospitalization with subsequent development of mild cognitive impairment (MCI), dementia, and longitudinal cognitive trajectories.This cohort study used data from participants with hospitalizations in the Mayo Clinic Study of Aging (MCSA) from October 2004 to December 2023. The MCSA is a prospective, population-based longitudinal study of cognitive aging among residents of Olmsted County, Minnesota. Of participants enrolled in the MCSA between 2004 and 2023, individuals who experienced 1 or more hospitalization prior to their last MCSA encounter were included in this study. Participants with dementia at MCSA enrollment or prior to first hospitalization were excluded. Follow-up continued until development of MCI or dementia, last MCSA visit, or the end of the study.Delirium was identified using a validated natural language processing algorithm applied to clinical notes from hospitalizations, associated emergency department visits, and follow-up within 30 days after hospitalization. Delirium status was modeled as a time-dependent exposure.Incident MCI and dementia were assigned through MCSA expert consensus evaluations, including neuropsychological testing performed every 15 months. Association between delirium and development of MCI or dementia was assessed using Cox proportional hazards regression, adjusted for patient age, sex, level of education, and apolipoprotein E (APOE) ε4 allele carrier status; cognitive trajectories were assessed with linear mixed-effects models.Of 7030 participants enrolled in the MCSA, 3542 individuals experienced 1 or more hospitalization prior to their last MCSA encounter and were included, and 41 participants with dementia at enrollment or prior to first hospitalization were excluded. The cohort included 3501 participants with at least 1 hospitalization. Median (IQR) age was 74.1 (66.6-80.9) years, 1676 participants (47.9%) were female, median (IQR) level of education was 14 (12-16) years, and 910 participants (26.0%) were APOE ε4 carriers. During a median (IQR) follow-up of 7.2 (4.1-10.4) years, 75 participants (2.1%) had delirium documented within 30 days of hospitalization. Delirium was associated with increased risk of MCI (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 3.67; 95% CI, 2.19-6.15) and dementia (aHR, 5.39; 95% CI, 2.94-9.85) and with accelerated decline in longitudinal cognitive testing.In this cohort study among adults in the MCSA, including those with unimpaired cognition at baseline, delirium during hospitalization was strongly associated with increased risk of MCI and dementia and accelerated cognitive decline in subsequent years.

title: Global Epidemiology of Neonatal and Infantile-Onset Epilepsies and Epilepsy Syndromes (GENIE): A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Despite the profound impact of neonatal and infantile-onset epilepsies on neurodevelopmental outcomes and mortality, consolidated global epidemiological evidence remains lacking.To estimate the global incidence and prevalence of neonatal and infantile-onset epilepsies and epilepsy syndromes and to characterize their associated etiological profiles.PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched from inception through December 18, 2025.Population-based observational studies reporting the incidence or prevalence of neonatal and infantile-onset epilepsies or epilepsy syndromes were eligible for inclusion.Two authors independently and in duplicate performed study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment of included studies using the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal checklist for prevalence studies. Generalized linear mixed-model random-effects meta-analysis was used to pool the estimates of incidence, prevalence, and etiology. Subgroup meta-analyses were conducted by country, World Health Organization (WHO) region, World Bank income, and diagnostic criteria. Metaregression was used to investigate the association between study-level covariates and pooled incidence estimates of infantile-onset epilepsy syndromes.Cumulative incidence and prevalence of neonatal and infantile-onset epilepsies and epilepsy syndromes.A total of 86 population-based studies from 30 countries across 4 WHO regions were included. The pooled cumulative incidence of infantile-onset epilepsies within the first 2 years of life was 236.0 cases (95% CI, 164.7-338.2; 95% prediction interval [PI], 53.0-1044.3) per 100 000 live births. Among epilepsy syndrome subgroups, developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEEs) had the highest incidence at 67.7 cases (95% CI, 42.1-108.9; 95% PI, 7.1-636.1) per 100 000 live births. Infantile epileptic spasms syndrome (IESS) was the most incident DEE, with 31.6 cases (95% CI, 27.5-36.2; 95% PI, 13.7-72.6) per 100 000 live births. Among self-limited epilepsies, self-limited infantile epilepsy had the highest incidence at 13.0 cases (95% CI, 9.2-18.2; 95% PI, 6.4-26.4) per 100 000 live births. Subgroup analyses revealed limited geographical representativeness, with the majority of studies from high-income countries in the European Region.The findings underscore a significant global burden of neonatal and infantile-onset epilepsies, primarily driven by DEEs, specifically IESS. Given substantial between-study heterogeneity, the pooled estimates should be interpreted as broad indicators rather than precise, generalizable rates. Geographic disparities, with a lack of data from the African and Eastern Mediterranean Regions, underscore the need for population-based studies in underrepresented regions and longitudinal research on survival, remission, and functional outcomes.

title: Risk of Obstructive Sleep Apnea in Open-Angle Glaucoma: A Population-Based Cohort Study.
abstract: In this retrospective population-based cohort study, patients with open-angle glaucoma were more likely to develop obstructive sleep apnea than matched controls from the general population of Olmsted County, Minnesota.To investigate the risk of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) in patients with open-angle glaucoma (OAG) compared to the risk of OSA in matched controls from a general population.Retrospective population-based case-control study comparing the incidence of OSA with a diagnosis of OAG (cases) to the incidence of OSA in matched patients without OAG (controls) from Olmsted County, Minnesota between January 1, 1980 and December 31, 2018. Patients were identified using the Rochester Epidemiology Project. Medical records were reviewed to confirm OAG diagnoses. OSA diagnoses were based on sleep study data and polysomnography parameters. Cumulative probability of OSA was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method.This cohort had 7,000 patients: 3,500 case patients with OAG diagnosed at any time point, and 3,500 matched control subjects without OAG, with all OAG and OSA diagnoses manually confirmed. There was no statistically significant difference of OSA frequency prior to index date in cases versus controls (P=0.52). There were 371 (12.5%) cases who developed OSA after glaucoma diagnosis compared to 297 (10.2%) patients who were diagnosed with OSA after the index date (P=0.0068). The multivariate hazard ratio for diagnosis of OSA after OAG diagnosis was 1.17 (P=0.047, 95% CI: 1.00, 1.36). The 10-year absolute risk of OSA after OAG diagnosis was 12.5%, and risk of OSA increased with time.In this population-based study, patients with OAG were more likely to be diagnosed with OSA compared to patients without OAG, suggesting a possible association that may justify increased clinical awareness.Copyright © 2026 Wolters Kluwer Health, LLC. title: Effects of Concomitant Medications on Clinical and Immunological Outcomes of Cancer Patients Treated With Oncolytic Adenoviruses.
abstract: Medication taken for other reasons than for the treatment of malignant disease, termed concomitant medication, is known to affect outcomes when used with immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy and other oncological drugs. However, no research in humans has addressed the relationship between concomitant medications and efficacy of oncolytic adenovirus (OAd) therapy. We retrospectively collected medication history of 290 patients enrolled in the Advanced Therapy Access Program (ATAP), an individualized treatment program of OAds. We analyzed associations of different concomitant medications with overall survival and imaging response following therapy. Additionally, to provide further insights into mechanisms using tissue samples, we collected concomitant medication data, tumor transcriptomic data and serum proteomic data from recent Phase I clinical trials with OAd igrelimogene litadenorepvec (Ad5/3-E2F-d24-hTNF-IRES-hIL2, TILT-123). In ATAP, acetaminophen (paracetamol), opium alkaloids, anti-emetics, proton pump inhibitors, beta blockers, laxatives, and antidepressants use showed a statistical association with shorter overall survival. Use of lipid-modifying drugs (statins) and thyroid hormones showed a statistical association with better disease control in imaging. In clinical trials with TILT-123, beta blockers, anti-emetics, opioids, and benzodiazepines showed a statistical association with shorter overall survival, and lipid-modifying drugs and thyroid hormones showed a statistical association with improved disease control. Tumor transcriptomic and serum proteomic analysis showed varied temporal and locational effects on inflammatory response varying by drug class. The results provide the first human data suggesting that OAd therapy outcomes might be influenced by concomitant medications. title: Identifying novel genomic alterations in relapsed childhood B-ALL: a report from the Children's Oncology Group.
abstract: Relapsed B-acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) generally occurs due to the emergence of subclones resistant to therapy, leading to poor outcome. Here, we describe novel genomic alterations responsible for therapeutic resistance at a subtype level in a clinical trial (AALL1331) which randomized patients to blinatumomab and chemotherapy versus chemotherapy alone. We performed whole-genome and transcriptome sequencing on 288 patients (183 diagnosis/first relapse/germline trios and 105 additional patients with first-relapse samples) and analyzed 41 second-relapse samples. For ETV6::RUNX1, we showed that cases with gain of the fusion allele or with fusion transcript involving exon 5 of ETV6 and exon 4 of RUNX1 (E5-E4) had a higher risk of first relapse than cases with E5-E3. For the hyperdiploid subtype, we demonstrated that low modal chromosomal numbers (51-52) were more prone to first relapse than those with ≥53 chromosomes, with an additive effect of CREBBP mutations. title: Antithrombotic Therapy After Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion: The SIMPLAAFY Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract: Following a left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) procedure, antithrombotic therapy is administered to safely allow time for device endothelialization. However, the optimal postimplant antithrombotic regimen is unknown.To determine if either reduced-dose non-vitamin K oral anticoagulants (NOACs) or aspirin alone are noninferior to dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) for the composite clinical end point of death, stroke, systemic embolism, or major bleeding through 6 months post LAAC.This open-label, 3-group, multicenter clinical trial randomized 1857 patients between October 2024 and December 2025 at 87 US investigational sites, with the final 6-month follow-up in July 2026. Enrolled patients had nonvalvular atrial fibrillation, underwent successful LAAC, and were eligible for all 3 regimens.Patients were randomly allocated 1:1:1 to DAPT for 6 months followed by aspirin (n = 624), a reduced-dose NOAC for 3 months followed by aspirin (n = 620), or aspirin alone for 12 months (n = 613).The primary outcome was the 6-month composite of all-cause death, stroke, systemic embolism, or major bleeding. Noninferiority was tested in the primary analysis population with a 1-sided Farrington-Manning test (α = .025). Bleeding and 45-day device-related thrombus rates were exploratory without multiplicity adjustment.The cohort had a mean age of 76 (SD, 8) years, 42.9% were female, the mean CHA2DS2-VASc score was 4.2 (SD, 1.3), and 68.0% had paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. The primary outcome occurred in 41 patients (6.9%) with DAPT vs 31 (5.1%) with a reduced-dose NOAC (risk ratio, 0.75 [95% CI, 0.48-1.18]; risk difference, -1.7 percentage points; 97.5% upper bound, 1.2) and 20 (3.3%) with aspirin alone (risk ratio, 0.49 [95% CI, 0.29-0.82]; risk difference, -3.5 percentage points; 97.5% upper bound, -0.8). Both monotherapy strategies met noninferiority criteria (P < .001 for noninferiority for both). Major bleeding was 4.5% with DAPT, 2.7% with reduced-dose NOACs, and 1.7% with aspirin alone; clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding was 8.7%, 4.8%, and 3.8%, respectively. Device-related thrombus was observed in 3.4%, 0.9%, and 2.7%, respectively.Both reduced-dose NOACs and aspirin alone were noninferior to DAPT for 6-month outcomes after uncomplicated LAAC.ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06521463.

title: Persistent Circulating Proteomic Signatures Distinguish Magnetic Resonance Angiography-Defined Carotid Plaque Vulnerability.
abstract: Carotid artery luminal stenosis alone may not predict the risk of future neurovascular events. Plaque vulnerability is emerging as an independent predictor of higher risk for a neurovascular event. We evaluated blood proteomics, paired with high-resolution cross-sectional imaging preoperatively. From preoperative and postoperative blood samples, our objective was to identify blood proteins that distinguish patients with vulnerable and non-vulnerable carotid artery plaques.We conducted an exploratory, single-center proteomic study of 27 consecutive patients undergoing carotid endarterectomy with preoperative 3.0T magnetic resonance angiography with vessel wall imaging. Plaques were classified as vulnerable when magnetic resonance angiography with vessel wall imaging identified at least one high-risk feature: thin fibrous cap, lipid-rich necrotic core, ulceration, intraplaque hemorrhage, or inflammation. Serum samples were analyzed preoperatively and postoperatively using a high-throughput, untargeted proteomics technology (Olink). Differential protein abundance between vulnerable and non-vulnerable groups was assessed separately at each time point.For both time points, the vulnerable group demonstrated a blood proteomic signature involving diacylglycerol signaling and oxidative stress proteins, including diacylglycerol kinase iota and peroxiredoxin-like 2B, with postoperative vulnerability additionally associated with platelet activation (Ras guanyl releasing protein 2), cytoskeletal remodeling (metastasis suppressor 1), and ribonucleic acid/ribosome-related proteins (Shwachman-Bodian-Diamond syndrome protein, RNA-binding protein with multiple splicing 2, zinc ribbon domain-containing protein 2). Non-vulnerable plaques showed a higher abundance of proteins involved in cellular maintenance and deoxyribonucleic acid repair. Furthermore, the persistence of higher diacylglycerol kinase iota and peroxiredoxin-like 2B in the vulnerable group and X-ray repair cross-complementing protein 2 in the non-vulnerable group at both time points suggests stable, patient-level systemic differences detectable in blood, despite plaque removal.Serum proteomics identified distinct systemic pathways associated with cross-sectional imaging carotid plaque vulnerability, highlighting diacylglycerol signaling, oxidative stress, and platelet activation as candidate mechanisms and new biomarker candidates for risk stratification, symptom surveillance, and targeted medical interventions.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. title: Fatty acid desaturation controls cellular fate decisions between senescence and ferroptosis.
abstract: When subject to damage or stress, cells develop responses in order to maintain tissue homeostasis. Two such responses are ferroptosis and cellular senescence, but how cells decide between these outcomes remains unclear. Here, we show that senescent cells increase import and membrane levels of multiple polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs), but a specific intermediate PUFA, dihomo-gamma-linolenic acid (DGLA, 20:3ω-6), is reduced. Exogenous repletion of DGLA instead results in cell death by ferroptosis. Senescent cells manifest additional features associated with ferroptosis, including labile iron and expression of lipoxygenases as well as low-level membrane peroxidation. Oral DGLA supplementation lowers markers of senescence in aged mice and improves age-related functional outcomes. Finally, obese humans with lowered DGLA desaturation rates have lower markers of adipose tissue senescence. Together, our data implicate shifts in PUFA metabolism as a driver of decisions between senescence and ferroptosis.Copyright © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.
