title: Industrialization drives convergent microbiome and host physiological shifts in the human metaorganism.
abstract: Understanding how industrialization reshapes the human metaorganism requires integrating microbiome ecology with host physiology across globally diverse populations. Here, we generate multivariate data from the Global Microbiome Conservancy cohort, including gut microbiome, immunoglobulin A (IgA) sequencing, host genotyping, diet, lifestyle, and fecal biomarker profiles, to investigate host-microbiome interactions across gradients of industrialization and geography. We show that industrialization is associated with homogenized microbial compositions, reduced microbial diversity, and lower community stability, independent of host confounders. We further show that industrialization is linked to elevated markers of gut stress, increased IgA secretion, and altered patterns of IgA-bacteria interactions. Finally, we show that microbiome-based disease predictors trained on industrialized populations are uninformative in less industrialized cohorts, highlighting limited cross-population transferability. Together, our results reveal coordinated restructuring of the microbial ecosystem and host physiology and emphasize the need for inclusive, globally representative data to improve translational microbiome applications across diverse human populations.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). llm_summary: Researchers examined how industrialization affects the gut bacteria and immune system of people across different populations worldwide. They found that industrialization is associated with less diverse gut bacteria, increased signs of gut stress, and stronger immune responses, while these patterns differ significantly between industrialized and less industrialized communities. This suggests that disease prediction tools developed in industrialized populations may not work effectively for people in other parts of the world.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers examined host-microbiome interactions across gradients of industrialization using multivariate data from the Global Microbiome Conservancy cohort, including gut microbiome composition, IgA sequencing, host genotyping, diet, lifestyle, and fecal biomarkers. Industrialization was associated with homogenized microbial compositions, reduced microbial diversity, and lower community stability independent of host confounders. Industrialization was linked to elevated markers of gut stress, increased IgA secretion, and altered patterns of IgA-bacteria interactions. Microbiome-based disease predictors trained on industrialized populations showed limited cross-population transferability and were uninformative in less industrialized cohorts. These findings reveal coordinated restructuring of the microbial ecosystem and host physiology with industrialization, emphasizing the need for globally representative data to improve translational microbiome applications across diverse human populations.

title: Proliferative Glomerulonephritis With Monotypic Immunoglobulin Deposits of IgG1 Subclass: A Case Series.
abstract: Most cases of proliferative glomerulonephritis with monotypic immunoglobulin deposits (PGNMID) are associated with IgG3. The characteristics of IgG1 deposits within PGNMID have not been well defined and are the focus of this study.Retrospective case series.Forty-six PGNMID cases with granular monotypic IgG1 deposits (PGNMID-IgG1) identified in nephropathology archives.57% of cases were male and 78% had hematuria. The median age was 57 years, the median proteinuria level was 4.8 g/day, and the median eGFR level was 52 mL/min/1.73 m2. Hypocomplementemia was uncommon (12%). Kidney biopsy revealed MPGN (54%) or mesangial proliferative GN (33%), with membranous features in nearly half (43%). A nephropathic clone or monoclonal Ig (mIg) was detected in 19 of 42 patients with PGNMID-IgG1 who underwent evaluation, including 10 with chronic lymphocytic leukemia or small lymphocytic lymphoma (CLL/SLL). Among patients >50 years, the detection rate was 72% (18/25) vs. 6% (1/17) among younger patients. SPEP/SIF detected the nephropathic mIg in 13 of 40, and bone marrow biopsy done in 25 detected clonal B-cells in eight and clonal plasma cells in two patients. Follow-up (median 27 months) was available for 37 patients. Ten (83%) of 12 patients with an identifiable clone or mIg responded to clone-targeted (anti-plasma or B- cell) therapy, whereas 4 of 8 patients without an identifiable clone or mIg responded to anti-plasma cell therapy. At 60 months, the overall cumulative incidence of kidney failure requiring dialysis or death was 31.1% (7.9% to 48.5%). Four patients underwent kidney transplantation and three with transplant biopsies exhibited recurrent disease.Retrospective, single-center study, non-standardized hematologic workup and management.Nearly 75% of PGNMID-IgG1 cases >50 years of age have a clonal population detected and nearly a quarter have CLL/SLL. Response to anti-B-cell therapy may be greater in those with an identifiable clone or mIg. These data may inform treatment strategies for people with PGNMID-IgG1.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). title: Quality of Life and Late Effects Following Haploidentical vs. Matched Unrelated Donor Allogeneic Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation: Secondary Analysis of BMT CTN 1702.
abstract: Quality of life (QoL) is a critical indicator of therapeutic benefit and long-term recovery after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT). The BMT CTN 1702 clinical trial (NCT03904134), a multicenter study (2019-2022) evaluating donor search, selection practices and outcomes of HCT using alternative donor sources, incorporated QoL as a secondary endpoint. The aim of the QoL sub-study was to explore the long-term QoL in a more homogenous subset of patients with AML/ALL in CR1 and early-stage MDS who provided additional clinical and patient-reported outcomes (PRO) data, comparing those receiving matched unrelated donor (MUD) with Haploidentical (Haplo) donors.QoL was assessed using PROMIS measures and the Lee Symptom Scale (LSS). PROs were completed at baseline, 1 and 2 years post-HCT. PRO analysis used a generalized estimating equation linear regression model. Late effects, infection rates, and healthcare utilization were also compared.304 patients were analyzed (61 Haplo and 243 MUD). While PRO submission rates at baseline were similar, retention in the MUD cohort was higher than Haplo (80% and 83% vs. 58% and 60% at year 1 and year 2, respectively). There were no significant differences in QoL between haplo and MUD HCT recipients at baseline or throughout the 2-year post-transplant period. Both groups entered transplantation with substantial impairments in global physical and mental health relative to the U.S. population norms. No significant differences in late effects were observed within 2 years of HCT. The use of Haplo donors was associated with significantly more hospital days (median days 27.0 vs. 21.0, p<0.01). and more viral infections (49.2% vs. 31.8%, p=0.01) in the first 100 days. In a subset analysis restricted to patients receiving PTCy (N=117) for GVHD prophylaxis, the differences in hospital days were diminished; however, differences in viral infection remained (48.2% vs. 28.0%, p=0.02).This study provides evidence that the use of a haplo or MUD donor is not associated with differences in post-HCT QoL trajectories, while highlighting substantial pre-transplant symptom burden across all recipients. Despite similar QoL trajectories and late effect profile, the increased viral infections in Haplo HCT may reflect differences in post-transplant medical complications. Future studies with larger cohorts and longer follow-up will be essential to refine these observations and guide strategies to improve long term outcomes.Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Inc.

title: Isolated CSF Facet Effusions as a Predictor of Lateral Dural Tear Location in Spontaneous Intracranial Hypotension: A Multi-Institutional Study.
abstract: Ventral and lateral spinal dural tears are common causes of spontaneous intracranial hypotension, each requiring different myelographic approaches for leak localization. Spine MRI can infer the presence of a dural tear but has limited utility in localizing leaks. One recent case series described several patients with isolated facet effusions at the site of lateral dural tears. We investigated whether the presence of an isolated facet joint effusion on spine MRI could predict the type and location of a dural tear in patients with spontaneous intracranial hypotension.We identified consecutive patients with precisely localized ventral or lateral dural tears on advanced myelography at three centers. A single neuroradiologist at each center assessed for isolated facet effusions on pre-myelographic spine MRIs, defined as fluid accumulation in a single facet joint that was visually greater than any other joint in the spine. Myelographic studies were reviewed to confirm leak type/location. The frequency of isolated facet effusions was compared between patients with lateral and ventral dural tears using Fisher's exact test. The proximity of facet effusions to leak level/side was assessed.Sixty-four patients (32 ventral and 32 lateral dural tears) were included. All patients had epidural CSF on MRI. Isolated facet effusions were more common in patients with lateral dural tears (21/32, 66%) compared with ventral dural tears (0/32, 0%) (p < .001). The effusion was at the same level and side as the leak in 11/21 (52%) patients and within one ipsilateral spinal level of the leak in 7/21 (33%) patients. Contrast filling of a facet joint was seen in 9/21 (43%) cases and corresponded to the site of MRI effusion in 8/9 (89%).Isolated facet joint effusions on spine MRI were seen exclusively in patients with lateral dural tears and were usually located at or within one ipsilateral spinal level of the leak. This finding may provide a useful imaging clue that there is an underlying lateral dural tear, which is helpful to plan optimal myelographic positioning and technique.© 2026 by American Journal of Neuroradiology.

title: Hematologic Consequences of Radiopharmaceutical Therapy: From Clonal Hematopoiesis to Therapy-Related Myeloid Neoplasms.
abstract: Radiopharmaceutical therapy (RPT) uses radionuclides linked to targeting ligands to bind tumor-associated receptors or antigens and deliver ionizing radiation to malignant cells. Approved agents include [177Lu]Lu-DOTATATE for gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, and 223Ra-dichloride for bone-predominant metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Accumulating evidence suggests that RPT may impose genotoxic stress on the hematopoietic system, resulting in prolonged cytopenias and, in some patients, therapy-related myeloid neoplasms (tMNs). This review synthesizes evidence regarding hematologic toxicities associated with [177Lu]Lu-based RPT, emphasizing mechanisms of marrow injury, limitations of dose-only frameworks, host susceptibility factors, and emerging strategies for risk stratification, monitoring, and mitigation. We propose an integrated radiogenomic framework in which hematologic toxicity and tMN risk after RPT may arise from interactions among prior genotoxic exposure, heterogeneous red marrow radiation delivery, host genomic susceptibility-including clonal hematopoiesis and germline predisposition-and baseline marrow reserve. As RPT moves into earlier lines of therapy and populations with a longer expected survival, anticipating hematologic consequences will be essential for safe and precise clinical implementation.© 2026 by the Society of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging.

title: Penicillin Allergy Delabeling in Children.
abstract: Nearly 10% of the global population has been labeled as having a penicillin allergy. Of those labeled, about 95% are not truly allergic, yet most do not receive any allergy evaluations. Patients with penicillin allergy labels are more likely to have worse clinical outcomes and incur higher health care costs, largely because they do not receive penicillin and other first-line β-lactam antibiotics for the treatment of infectious diseases. Consequently, the process of evaluating and removing inaccurate penicillin allergy labels-a process known as "delabeling"-has become increasingly supported by a growing body of evidence. Recently, penicillin allergy has garnered substantial public interest with the proposal of federal legislation to include evaluation of penicillin allergy during routine medical visits for Medicare patients. Although this moves delabeling into the generalist purview, most of the emphasis on penicillin allergies and delabeling has been on adult patients. Yet, penicillin allergy is a pressing issue for pediatrics, as most penicillin allergy labels are placed in childhood. Pediatric literature similarly demonstrates negative clinical and public health consequences of inaccurate penicillin allergy labels. Recent guidelines have strongly recommended a proactive effort to identify and delabel inaccurate penicillin allergies in children. title: Sellar spine in children and young adults: clinical presentation, imaging characteristics, and pituitary outcomes.
abstract: The true clinical relevance of a sellar spine remains unclear because of limited available data. We aimed to describe the presentation and associated pituitary dysfunction among children and young adults with a sellar spine.We retrospectively reviewed patients with a sellar spine found on brain imaging obtained in individuals less than 25 years of age. Extracted variables included age at initial brain imaging, indication for imaging, and pituitary dysfunction status and type.Eleven patients were included. Age at initial identification of a sellar spine ranged from 6 to 24 years. Indications for neuroimaging included headaches (n=3), seizures (n=2), precocious puberty (n=1), severe obesity with advanced bone age (n=1), suspected stroke/ataxia (n=1), nasal polyp evaluation (n=1), hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and secondary hypothyroidism (n=1), and as part of screening testing for Von Hipple Lindau (n=1). Pituitary stalk deviation was found in 7 patients (63.6 %). Pituitary gland distorted morphology leading to a misdiagnosis of pituitary adenoma found in 2 patients (18.2 %). Among younger children (n=5; age ≤9 years), precocious puberty occurred in one patient who demonstrated pituitary stalk deviation with an AP size-to-sella ratio of 0.5. Another child with stalk deviation did not develop precocious puberty. Pituitary hormone deficiency was identified in one patient (hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and hypothyroidism) with stalk deviation and AP size-to-sella ratio of 0.63.The presence of a sellar spine can distort pituitary anatomy and result in diagnostic misclassification. Endocrinopathies may develop in some affected patients. Most patients had pituitary stalk deviation, and a few developed hormone deficiencies or were initially misdiagnosed with pituitary tumors, though the connection between the spine and these problems remains unclear. llm_summary_expert: Researchers retrospectively reviewed eleven patients aged 6 to 24 years who had a sellar spine identified on brain imaging to characterize clinical presentation and associated pituitary dysfunction. title: Opioid prescribing and pain trajectories after periacetabular osteotomy : epidural versus periarticular injection analgesia.
abstract: Periacetabular osteotomy (PAO) is performed in young, opioid-naive patients and is associated with postoperative pain. Optimizing perioperative analgesia while limiting opioid exposure remains a priority. This study evaluated postoperative pain trajectories, hospital length of stay (LOS), and opioid-prescribing patterns associated with an institutional transition from epidural-based to periarticular injection (PAI)-based analgesia after PAO. Secondary aims were to assess the influence of preoperative opioid exposure and compare outcomes between ropivacaine-based and bupivacaine PAI formulations.The study included 724 patients who underwent PAO between January 2010 and December 2022 at a single academic institution, with epidural use replaced by PAI in 2016. Patients were stratified by postoperative analgesia strategy: epidural catheter (n = 333) or PAI (n = 391). Outcomes included daily postoperative pain scores, LOS, discharge opioid prescriptions (morphine milligram equivalents (MMEs)), total opioid exposure, and 30-day refill rates. Statistical comparisons were performed using chi-squared, Fisher's exact, and Kruskal-Wallis tests.Baseline characteristics were similar between groups. Epidural analgesia was associated with lower pain scores during the first 48 hours (last pain postoperative day 0 to 1: mean 2.9 (SD 2.0) vs 4.7 (SD 2.1); p < 0.001), whereas the PAI group had a shorter LOS (mean 2.2 days (SD 1.0) vs 3.4 days (SD 0.9); p < 0.001) and higher pain scores at discharge (mean 4.8 (SD 1.9) vs 4.0 (SD 1.9); p < 0.001). Median discharge opioid prescriptions (313 (IQR 225 to 388) vs 825 (IQR 600 to 1,000) MMEs) and total 30-day opioid exposure (360 (IQR 275 to 575) vs 900 (IQR 638 to 1,100) MMEs) were lower in the PAI group (both p < 0.001), while refill rates were higher (34.0% vs 19.2%; p < 0.001). title: Cost-Effectiveness of Anterior and Posterior Surgical Approaches for Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy: An Economic Evaluation of a Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract: Surgery for cervical spondylotic myelopathy improves quality of life but remains expensive. We conducted a cost-effectiveness analysis of patients treated with anterior cervical diskectomy/fusion (ACDF), posterior cervical decompression/fusion (PCDF), and laminoplasty (LP) in the Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy Surgical (CSM-S) Trial, a randomized trial comparing surgical approaches for cervical spondylotic myelopathy.In the trial, patients were randomized (2:3) to anterior (ACDF) or posterior surgery (LP or PCDF, at surgeon's discretion). A cost-effectiveness analysis was performed from a societal perspective with a 1-year time horizon, including only US patients as-treated. Cumulative costs were estimated using patient data on utilization and lost productivity using a human capital approach. Direct costs were calculated using 2022 Medicare rates for professional fees and cost-to-charge ratios for hospital services. Quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs) were calculated from patient responses to the EuroQol-5-Dimensions instrument at baseline and 3, 6, and 12 months postoperatively. Incremental cost-effectiveness ratio analysis was performed with bootstrapping to address uncertainty.Of 163 total patients enrolled in the CSM-S Trial, 153 from the United States (mean age, 62 years; 80 (52%) female) were included as-treated (ACDF = 61, PCDF = 64, LP = 28) in a cost-effectiveness analysis. Economic data were not available for 9 patients. The remaining 144 patients treated (ACDF = 55, PCDF = 61, LP = 28) had cost data through a 1-year follow-up. Mean hospitalization costs were higher after PCDF than ACDF and LP ($33 410 vs $26 468 vs $25 550; P < .001). Mean total costs were higher after PCDF than ACDF and LP ($62 383 vs $53 074 vs $47 426; P = .017). LP yielded greater QALY gains than ACDF (0.792 vs 0.732; P = .08) and PCDF (0.792 vs 0.698; P = .01). At a willingness-to-pay threshold of $150 000/QALY-gained, the probability that LP was cost-effective compared with PCDF was 99.7% and the probability compared with ACDF was 96%.In the CSM-S Trial, LP yielded greater 1-year quality-of-life improvements at lower costs than PCDF and ACDF.Copyright © Congress of Neurological Surgeons 2026. title: Brain network functional connectivity alterations associated with acute posttraumatic headache.
abstract: To investigate disruptions in resting state networks in participants with acute posttraumatic headache (PTH) due to mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI). Neuroimaging studies have demonstrated alterations in functional connectivity (FC) within core resting-state networks in participants with headache versus healthy controls (HCs), which may provide insights into disease mechanisms; however, the extent to which these alterations relate to PTH remains incompletely understood.In this comparative cross-sectional study with an embedded prospective cohort, participants with acute PTH and HCs were enrolled from the Mayo Clinic Arizona and Minnesota, and the Phoenix Veterans Affairs Health Care between 2020 and 2024. Participants with PTH underwent resting-state magnetic resonance imaging within 2 months following mTBI. We investigated differences within and between functional brain networks in participants with PTH compared to HCs. Associations between altered FC with headache frequency, alterations of mood, post-mTBI symptoms, and concussion history were determined and corrected for age and sex. Relationships between PTH outcomes at 3 months and baseline FC were investigated.Ninety-six participants with acute PTH (35 male, 61 female) and 84 age-balanced HCs were included. Decreased resting state network connectivity in participants with PTH compared to HCs (False Discovery Rate (FDR) corrected <0.05) was observed in two default mode network (DMN) regions encompassing the bilateral frontal and anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), as well as the left postcentral gyrus. Within those DMN regions, exploratory analyses revealed that FC was positively associated with headache frequency in the bilateral ACC, right precuneus and frontal gyrus, and with trait anxiety in the right ACC. In contrast, negative associations were observed between FC and number of mTBIs, as well as state anxiety, in the left ACC (uncorrected, p<0.05). No significant associations with clinical headache variables were observed in the DMN comprising the left postcentral gyrus. Baseline group differences in network connectivity between recovered and nonrecovered participants were found in visual, sensorimotor, default mode, executive control and salience networks. Alterations in baseline connectivity between independent components in recovered and nonrecovered participants were not statistically significant after corrections for multiple comparisons.In participants with PTH, the DMN regions showing decreased connectivity also exhibited associations with headache frequency, state and trait anxiety, and number of lifetime mTBIs, suggesting that these changes relate to the severity and persistence of post-mTBI symptoms. title: Cerebrospinal Fluid GAD65-Antibody Levels Accurately Identify Relevant Neurological Diseases.
abstract: Retrospective cohort study to investigate which factors most reliably distinguish incidental GAD65-antibodies (iGAD65) from true GAD65-antibody neurological disease (tGAD65). 167 adults with positive serum and CSF GAD65-antibodies (> 0.02 nmol/L by radioimmunoassay) were classified as tGAD65 or iGAD65, with diagnostic performance of paraclinical parameters compared in discovery and validation cohorts. CSF GAD65-antibody titers ≥ 1 nmol/L performed best in discovery (AUC 0.956) and validation (AUC 0.949; p = 0.814), with 89.7% sensitivity and 94% specificity for identifying tGAD65. This suggests the improved test could help doctors identify patients at risk of recurrence earlier than current methods allow.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers applied ultrasensitive MAESTRO ctDNA assays to 331 plasma samples from 36 esophageal cancer patients treated with curative intent to evaluate postoperative minimal residual disease detection. Esophageal cancer produces low levels of circulating tumor DNA, which limits the sensitivity of first-generation MRD assays and allows occult disease to escape detection. The study found that 60% of ctDNA-positive samples contained DNA concentrations below 100 parts per million, demonstrating that most detectable ctDNA exists at very low abundance. All recurrences in the cohort were preceded by postoperative ctDNA detection, indicating that ultrasensitive assays can identify patients with circulating tumor DNA before clinical recurrence becomes apparent. The low shedding of ctDNA by esophageal cancer necessitates ultrasensitive detection methods to avoid missing disease that would otherwise remain undetected by conventional assays.

title: Pediatric Epilepsy Surgery: Global Survey of Surgical Approaches.
abstract: Pediatric epilepsy surgery is an established treatment, but current global data on surgical practices are limited. This study, conducted by the International League Against Epilepsy Pediatric Epilepsy Surgery Taskforce, provides an updated international overview of surgical approaches and their regional variation.Group-level data were collected from 61 epilepsy surgery programs (49 pediatric-only) across 29 countries on 6 continents. All children and adolescents who underwent epilepsy surgery in 2023 were included. The study was designed to enable direct comparison with the similar survey conducted by the International League Against Epilepsy in 2004.The cohort comprised 2427 patients. Resections accounted for 50.6% and disconnections for 23.0% of procedures. Resection rates were highest in Oceania (87.3%) and lowest in North America (40.3%). Resections were 43.0% unilobar-most commonly temporal (39.6%) and frontal (32.7%)-and 9.7% multilobar, with 61.9% involving the posterior quadrant. Hemispheric surgeries comprised 12.9% of all cases (highest in South America: 18.1%). Subcortical procedures (eg, for hypothalamic hamartomas or deep-seated lesions) represented 2.7% (highest in South America: 12.1%). Intraoperative electrocorticography was used in 38.3% of cases, most commonly in Oceania (84.1%) and Asia (85.5%). Minimally invasive techniques were used in 7.7% of cases, with the highest rate in North America (16.9%). Laser interstitial thermal therapy was most common (4.9%), followed by radiofrequency ablation (2.1%), endoscopic surgery (0.7%), and radiosurgery (0.1%). Corpus callosotomy was performed in 5.9% of all cases, and no multiple subpial transections were reported. Neurostimulation was used in 14.7% of patients, highest in North America (35.6%), and included vagal nerve stimulation (11.8%), deep brain stimulation (1.5%), and responsive neurostimulation (1.4%).Resections and disconnections, including extensive multilobar and hemispheric procedures, remain the core procedures of pediatric epilepsy surgery. Although minimally invasive and neuromodulatory techniques are increasingly used in selected regions-particularly North America-their global adoption remains limited.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). title: ESR Essentials: MRI of the scrotum-practice recommendations by the European Society of Urogenital Radiology.
abstract: While conventional ultrasonography (US) remains the first-line imaging modality for scrotal pathology, multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) has emerged as a valuable problem-solving tool for indeterminate US findings. Owing to its superior soft-tissue contrast, functional imaging capabilities, and operator independence, mpMRI allows for the precise localization and characterization of scrotal lesions. This paper from the European Society of Urogenital Radiology Scrotal and Penile Imaging Working Group provides a comprehensive, evidence-based overview of scrotal mpMRI for a general radiologist. It details optimized imaging protocols, recommending a standard sequence of T1-weighted, T2-weighted, diffusion-weighted, and subtracted dynamic contrast-enhanced imaging. The article highlights key clinical indications, including the characterization of intratesticular and paratesticular masses, local staging of testicular germ cell tumors, and differentiation between germ cell and sex cord-stromal neoplasms. This paper familiarizes radiologists with normal MRI appearances and MRI findings of common scrotal diseases. Evidence-based recommendations for reporting basic MRI examinations of the scrotum are also provided. The potential of advanced techniques, such as diffusion tensor imaging and proton MR spectroscopy, and the future integration of artificial intelligence and radiomics, are also discussed. We hope the implementation of these recommendations into radiological practice will enhance diagnostic confidence and promote standardized practice in scrotal MRI for radiologists. KEY POINTS: While conventional ultrasound is the first-line modality for scrotal pathology, it can yield inconclusive findings regarding complex mass characterization and local tumor staging. Multiparametric MRI combines anatomical and functional data to accurately characterize scrotal masses, localize impalpable, undescended testes, and provide precise local tumor staging. Scrotal multiparametric MRI serves as a valuable problem-solving tool that enhances diagnostic confidence in sonographically indeterminate cases, prevents unnecessary radical orchiectomies, supports testis-sparing surgery or active surveillance, and standardizes radiological reporting templates to optimize personalized patient management.© 2026. title: Presentation, management, and outcomes of ectopic Cushing syndrome: an international, multicentre, retrospective, cohort study.
abstract: Ectopic Cushing syndrome is a rare condition with scarce outcome data. We sought to characterise its course and determinants of complications and mortality.In this international, multicentre, retrospective, cohort study, 49 high-volume endocrine referral centres across Asia, Europe, North America, South America, and New Zealand identified consecutive eligible patients. We included patients with a clinical diagnosis of ectopic Cushing syndrome, defined by expert adjudication at the treating institution with at least one of the following criteria: inferior petrosal sinus sampling or dynamic testing supportive of ectopic Cushing syndrome, biochemical remission of hypercortisolism following treatment of the ectopic Cushing syndrome source (surgical excision, radiotherapy, or cryoablation), evidence of a non-metastatic tumoural source of ectopic Cushing syndrome, either on initial or subsequent imaging, or evidence of a metastatic tumoural source of ectopic Cushing syndrome either on imaging or from chart notes. Data collection was completed between May 31, 2024 and April 22, 2025. Clinical features, biochemical severity, management, complications, and mortality were assessed. The primary outcome was Cushing syndrome-related mortality (investigator-adjudicated). Secondary outcomes were overall mortality and incidence of complications. Outcomes were stratified based on biochemical remission and timeline since diagnosis. Early (within 6 months of diagnosis) and late (>6 months after diagnosis) outcomes were analysed using landmark methods.Among 1463 patients (median age 51 years [IQR 37-64; range 3-87], 824 [56·3%] women, 639 [43·7%] men, and 1021 [69·8%] of White race), 836 (57·1%) had metastatic disease. Severe hypercortisolism (1204 [91·1%] of 1321) and hypokalaemia (1111 [79·4%] of 1399) were common. Median duration of follow-up was 57 months (IQR 19-124). Cushing syndrome-related death occurred in 196 (13·4%) patients. 626 (42·8%) patients died overall. Infection occurred in 464 (31·7%) patients, venous thromboembolism in 124 (8·5%), cardiovascular events in 93 (6·4%), and cerebrovascular events in 37 (2·5%). Achievement of complete biochemical remission within 6 months of diagnosis was independently associated with lower risk of late complications (adjusted HR 0·55 [95% CI 0·38-0·80]) and Cushing syndrome-related mortality (0·49 [0·27-0·89]), whereas no association was observed with non-Cushing syndrome-related mortality.Outcomes in ectopic Cushing syndrome are driven by early control of hypercortisolism. Failure to achieve remission within 6 months is associated with markedly worse complications and mortality, supporting ectopic Cushing syndrome as a time-critical endocrine emergency.Mayo Clinic.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: TrkB and NMDA receptor mRNA expression in phrenic motor neurons following cervical spinal hemisection.
abstract: Cervical spinal cord injury (SCI) can interrupt descending bulbospinal pathways that support breathing, increasing the risk of serious respiratory complications and death. The C2 spinal hemisection (C2SH) model reduces neural drive to the phrenic motor pool, impairing ventilatory-related diaphragm activity with incomplete spontaneous recovery. Signaling via the tropomyosin receptor kinase B (TrkB) and glutamatergic transmission through N-methyl-d-aspartate receptors (NMDA-R) have been implicated in this recovery, but whether injury-related changes in TrkB and NMDA-R mRNA expression are uniform across phrenic motor neurons (PhMNs) remains unknown. We hypothesized that TrkB and NMDA-R mRNA transcript number or density would show size- and side-dependent regulation after C2SH. RNAscope was used to quantify the number and density of TrkB and NMDA-R mRNA transcripts in PhMNs ipsilateral and contralateral to C2SH in adult male rats. In mixed linear models with animal as a random effect, there was no effect of PhMN surface area, spinal cord side relative to C2SH or experimental group on TrkB or NMDA-R mRNA transcript number per PhMN. Interaction effects showed TrkB mRNA transcript number increased after C2SH, predominantly ipsilaterally and at larger PhMNs by 21 days post-C2SH (21DSH). Within individual PhMNs, concurrent increases in TrkB and NMDA-R mRNA transcript number were evident by 21DSH. Results were concordant for TrkB and NMDA-R mRNA density within motor neurons. These findings suggest size- and side-dependent changes in TrkB and NMDA-R mRNA regulation within the phrenic motor pool after C2SH, consistent with motor unit-specific plasticity that may contribute to spontaneous respiratory recovery after cervical SCI.Copyright © 2026. title: Therapeutic Signals Without Histologic Certainty: FGF Analogues in Compensated MASH Cirrhosis-A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Compensated MASH cirrhosis is an advanced disease with no current approved pharmacologic therapy. FGF analogues have shown biological activity, but individual trials have not established histologic efficacy. We aim to evaluate their effects across histologic and non-invasive outcomes in this population.PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception through 8 July 2026 for RCTs comparing FGF analogues with placebo in adults with compensated (F4) MASH cirrhosis. The primary outcome was at least 1-stage fibrosis improvement without MASH worsening. Secondary outcomes included Pro-C3, Enhanced Liver Fibrosis (ELF) score and liver stiffness. MASH resolution and safety were exploratory. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed. RoB 2 and GRADE assessments were conducted.Five RCTs involving 589 participants were included. FGF analogues did not significantly improve fibrosis by at least one stage without worsening of MASH (RR, 1.32; 95% CI, 0.89-1.97). In post hoc exploratory analyses, FGF21 analogues increased MASH resolution alone (RR, 3.17; 95% CI, 1.49-6.73), whereas resolution without worsening of fibrosis remained inconclusive (RR, 1.75; 95% CI, 0.95-3.23). Treatment reduced ELF score (MD, -0.52; 95% CI, -0.79 to -0.25), Pro-C3 (MD, -26.49 percentage points; 95% CI, -40.47 to -12.51) and liver stiffness (MD, -2.30 kPa; 95% CI, -3.90 to -0.71). Serious adverse events were not significantly increased, but adverse-event-related discontinuation was more frequent (RR, 3.44; 95% CI, 1.13-10.43). FGF19 findings derive from a single trial (aldafermin).FGF analogues did not significantly improve the primary fibrosis endpoint, but improved MASH resolution and non-invasive fibrosis measures, supporting continued evaluation of FGF analogues in Phase 3 trials with longer follow-up.© 2026 John Wiley & Sons Ltd.

title: Cancer Immunotherapy Using AIRE Conditioning of the Tumor Epitopeome.
abstract: T-cell immune tolerance is established in part through the activity of the autoimmune regulator (AIRE) transcription factor in medullary thymic epithelial cells (mTEC) of the thymus. AIRE induces expression of peripheral tissue-specific self-antigens for presentation to naïve T cells to promote activation/deletion of autoreactive T cells. This traditional role of AIRE in mTECs is to prevent autoimmunity. Herein, we demonstrate that tumors mimic the role of AIRE in mTECs to evade immune rejection. We found that AIRE induced a profile of "selfness" at the RNA and protein levels which, when presented on major histocompatibility complexes (MHC), shielded the tumor from inherently self-tolerized T cells. Moreover, we describe an in vivo immunotherapy in which engineered changes in AIRE expression in tumor cells altered their profile of selfness, exposing both AIRE-modified and parental unmodified tumor cells to T-cell attack. Therefore, by resetting the immunologic selfness of cancer cells, this AIRE-mediated immunotherapy (i) converted a highly tolerized T-cell compartment into a tumor-reactive T-cell population; (ii) conferred upon nonimmunogenic tumors de novo sensitivity to immune checkpoint blockade; (iii) removed the need to identify potentially immunogenic tumor-associated antigens as targets for generation of T-cell responses; and (iv) lead to potent T cell-mediated rejection of aggressive, immunologically cold, nonimmunogenic tumors. Patient RNA sequencing data showed that the expression of AIRE predicted response to immune therapies with a strong correlation between AIRE expression and markers of T-cell receptor signaling, suggesting that our studies have therapeutic translational value.©2026 American Association for Cancer Research.

title: Pneumococcal vaccination for prevention of infection and diagnosis of antibody deficiency in the extended conjugated vaccine era.
abstract: Pneumococcal conjugate vaccines (PCV) have transformed pneumococcal disease prevention. Recent expansion to higher-valency formulations (PCV15, PCV20, PCV21) and updated Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) recommendations extending coverage to all healthy PCV-naïve adults ≥50 years in the United States have introduced new complexity in vaccine selection, timing, and dosing. Concurrently, universal childhood conjugate priming complicates the diagnosis of specific antibody deficiency (SAD), as prior PCV immunization alters interpretation of the Pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccines (PPSV23) challenge. This review synthesizes recent evidence on vaccine effectiveness in invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD) prevention, serotype dynamics, and the evolving diagnostic framework for SAD.In October 2024, ACIP expanded pneumococcal vaccination to all PCV-naïve adults ≥50 years. title: Intraoperative Management of Fibular Free Flap With Chronic DVT: Case and Technique.
abstract: Chronic post-thrombotic syndrome (PTS) involving the peroneal venae comitantes is an uncommon but potentially flap-threatening finding during fibular free flap reconstruction that may not be detected on routine preoperative computed tomography angiography. We describe the successful management of extensive chronic PTS encountered unexpectedly during fibular free flap reconstruction for advanced oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma.Following unsuccessful mechanical thrombectomy, arterial inflow was established before venous reconstruction to identify the dominant functional venous outflow pathway, followed by selective venous anastomosis.Early postoperative venous congestion was successfully managed with revision and a second venous anastomosis. The flap remained viable with excellent functional and oncologic outcomes at 1 year.This case demonstrates that chronic PTS should not necessarily preclude fibular free flap reconstruction and presents a practical intraoperative and postoperative strategy for managing this challenging and previously underreported scenario.© 2026 Wiley Periodicals LLC.

llm_summary: This case report describes a patient who unexpectedly had chronic blood clots in veins of the leg during surgery to reconstruct the mouth using a fibular free flap, a tissue graft taken from the fibula bone. The surgical team successfully managed the clotted veins by establishing blood flow through an artery first, then creating two separate venous connections to ensure proper drainage. The flap remained healthy and functional one year after surgery, suggesting that chronic vein clots should not automatically prevent this type of reconstruction.
llm_summary_expert: This case report describes the intraoperative and postoperative management of a patient undergoing fibular free flap reconstruction for advanced oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma who was found to have unexpected chronic post-thrombotic syndrome involving the peroneal venae comitantes. After mechanical thrombectomy proved unsuccessful, the surgical team established arterial inflow before venous reconstruction to identify the dominant functional venous outflow pathway and then performed selective venous anastomosis. Early postoperative venous congestion was managed with revision and a second venous anastomosis, resulting in flap viability. At one year follow-up, the flap demonstrated excellent functional and oncologic outcomes. This case demonstrates that chronic post-thrombotic syndrome involving the peroneal venae comitantes, though uncommon and potentially undetected on preoperative imaging, should not necessarily preclude fibular free flap reconstruction when appropriate intraoperative and postoperative management strategies are employed.

title: Communication Difficulties and Management: The Lived Experience of Individuals With Frontotemporal Lobar Degeneration Spectrum Disorders.
abstract: Frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD) is the neuropathology that underlies a collection of progressive clinical syndromes typically classified by the initial/primary symptom. For example, individuals with loss of word meaning as a first manifestation are often diagnosed with the semantic variant of primary progressive aphasia. Growing evidence suggests that language and communication can be impacted in all clinical syndromes across the FTLD spectrum, but the functional relevance of these symptoms has yet to be explored.The Frontotemporal Degeneration (FTD) Insights Survey is the largest community survey of individuals affected by FTLD. It was administered online and included questions related to demographics, symptoms, life participation, quality of life, and experiences with and hopes for treatment. Self-reported diagnoses of respondents included the nonfluent/agrammatic, semantic, and unspecified variants of primary progressive aphasia, semantic dementia, corticobasal syndrome, progressive supranuclear palsy, and behavioral variant FTD. Here, we grouped respondents according to whether they had a language-predominant (n = 43), motor-predominant (n = 43), or behavior-predominant (n = 90) variant of FTLD and used descriptive statistics to explore how they perceive their own communication difficulties and gauge their motivation for management.Over 65% of respondents in each group identified changes to communication as a symptom; subsequent analyses focused on the responses of this cohort. Across groups, word finding and speaking were two of the most frequently endorsed difficulties. Over 50% of each group identified improved communication as a treatment priority, reflecting the impact that these symptoms have on their day-to-day life. Speech-language therapy is an important approach to manage these changes and minimize their impact. Whereas 76% of the language and motor groups had attended speech-language therapy, this was true for only 16% of the behavior group.Individuals across the FTLD spectrum experience changes to communication that impact their social engagement and quality of life. Management needs to be tailored to the needs of each individual, but recommendations are provided based on the insights and group-level preferences reported here. Future research is needed to identify current referral practices and how to increase engagement in skilled communication interventions, especially for individuals with the behavioral variant of FTD.https://doi.org/10.23641/asha.33940597.

title: Monoallelic variants in BRSK1 are associated with a neurodevelopmental disorder with or without epilepsy.
abstract: Brain-specific serine/threonine kinase (BRSK1; synapses of amphids defective [SAD]-B) encodes an AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK)-related serine/threonine kinase required for neuronal polarization and synaptic function. An individual with a variant in BRSK1 was identified in the Texome Project, which provides genomic diagnosis to financially disadvantaged individuals in Texas, using AI-MARRVEL. We subsequently found nine individuals harboring rare heterozygous BRSK1 variants through GeneMatcher. Affected individuals present with developmental delay and variable phenotypes including anxiety, attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), autism, and seizures. All variants (missense and nonsense) are predicted to be deleterious by pathogenicity prediction tools. We utilized Drosophila to model three missense variants to assess the impact of the variants in vivo. We show that Drosophila sff (sugar-free frosting; ortholog of BRSK1) is expressed in neurons of the larval central nervous system (CNS) and adult brain. Loss of sff leads to viable flies with severe locomotor impairment, bang and heat sensitivity, and a short lifespan. In addition, the third-instar neuromuscular junctions (NMJs) in sff null mutants display a significant overgrowth, associated with elevated levels of Futsch (MAP1B), a microtubule-associated protein. Expression of the human reference BRSK1 cDNA in the sff null mutant rescues the behavioral, NMJ morphology, and Futsch phenotypes, showing that the human gene is functional in flies. In contrast, the three individual-derived alleles (BRSK1p.Ile202Val, BRSK1p.Arg237Cys, and BRSK1p.Thr406Ile) provide only a partial rescue and fail to normalize NMJ morphology and Futsch levels, suggesting that they are partial loss-of-function alleles. llm_summary: Researchers identified ten individuals with rare mutations in the BRSK1 gene, which is important for brain development, and found that these mutations were associated with developmental delays and variable symptoms including seizures, autism, and attention problems. Using fruit flies as a model, they showed that the mutated versions of the gene only partially restored normal brain function compared to the normal gene, suggesting these mutations reduce the gene's effectiveness. These findings indicate that having one faulty copy of the BRSK1 gene can cause a neurodevelopmental disorder with different symptoms across affected individuals.

title: Long-Term Shoulder Outcomes Following Tendon Transfers for Brachial Plexus Birth Injuries.
abstract: Although the majority of children with brachial plexus birth injuries recover spontaneously, permanent functional deficits at the shoulder can be seen following both incomplete spontaneous recovery and microsurgical reconstruction. Incomplete recovery of upper trunk injuries typically results in shoulder internal rotation contractions and muscular imbalances. Tendon transfers are a well-established procedure for improving shoulder function in this population. Long-term outcomes of this procedure remain understudied.A retrospective review of patients 5 years of age or younger who underwent tendon transfers for brachial plexus birth injury at a single, tertiary-referral center from the year 2000 to 2022 was conducted. Demographics, clinical and surgical variables, and postoperative outcomes were examined. Paired t tests and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests were utilized to compare preoperative and postoperative scores.Eighty-eight children (61% female, 75% Caucasian) diagnosed with either C5-C6 (71.6%), C5-C7 (13.6%), or total palsy (14.8%) due to a brachial plexus birth injury were identified. Average age at surgery was 28.5±14.6 months, and average follow-up was 8.7±5.0 years. Nerve grafting, nerve transfers, or neurolysis was performed before tendon transfer in 20 patients. Twenty patients underwent isolated latissimus dorsi transfer, while 62 underwent combined latissimus dorsi and teres major transfers. Mean modified Mallet scores improved by +0.60 for abduction, +0.85 for external rotation, and +1.10 for hand-to-mouth (P<0.001). Active external rotation improved by 19.7 degrees, external rotation at 90 degrees improved by 11.0 degrees, and forward flexion improved by 47.2 degrees (P<0.001). Two patients (2.4%) underwent revision tendon transfers, and 16 patients (19.5%) underwent subsequent shoulder procedures. Separately, 6 patients underwent isolated trapezius transfer with no significant changes in preoperative versus postoperative outcomes.Tendon transfer for brachial plexus birth injury results in long-lasting improvements in shoulder function in young children. Although postoperative complications and subsequent procedures were observed, revisions were infrequent.Level III-retrospective study.Copyright © 2026 Wolters Kluwer Health, LLC. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether tendon transfer surgery, which moves muscles to restore shoulder function, produces lasting benefits in young children with brachial plexus birth injuries that don't fully heal on their own. Over an average of nearly nine years of follow-up, children who underwent the procedure showed significant improvements in shoulder movement and strength, with only a small percentage requiring revision surgery. These results suggest that tendon transfer can provide durable functional gains, though some children needed additional procedures afterward.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers conducted a retrospective review of 88 children aged 5 years or younger who underwent tendon transfers for brachial plexus birth injury at a single tertiary center between 2000 and 2022, with an average follow-up of 8.7 years. The cohort predominantly presented with C5-C6 palsy (71.6%), and 62 patients underwent combined latissimus dorsi and teres major transfers while 20 underwent isolated latissimus dorsi transfer. Revision tendon transfers were required in only 2 patients (2.4%), although 16 patients (19.5%) underwent subsequent shoulder procedures during the follow-up period. title: Pacing Performance of a Modular Communicative Leadless Pacing-Defibrillator System.
abstract: MODULAR ATP is an ongoing trial assessing the efficacy of a subcutaneous implantable cardioverter defibrillator (S-ICD) in communication with a leadless pacemaker (LP) that can deliver bradycardia pacing and antitachycardia pacing. The objective of this study was to assess safety and pacing performance of the investigational LP.The study enrolled patients with an ICD indication and at high risk for monomorphic ventricular tachycardia. Pacemaker dependent patients were excluded. Primary safety endpoint 2 was the percentage of patients free from major LP-related complications at 12 months. The secondary effectiveness endpoint assessed the rate response performance of the LP under workload. Parameters related to the pacing performance were also measured.In 297 patients, the mean age was 59±12 years, the mean left ventricular ejection fraction was 35.3±13.1%, and 17.5% were female. LP implant was attempted in 286 patients and was successful in 100%. The major LP-related complication free rate at 12 months was 97.2% (one-sided 97.5% LCL 94.5%), surpassing the performance goal of 81%. There were no LP-related complications following Implant. For the secondary effectiveness endpoint, the slope of the normalized sensor rate versus the normalized workload was 0.96 (95% LCL 0.91, 95% UCL 1.02), within the performance goal range of 0.65-1.35. At 12 months, 96.8% of patients had a pacing capture threshold ≤ 2V @ 0.4ms pulse width.The performance of the modular pacing-defibrillator system at one year demonstrated a low complication rate and reliable pacing functionality.© The Author(s) 2026. llm_summary: Researchers tested a new pacemaker system designed to work with an implantable defibrillator to treat patients at risk for dangerous heart rhythms. In 297 patients followed for one year, the pacemaker was successfully implanted in all cases and had very few complications, with 97.2% of patients remaining free from major problems. The device reliably maintained proper heart pacing function, suggesting it is a safe and effective treatment option for eligible patients.
llm_summary_expert: The MODULAR ATP trial evaluated the safety and pacing performance of a leadless pacemaker (LP) designed to communicate with a subcutaneous implantable cardioverter defibrillator in 297 patients with an ICD indication and high risk for monomorphic ventricular tachycardia, with a mean age of 59 years and mean left ventricular ejection fraction of 35.3%. The primary safety endpoint assessed the percentage of patients free from major LP-related complications at 12 months, while secondary effectiveness endpoints included rate response performance under workload and pacing capture threshold measurements. At 12 months, 97.2% of patients were free from major LP-related complications, exceeding the performance goal of 81%, with no LP-related complications occurring after implant in the 286 patients who underwent attempted implantation. The rate response slope of normalized sensor rate versus normalized workload was 0.96, falling within the performance goal range of 0.65–1.35, and 96.8% of patients achieved pacing capture thresholds of 2 volts or less at 0.4 millis.

title: Depletion of CD19-positive B-cells and dexamethasone premedication may result in immune suppression in patients with B-precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia after consolidation treatment with blinatumomab.
abstract: Treatment of patients with B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) has benefited greatly from the introduction of different immunotherapy approaches targeting CD19 or CD22. In particular, when added to or when replacing some parts of chemotherapy treatment, blinatumomab, a bispecific T-cell engager which creates an immunological synapse between patient's CD3-expressing T lymphocytes and CD19-positive cells, including leukemia blasts, has shown unprecedented efficacy in preventing leukemia relapse/progression in both adults and children with either newly diagnosed or relapsed B-ALL. Despite the great anti-leukemia efficacy shown by blinatumomab, data obtained in large randomized studies in adults and children with newly diagnosed B-ALL have shown that the benefit of immunotherapy has, in part, been offset by an increased risk of infections, which can even occur long after completion of immunotherapy. Blinatumomab is also able to lyse normal B lymphocytes, and the resulting long-lasting, profound B-cell aplasia may lead to severe hypogammaglobulinemia, in turn increasing the incidence of infectious complications. Premedication with dexamethasone is widely used for mitigation of neurotoxicity and other systemic toxicities related to initial exposure to blinatumomab, but the dose usually employed does not derive from well-conducted studies aimed at identifying the recommended steroid dose. In addition, there is no robust evidence of a neuroprotective effect of Dexamethasone. This Spotlight Review aims to highlight the importance of monitoring immunoglobulin levels and to provide guidelines for initiation and continuation of immunoglobulin replacement therapy. In addition, we focus on need to conduct studies properly addressing the identification of optimal corticosteroid doses, regimens, and timing.

llm_summary: Blinatumomab, an immunotherapy drug for blood cancer, effectively prevents leukemia relapse but destroys healthy B-cells, which produce infection-fighting proteins, leading to increased infections even after treatment ends. The steroid drug dexamethasone is commonly given to reduce side effects, but there is no strong evidence it actually protects against nerve damage. Researchers recommend monitoring patients' immunoglobulin levels and conducting better studies to determine the safest steroid doses and timing.
llm_summary_expert: Blinatumomab, a bispecific T-cell engager targeting CD19, has demonstrated unprecedented efficacy in preventing relapse and progression in adults and children with newly diagnosed or relapsed B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia when added to or replacing components of chemotherapy. Despite its anti-leukemia efficacy shown in large randomized studies, blinatumomab treatment is associated with increased infection risk that can persist long after immunotherapy completion, partly due to profound and long-lasting B-cell aplasia resulting in severe hypogammaglobulinemia. Dexamethasone premedication is widely used to mitigate neurotoxicity and systemic toxicities from initial blinatumomab exposure, though the doses employed lack derivation from well-conducted studies identifying optimal steroid dosing and no robust evidence supports a neuroprotective effect. This review emphasizes the importance of monitoring immunoglobulin levels and establishing guidelines for initiating and continuing immunoglobulin replacement therapy in patients receiving blinatumomab consolidation treatment. The authors highlight the need for properly designed studies to identify optimal corticosteroid doses.

title: Treatment-related neutropenia as predictor of response to adjuvant palbociclib in the PALLAS trial (ABCSG-42/AFT-05/BIG-14-13/PrE0109).
abstract: Prior analyses of PALLAS (NCT02513394), a phase III trial that randomized patients with stage II-III hormone receptor-positive breast cancer to receive adjuvant palbociclib plus endocrine therapy (ET) or ET alone, did not show benefit of the combination. Separate data show extent of treatment-related neutropenia is associated with improved response to palbociclib and other cell cycle-specific therapies. We conducted an exploratory analysis to assess whether grade of treatment-related neutropenia could identify benefit from palbociclib in the adjuvant setting.Patients receiving palbociclib were classified into those with treatment-emergent high-grade neutropenia (HGN) with maximum grade ≥3 (absolute neutrophil count <1000/mm3), or low-grade/no neutropenia (LGN) with maximum grade ≤2. These groups were compared to each other and to the ET-alone group for 5-year invasive disease-free survival (iDFS).5736 patients were included: 2840 in the palbociclib+ET arm and 2896 in the ET-alone arm. Patients receiving palbociclib+ET consisted of 1006 (35.4%) LGN and 1834 (64.6%) HGN. Lower body mass index (BMI), Asian race, prior chemotherapy, and mastectomy were associated with HGN (all p < 0.05). Patients receiving ET alone had inferior 5-year iDFS compared with patients who developed HGN by cycle 6 on palbociclib+ET (hazard ratio [HR] 1.19, 95% confidence interval [CI]:1.01-1.40; p = 0.04), an association that persisted after adjustment for prior chemotherapy, race, and BMI (HR 1.20, 95% CI:1.02-1.42; p = 0.03).In this exploratory analysis of the PALLAS trial, palbociclib+ET showed benefit over ET alone in patients who developed HGN in the first 6 treatment cycles. title: Establishing Absolute Neutrophil Count and White Blood Cell Count Reference Intervals for the Duffy Null Population.
abstract: Most reference intervals (RI) for absolute neutrophil count (ANC) and white blood cell count (WBC) in the United States (US) are not representative of people with the Duffy null phenotype (10% of the US population), which leads to misdiagnoses and inequity in care. We aimed to verify the adult Duffy null ANC RI and develop WBC and ANC RIs for pediatrics. 1,412 healthy Duffy null participants from 23 sites were included. All sites agreed on eligibility criteria. Otherwise, this was a pragmatic design with site-specific variation in collection approach. ANC and WBC were stratified into 5 age categories: 6 months-2 years, 3-6 years, 7-12 years, 13-17 years, and 18+ years. RI were calculated by Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute guidelines. Duffy null-specific ANC RI were 0.53-4.50×109/L (6 months-2 years, n=184), 0.78-4.67×109/L (3-6 years, n=160), 0.87-5.34×109/L (7-12 years, n=190), 0.90-4.89×109/L (13-17 years, n=216), and 1.03-7.30×109/L (18+ years, n=662). 25% of adults had ANC <2.00×109/L and 24-53% of children had ANC <1.50×109/L. Sensitivity analyses did not show any significant differences in ANC RI when accounting for blood draw type, setting, collection site, hematology analyzer, or hemoglobin and platelet counts. This study provides the first report of Duffy null-specific pediatric ANC and WBC RI, as well as a large-scale verification of adult Duffy null-specific ANC and WBC RI. Adoption of Duffy null-specific RIs is necessary for the accurate interpretation of laboratory values that will support appropriate and equitable medical decision-making.Copyright © 2026 American Society of Hematology.

llm_summary: Researchers studied blood cell counts in over 1,400 healthy people with the Duffy null trait, a genetic variation found in about 10% of Americans, to establish normal ranges for children and adults. They found that people with this trait naturally have lower neutrophil counts (a type of white blood cell) than current standard reference ranges suggest, with many having counts that would be considered abnormal by existing guidelines. These new Duffy null-specific ranges could prevent misdiagnosis and ensure more equitable medical care for this population.

title: GAD65 Autoimmune-Associated Epilepsy: Pathophysiology, Diagnosis, and Treatment.
abstract: GAD65 autoimmune-associated epilepsy (AAE) is an underrecognized cause of epilepsy with common delays to immunotherapy. We review advances in its pathophysiology, diagnosis and management.GAD65 AAE predominantly affects young women, presenting as drug resistant temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE), often without mesial temporal sclerosis. Patients lie within a continuum where T cell mediated inflammation predominates in early disease, temporally overlapping with progressive structural injury, which leads to chronic epilepsy. Diagnosis is supported by high-level antibody detection in serum (RIA > 20 nmol/L or > 2000 U/mL, ELISA > 10,000 IU/mL), and in select cases CSF testing may be helpful. Treatment requires both immunotherapy and antiseizure medications. Immunotherapy response is greatest in early disease but can occur at later stages. Epilepsy surgery workup and neuromodulation may benefit some patients, although seizure freedom is rare. GAD65 AAE can resemble non-autoimmune TLE. Phenotype-based antibody testing and early recognition are important to guide timely, individualized treatment.© 2026. title: Cellular senescence mediates facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy.
abstract: Facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD) is driven by aberrant expression of the early embryonic transcription factor Double Homeobox 4 (DUX4), yet the mechanisms linking low, sporadic DUX4 activity to progressive muscle degeneration remain unclear. Here, we identify cellular senescence as a central and early mechanism in FSHD pathogenesis. Analysis of patient muscle transcriptomes revealed strong enrichment of senescence and senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) programs that correlated with DUX4 activity, clinical severity, and histopathological changes. Notably, these signatures were detectable even in STIR-negative muscles, defining a prodystrophic state characterized by early molecular alterations preceding overt MRI-detectable inflammation and highlighting their potential utility as early biomarkers of disease activity. Using an FSHD mouse model, we show that DUX4-induced muscle injury rapidly triggers senescence, which then progressively expands. Fibroadipogenic progenitors and macrophages emerged as the principal senescent populations and key sources of pro-inflammatory and profibrotic SASP signals. Importantly, senescence was therapeutically modifiable. Treatment with the nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor lamivudine (3TC), which inhibits LINE-1 reverse transcriptase activity, significantly reduced senescence, inflammation, and fibrosis while promoting muscle regeneration. These findings identify cellular senescence as a tractable driver of FSHD and warrant senotherapeutic strategies, particularly lamivudine, for clinical intervention in FSHD.

title: "He's Been Real Professional About It…and That's What We Expect": Framing of Media Coverage of the Tyrod Taylor Punctured Lung Adverse Event.
abstract: In 2020, Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Tyrod Taylor suffered a punctured lung as the result of an adverse event. The purpose of this study was to analyze the ways journalists presented the punctured lung adverse event and subsequent malpractice lawsuit in their news coverage. Guided by framing theory, the qualitative thematic analysis of news coverage identified that journalists used language that minimized the severity of the adverse event, presented Taylor's response as one of professionalism, and reported on the team's position to maintain the professional integrity of the team doctor who performed the procedure. Additionally, the news stories highlighted the larger issue of athlete understanding of medical risk when receiving care. These results raise questions about journalists' ability to accurately report about adverse events as well as the need for discussions of non-play‑related injuries in sports.

title: Technology Assistance and Fixed-Bearing Design Were Associated with Higher Revision-Free Survival at 15 Years After UKA: A Cohort Study of 2,234 Consecutive Knees.
abstract: Unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA) is an alternative to total knee arthroplasty for isolated compartment osteoarthritis; however, concerns persist regarding its long-term durability. The purpose of this study was to evaluate revision-free survivorship, risk factors for revision, and clinical outcomes in a large consecutive series of contemporary UKAs.We retrospectively reviewed consecutive primary UKAs performed from 2000 to 2021 at a single tertiary academic center. Revision-free survivorship was estimated using a Kaplan-Meier analysis, and risk factors for revision were assessed using Cox proportional hazards modeling. Clinical outcomes were assessed using the Knee Society Score (KSS).A total of 2,234 UKAs were included. Fixed-bearing implants were used in 78% of UKAs. Technology assistance was used in 59% of UKAs (fluoroscopy, 43%; robotic assistance, 15%; computer navigation, 1%). The mean patient age was 65 years, the mean body mass index was 31 kg/m2, and 49% of UKAs were performed in female patients. Patient race was White in 97% of UKAs, and patient ethnicity was not Hispanic or Latino in 94%. Revision-free survivorship was 92% at 10 years and 85% at 15 years. Overall, 118 UKAs were revised, most commonly through conversion to total knee arthroplasty (97%). The most frequent indications for revision were progression of osteoarthritis in an adjacent compartment (41%), aseptic loosening (23%), unexplained pain (9%), and hardware failure (9%). Factors associated with a lower risk of revision in the univariable analysis included technology assistance (hazard ratio [HR], 0.4; p < 0.01) and high surgeon volume (HR, 0.5; p < 0.01). Mobile-bearing design (HR, 1.9; p < 0.01) was associated with an increased risk of revision in the univariable analysis. The mean KSS improved from 47 preoperatively to 75 at 5 years postoperatively (p < 0.001).In this large consecutive series, UKA demonstrated excellent long-term survivorship, with an approximately 1% annual risk of revision through 15 years. Technology assistance, a fixed-bearing implant design, and high surgeon volume were each associated with a lower risk of revision, underscoring the importance of operative technique and implant selection in achieving durable outcomes.Therapeutic Level III. title: Renal Decline Before Heart Transplantation in Left Ventricular Assist Device-Supported Recipients: United Network for Organ Sharing Analysis.
abstract: Although baseline renal impairment and post-heart transplantation (HT) dialysis are established clinical predictors, the prognostic impact of pre-HT renal decline in patients bridged with left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) remains unclear. We retrospectively analyzed patients from the United Network for Organ Sharing registry who underwent HT following LVAD support between 2009 and 2024. Renal decline was defined as a greater than or equal to 40% reduction in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) from listing to HT. Among 10,454 patients, 624 (6.0%) experienced pre-HT renal decline. Patients with renal decline had longer waitlist durations (median 297 vs. 197 days; p < 0.001), lower eGFR at HT (42.0 vs. 70.6 ml/min/1.73 m2; p < 0.001), and higher rates of post-HT dialysis (23.7 vs. 12.8%; p < 0.001). Independent predictors of renal decline included longer waitlist time and perioperative blood transfusions, whereas HeartMate 3 LVAD use was protective. Renal decline was independently associated with an increased risk of post-HT dialysis (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]: 2.64) and all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR]: 1.16), with post-HT dialysis strongly predicting mortality (aHR: 3.48). Renal deterioration is a significant predictor of post-HT dialysis and mortality in LVAD-bridged patients. Incorporating renal trajectory into risk stratification may enhance candidate selection and promote perioperative renal protection strategies.Copyright © ASAIO 2026.

title: A phase I trial of intravenous vesicular stomatitis virus expressing thyroidal sodium iodide symporter (NIS) and human interferon beta (hIFNβ) in metastatic or recurrent endometrial cancer.
abstract: We report the results of a Phase I trial of intravenous (IV) vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV) engineered to express human interferon beta (hIFNβ) and thyroidal sodium iodide symporter (NIS) in patients with stage IV or recurrent endometrial cancer (EC).Eligible patients with stage IV or recurrent EC with largest tumor diameter ≤ 5 cm were enrolled and received a single IV infusion of VSV-hIFNβ-NIS in a standard '3 + 3' dose escalation. Five dose-levels were planned. Primary endpoint was determination of the maximum tolerated dose (MTD). Secondary endpoints included pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, tumor response, and immune correlates. An exploratory post-hoc analysis evaluated clinical responses to subsequent immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based therapies.From 9/15/2017-1/10/23, 21 eligible patients were treated. One patient at DL2 experienced grade 3 dehydration associated with cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and one experienced transient grade 4 asymptomatic lymphopenia, prompting protocol modification of the DLT definition. One of six patients at DL4 experienced grade 3 delirium meeting DLT criteria. Dose escalation to DL5 was not feasible because of investigational agent production limitations; MTD was not reached. The most common treatment related AEs were transient hematologic toxicities, liver enzyme elevations, and CRS. At day 29, 8 patients had progressive disease (PD); 1 entered hospice due to PD before day 29. Two patients had stable disease for at least 6 months following VSV-hIFNβ-NIS. Of the 15 patients who received subsequent ICI-based therapy following VSV-hIFNβ-NIS, 4 had durable SD with a median follow up of 40.4 (95% CI 30.4-not reached) months.IV VSV-hIFNβ-NIS had an acceptable safety profile in patients with advanced or recurrent EC. Further investigation of VSV-hIFNβ-NIS, particularly in combination with immune checkpoint blockade, is warranted.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

title: Femoral Neck Morphology: A Computed-Tomography-Based Anatomic Framework Informs Medial Collar Design for Contemporary Collared Cementless Femoral Stems.
abstract: The level of femoral neck resection in total hip arthroplasty (THA) affects implant position, restoration of limb length, and degree of cortical support available for collared cementless stems. With increasing use of computed tomography (CT)-based planning and collared stems, understanding femoral neck and calcar morphology at the osteotomy plane is valuable. The aims of this study were to (1) quantify femoral neck cortical thickness at the achieved osteotomy plane reconstructed from postoperative imaging and adjacent levels, (2) assess the effect of osteotomy height on regional cortical support, and (3) determine the medial collar length that best matches cortical thickness at the osteotomy plane.We reviewed preoperative CT scans from 100 consecutive primary THAs performed by a single surgeon using a single cementless femoral stem design. Using multiplanar reconstruction, calcar cortical thickness was measured on axial images at the osteotomy plane (zero mm) and at standardized levels 5.30 mm proximal and 5.30 mm distal to that plane. At each level, thickness was recorded at five locations (anterior, posterior, medial, antero-medial, and postero-medial). The medial cortical thickness at the osteotomy plane was used to determine the collar length, minimizing absolute overhang/underhang, which corresponds to its median.Cortical thickness increased from proximal to distal levels, most prominently in the medial (P < 0.001) and postero-medial (P < 0.001) regions. Antero-medial thickness increased from the proximal level to the osteotomy plane (P = 0.004), but did not increase further distally (P = 0.641). For this cohort and osteotomy technique, the collar length minimizing mean absolute overhang or underhang was 5.3 mm, the median medial cortical thickness at the osteotomy plane.At and around the planned femoral neck osteotomy plane, medial and postero-medial cortices were thickest and increased in thickness distally, whereas antero-medial thickness plateaued. title: Artificial Intelligence as a Bridge to Gaps in Delirium Prediction, Detection, and Management.
abstract: Delirium affects up to one-third of hospitalized older adults and is associated with adverse outcomes. Despite its clinical importance and the availability of validated screening tools, current care gaps extend beyond under-recognition to inconsistent risk stratification, workforce constraints, documentation burden, fragmented intervention delivery, and practical challenges with monitoring of response. We review how artificial intelligence (AI) could bridge these gaps and distinguish model development and validation, real-world clinical implementation, and emerging concepts in delirium care.Prediction models leveraging multimodal health record data, including structured variables and unstructured clinical notes, report good discrimination for delirium risk stratification, but only a few models have been integrated into clinical practice. A live multimodal machine learning model increased targeted delirium detection, yet a pre-post comparative study found a longer length of stay; improved recognition alone therefore does not equate with improved outcomes. Natural language processing, large language models, computer vision, ambient sensing, and wearable technologies enable more continuous, objective, and less labor-intensive assessment compared with traditional screening methods, but evidence remains limited with concerns about false positives and generalizability. AI-supported delirium management through reinforcement learning and digital twins is currently largely conceptual. Responsible AI adoption requires a clearly defined intended use, external validation, action pathways, equitable performance, privacy and security, consent and transparency, clinician oversight, patient preferences, and post-deployment monitoring.AI is most defensible as an adjunct that connects evidence-based delirium care to reliable execution rather than as a replacement for clinical assessment. llm_summary: Researchers reviewed how artificial intelligence could help detect and manage delirium, a serious confusion condition affecting up to one-third of hospitalized older adults. While AI models show promise in identifying patients at risk and detecting delirium more continuously than traditional methods, most have not been put into actual clinical practice, and improved detection alone did not lead to better patient outcomes in one study. The authors conclude that AI works best as a tool to support doctors rather than replace their judgment, and more research is needed to determine whether it actually improves patient care.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers reviewed how artificial intelligence could address care gaps in delirium prediction, detection, and management among hospitalized older adults, who experience delirium at rates up to one-third and face associated adverse outcomes. Prediction models using multimodal health record data including structured variables and unstructured clinical notes demonstrated good discrimination for delirium risk stratification, though few have been integrated into clinical practice, and a live machine learning model that increased targeted delirium detection was associated with longer length of stay in a pre-post comparative study. Natural language processing, large language models, computer vision, ambient sensing, and wearable technologies enable more continuous and objective assessment compared with traditional screening methods, but evidence remains limited with concerns about false positives and generalizability. AI-supported delirium management through reinforcement learning and digital twins is currently largely conceptual, and responsible adoption requires clearly defined intended use, external validation, action pathways, equitable performance, privacy protections, consent and transparency, clinician oversight, and post-deployment monitoring. AI is most defensible as an adjunct connecting evidence-based delirium care to reliable execution rather than as a replacement for clinical assessment, and prospective comparative studies should.

title: Overlooked Writings of Sir William Gowers on Neurology in General Practice, Shorthand, and Education.
abstract: Sir William Richard Gowers (1845-1915), long hailed as the "Father of Clinical Neurology," has been the subject of 2 biographies and many essays relating to his contributions to the study of nervous disorders. Yet, despite extensive bibliographies, several of his publications have hitherto escaped notice. We reviewed archival sources and digital repositories to identify overlooked works. This led to the discovery of his contributions to George Alexander Gibson's 1901 Text-Book of Medicine, which distilled neurology for the general practitioner, as well as lectures and articles on shorthand and education, reflecting his interest in communication, educational practice, and the process of learning. Gowers advocated cultivating ambidexterity in youth, reasoning that it may confer resilience against neurologic injury later in life. Recovered only through primary source research, these writings broaden our understanding of Gowers' intellectual range, showing him not only as a pioneering specialist in the study of nervous disorders but also as a physician engaged with general medicine and educational reform.
