llm_summary: Researchers examined 14 superficial tumors with genetic fusions to determine whether they should be classified as Ewing sarcoma or a rarer neurocristic tumor, since this distinction affects treatment decisions. DNA analysis showed that tumors with classic features and specific protein markers clustered together as neurocristic tumors and had better survival outcomes than Ewing sarcoma. The study recommends diagnosing tumors with ambiguous features as Ewing sarcoma until these exceptionally rare tumors are better understood.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers examined 14 superficial small round cell tumors with FET::ETS fusions or EWSR1 rearrangements and S100 and/or SOX10 expression to clarify the diagnostic distinction between Ewing sarcoma and superficial neurocristic tumors using clinicopathologic, immunohistochemical, and DNA methylation analysis. Tumors were classified as superficial neurocristic tumor (n=2) when displaying superficial location, nests or cords of bland cells, absent necrosis, and diffuse S100/SOX10 co-expression, whereas Ewing sarcoma (n=8) showed nests or sheets of primitive cells with malignant cytology, with four cases designated "Difficult to classify" based on intermediate features. DNA methylation clustering concorded with histologic classification in 9 of 10 confidently classified tumors and consistently classified all SOX10-expressing tumors as superficial neurocristic tumor, while Ewing sarcoma cases demonstrated significantly higher copy number variation with recurrent chromosome 8 gains compared to largely copy number neutral superficial.

title: Clinical Consensus Guidelines on Antibiotic Prescribing Practices for Infants with Gastroschisis Utilizing Modified Delphi Methodology.
abstract: Gastroschisis is the most common congenital abdominal wall defect in newborns and common surgical diagnosis for which antibiotics are prescribed in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU). Multiple studies demonstrate early and prolonged antibiotic exposure, despite evidence of overuse resulting in delayed initiation of feedings, later full feedings, and blood stream infection. The purpose was to develop expert consensus on evidence-driven clinical guidelines for microbiologic screening and antibiotic usage in neonates with simple gastroschisis.The Children's Hospitals Neonatal Consortium (CHNC) Gastroschisis Focus Group utilized a modified Delphi method to develop clinical consensus guidelines (CCG). Committee leaders drafted 10 recommendations after literature review and group discussion. Each recommendation was sent to focus group members via REDCap survey tool and members scored responses on a 5-point Likert scale.In the first survey, there were 23 respondents and 7/10 recommendations received a mean score >80%, meeting the criteria for consensus. Following review of results and comments, the remaining statements were edited and sent out for the second round survey where all achieved consensus. Themes included the practice of screening for infection at birth by blood culture, and antibiotic use practices at the time of birth and abdominal wall closure. These included risk stratification for infection, spectrum of antibiotic therapies utilized, length of therapy, and timing of antibiotic administration.We present a consensus evidence-based framework for antibiotic use and stewardship practices in infants with simple gastroschisis, which will be important as many centers lack standardized guidelines in this population.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. llm_summary: Researchers used expert surveys to develop standardized guidelines for antibiotic use in newborns with gastroschisis, a common birth defect of the abdominal wall. After two rounds of voting, the expert panel reached agreement on recommendations covering when to screen for infection, which antibiotics to use, and how long to treat patients. These new guidelines aim to reduce unnecessary antibiotic exposure and improve outcomes for affected infants.
llm_summary_expert: The Children's Hospitals Neonatal Consortium Gastroschisis Focus Group used a modified Delphi methodology to develop evidence-based clinical consensus guidelines for antibiotic prescribing and microbiologic screening in neonates with simple gastroschisis. In the first survey round, 23 respondents evaluated 10 recommendations on a 5-point Likert scale, with 7 of 10 recommendations achieving consensus defined as a mean score greater than 80%. Following review and revision of the remaining three recommendations, all 10 statements achieved consensus in the second survey round. The final guidelines addressed risk stratification for infection, antibiotic spectrum selection, duration of therapy, and timing of administration at birth and abdominal wall closure. These consensus recommendations provide a standardized framework for antibiotic stewardship in infants with simple gastroschisis, addressing a gap in clinical practice guidelines across many centers.

title: Can Outpatient Total Knee Arthroplasty Be Performed at a Complex, Academic, Quaternary Referral Center?
abstract: Outpatient (same-day discharge) primary total knee arthroplasties (TKAs) have been recently popularized, but results from academic medical centers remain limited. Outpatient surgery shifts perioperative responsibilities to the surgeon. Meanwhile, surgeon reimbursements continue to decrease. We retrospectively evaluated 90-day rates of emergency room (ER) visits, reoperations, revisions, and incoming/outgoing postoperative patient touches associated with outpatient TKAs at our complex, academic, quaternary referral center.At our institution, 1,787 outpatient primary TKAs were performed between 2019 and 2024 in 1,552 unique patients. The mean age was 65 years, 51% were women, the mean body mass index (BMI) was 33, the mean American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) score was 2.4, and the mean Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) was 1.5 (range, 0 to 10). Medical comorbidities, ER visits, reoperations, revisions, and postoperative touches within 90 days after TKA were collected. Univariate logistic regression analyses were completed.The rates of ER visits, reoperations, and revisions within 90 days of surgery were 8.5, 3.1, and 0.7%, respectively. Knees averaged nine postoperative touches, and total touches increased from 61 in 2019 to greater than 5,800 in 2024. The most common first-time ER visit reason was a medical issue unrelated to surgery (35%), followed by evaluation for venous thromboembolism (VTE; 29%). The actual VTE incidence was 0.6%. The most common reoperation was manipulation under anesthesia (MUA; incidence 1.5%). The 90-day periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) incidence was 0.7%, and all cases required reoperation or revision. Older age and increasing ASA score were significantly associated with risk of ER visits (odds ratio [OR] 1.2; P = 0.01 and OR 1.8; P < 0.001, respectively). Increasing CCI was significantly associated with risk of ER visits (OR 1.2; P = 0.001), revisions (OR 1.5; P = 0.001), and PJI (OR 1.3; P = 0.02).We found a high rate of ER visits within 90 days after outpatient TKAs, with nearly 40% unattributable to surgery. Increasing age and comorbidities were associated with increased ER visit risk, and comorbidities also increased revision and PJI risk. Knees averaged nine non-clinic postoperative touches.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether knee replacement surgery could be safely performed as outpatient procedures at a major academic medical center, tracking complications within 90 days for nearly 1,800 surgeries. About 8.5% of patients visited the emergency room after surgery, though more than one-third of these visits were for medical issues unrelated to the surgery itself. Patients with more existing health conditions faced higher risks of emergency visits and complications, suggesting that outpatient knee replacement may work best for healthier individuals.

title: Prevalence and Consequences of Guideline-Directed Indications for Aortic Valve Replacement in the EARLY TAVR Trial.
abstract: The current American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association valvular heart disease guidelines were published before several recent trials that provide greater support for early intervention in patients with asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis (AS).This study sought to investigate the prevalence and clinical impact of American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Class II recommendations for AVR in the EARLY TAVR trial.The EARLY TAVR trial randomized patients with asymptomatic severe AS to transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) with a balloon-expandable valve or clinical surveillance (CS) with conversion to TAVR based on development of ACC/AHA Class I indications. Patients in the intention-to-treat cohort were stratified by presence of a Class II indication for AVR at randomization. The primary endpoint of the present analysis was the composite of all-cause death, stroke, or heart failure hospitalization. Interaction tests were performed to assess whether the treatment effect differed by level of guideline recommendation. Timing of conversion to AVR in the CS group according to the presence/absence of Class II indications was also assessed.Of the 901 patients randomized to TAVR (N = 445) and CS (N = 446), 636 (70.6%) patients had no guideline recommendation, and 265 (29.4%) had at least1 1 Class II recommendation for AVR at the time of randomization. At a median follow-up of 3.8 years, patients with a Class II indication for AVR experienced higher rates of the primary endpoint (Class II: 24.5% vs no recommendation: 14.5%; HR = 1.78; 95% CI: 1.30-2.44; P < 0.001) and were more likely to have acute valve syndrome at the time of conversion. Compared with CS, the relative benefit of early TAVR on the primary endpoint was similar regardless of the presence or absence of a Class II guideline recommendation (HR = 0.62; 95% CI: 0.37-1.02 vs 0.61; 95% CI: 0.40-0.92; Pinteraction = 0.96).Among patients in the EARLY TAVR trial, Class II indications for AVR were present in almost one-third of patients at baseline. The benefit of early TAVR was consistent regardless of the presence or absence of Class II indications. These findings support the strategy of early TAVR over CS in asymptomatic patients with severe AS, independent of guideline indications.https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03042104; Unique Identifier: NCT03042104.Copyright © 2026 The Authors. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether early valve replacement surgery benefited patients with severe aortic stenosis (a narrowing of the heart valve) who had no symptoms, comparing those who received immediate treatment to those who waited for symptoms to develop. Nearly one-third of patients showed warning signs at the start of the study, and these patients had worse outcomes overall, but early treatment reduced serious complications equally well regardless of whether warning signs were present. The findings suggest that offering early valve replacement to asymptomatic patients with severe aortic stenosis may improve their health outcomes.

title: Dual-Energy X-Ray Absorptiometry-Derived Body Composition Asymmetry in Pain-Free Adults: Associations With Age, Lumbar Disc Degeneration, and Physical Activity.
abstract: To characterize body composition asymmetry in asymptomatic adults and examine its associations with age, lumbar intervertebral disc degeneration (DD), and physical activity.Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry scans were performed, and lumbar DD grading, and physical activity levels were assessed in clinically asymptomatic adults in this cross-sectional study.Fifty-one participants were included. Asymmetry in trunk fat and lean tissue mass was present in the overall cohort (P<0.0001), and leg lean tissue mass also differed between sides (P=0.0178), with right-sided predominance in older participants (P=0.0094). Trunk lean AI (TLAI) was higher in older than younger participants (6.3±4.9 vs. 3.5±2.6; P=0.012), whereas the corresponding trunk fat AI (TFAI) difference was not statistically significant (8.0±5.9 vs. 5.0±3.6; P=0.085). Greater age was associated with TLAI (P=0.008), while the trunk fat association was less robust in sensitivity analyses. Signed TFAI and TLAI shifted toward non-dominant-side predominance with greater age (P<0.05). Lumbar DD and physical activity were not significantly associated with asymmetry.Body composition asymmetry was most evident in the trunk. Trunk lean asymmetry was greater at older ages, whereas the corresponding trunk fat association was weaker. Because functional outcomes were not assessed, the clinical significance of these findings requires further investigation.Copyright © 2026 Wolters Kluwer Health, LLC. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether the human body's left and right sides differ in muscle and fat distribution, and whether these differences relate to age, spine degeneration, or exercise habits in pain-free adults. They found that asymmetry was most noticeable in the trunk, with older adults showing greater muscle imbalance between sides compared to younger adults, while spine degeneration and physical activity showed no significant association with asymmetry. The clinical importance of these findings remains unclear because the study did not measure whether asymmetry affects how people function or move.
llm_summary_expert: Researchers examined body composition asymmetry in 51 clinically asymptomatic adults using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry scans, assessing associations with age, lumbar intervertebral disc degeneration, and physical activity levels in this cross-sectional study. Significant asymmetry was detected in trunk fat and lean tissue mass across the cohort (P<0.0001), with trunk lean asymmetry index higher in older participants (6.3±4.9 versus 3.5±2.6; P=0.012) compared to younger participants. Greater age was associated with trunk lean asymmetry index (P=0.008), while the association between age and trunk fat asymmetry was weaker and not statistically significant in sensitivity analyses. Lumbar disc degeneration and physical activity were not significantly associated with body composition asymmetry in this population. The clinical significance of these findings remains unclear because functional outcomes were not assessed in this study.
